source_text: The overcoming of morality through itself -
target_text: The overcoming of morality through itself -

source_text: through truthfulness, the overcoming of the moralist through his opposite -
target_text: through truthfulness, the overcoming of the moralist through his opposite -

source_text: that is what the name Zarathustra means in my mouth.
target_text: that is what the name Zarathustra means in my mouth.

source_text: There he enjoyed his spirit and solitude, and for ten years did not weary of it.
target_text: There he enjoyed his spirit and solitude, and for ten years did not weary of it.

source_text: But at last his heart changed, -
target_text: But at last his heart changed, -

source_text: and rising one morning with the rosy dawn, he went before the sun, and spake thus unto it:
target_text: and rising one morning with the rosy dawn, he went before the sun, and spake thus unto it:

source_text: For ten years hast thou climbed hither unto my cave:
target_text: For ten years hast thou climbed hither unto my cave:

source_text: I am weary of my wisdom, like the bee that hath gathered too much honey;
target_text: I am weary of my wisdom, like the bee that hath gathered too much honey;

source_text: I need hands outstretched to take it.
target_text: I need hands outstretched to take it.

source_text: Therefore must I descend into the deep:
target_text: Therefore must I descend into the deep:

source_text: Like thee must I GO DOWN, as men say, to whom I shall descend.
target_text: Like thee must I GO DOWN, as men say, to whom I shall descend.

source_text: This cup is again going to empty itself, and Zarathustra is again going to be a man.
target_text: This cup is again going to empty itself, and Zarathustra is again going to be a man.

source_text: Zarathustra went down the mountain alone, no one meeting him.
target_text: Zarathustra went down the mountain alone, no one meeting him.

source_text: When he entered the forest, however, there suddenly stood before him an old man, who had left his holy cot to seek roots.
target_text: When he entered the forest, however, there suddenly stood before him an old man, who had left his holy cot to seek roots.

source_text: And thus spake the old man to Zarathustra:
target_text: And thus spake the old man to Zarathustra:

source_text: No stranger to me is this wanderer: many years ago passed he by.
target_text: No stranger to me is this wanderer: many years ago passed he by.

source_text: Zarathustra he was called; but he hath altered.
target_text: Zarathustra he was called; but he hath altered.

source_text: wilt thou now carry thy fire into the valleys?
target_text: wilt thou now carry thy fire into the valleys?

source_text: Pure is his eye, and no loathing lurketh about his mouth.
target_text: Pure is his eye, and no loathing lurketh about his mouth.

source_text: Goeth he not along like a dancer?
target_text: Goeth he not along like a dancer?

source_text: Altered is Zarathustra;
target_text: Altered is Zarathustra;

source_text: a child hath Zarathustra become;
target_text: a child hath Zarathustra become;

source_text: an awakened one is Zarathustra:
target_text: an awakened one is Zarathustra:

source_text: what wilt thou do in the land of the sleepers?
target_text: what wilt thou do in the land of the sleepers?

source_text: As in the sea hast thou lived in solitude, and it hath borne thee up.
target_text: As in the sea hast thou lived in solitude, and it hath borne thee up.

source_text: Alas, wilt thou now go ashore?
target_text: Alas, wilt thou now go ashore?

source_text: Alas, wilt thou again drag thy body thyself?
target_text: Alas, wilt thou again drag thy body thyself?

source_text: Zarathustra answered:
target_text: Zarathustra answered:

source_text: I love mankind.
target_text: I love mankind.

source_text: said the saint,
target_text: said the saint,

source_text: did I go into the forest and the desert?
target_text: did I go into the forest and the desert?

source_text: Was it not because I loved men far too well?
target_text: Was it not because I loved men far too well?

source_text: Now I love God: men, I do not love.
target_text: Now I love God: men, I do not love.

source_text: Man is a thing too imperfect for me.
target_text: Man is a thing too imperfect for me.

source_text: Love to man would be fatal to me.
target_text: Love to man would be fatal to me.

source_text: Zarathustra answered:
target_text: Zarathustra answered:

source_text: I am bringing gifts unto men.
target_text: I am bringing gifts unto men.

source_text: "Give them nothing,"
target_text: "Give them nothing,"

source_text: said the saint.
target_text: said the saint.

source_text: Take rather part of their load, and carry it along with them -
target_text: Take rather part of their load, and carry it along with them -

source_text: that will be most agreeable unto them:
target_text: that will be most agreeable unto them:

source_text: replied Zarathustra,
target_text: replied Zarathustra,

source_text: I give no alms.
target_text: I give no alms.

source_text: I am not poor enough for that.
target_text: I am not poor enough for that.

source_text: The saint laughed at Zarathustra, and spake thus:
target_text: The saint laughed at Zarathustra, and spake thus:

source_text: They are distrustful of anchorites, and do not believe that we come with gifts.
target_text: They are distrustful of anchorites, and do not believe that we come with gifts.

source_text: The fall of our footsteps ringeth too hollow through their streets.
target_text: The fall of our footsteps ringeth too hollow through their streets.

source_text: And just as at night, when they are in bed and hear a man abroad long before sunrise, so they ask themselves concerning us:
target_text: And just as at night, when they are in bed and hear a man abroad long before sunrise, so they ask themselves concerning us:

source_text: Go not to men, but stay in the forest!
target_text: Go not to men, but stay in the forest!

source_text: Go rather to the animals!
target_text: Go rather to the animals!

source_text: Why not be like me - a bear amongst bears, a bird amongst birds?
target_text: Why not be like me - a bear amongst bears, a bird amongst birds?

source_text: "And what doeth the saint in the forest?"
target_text: "And what doeth the saint in the forest?"

source_text: asked Zarathustra.
target_text: asked Zarathustra.

source_text: The saint answered:
target_text: The saint answered:

source_text: I make hymns and sing them;
target_text: I make hymns and sing them;

source_text: With singing, weeping, laughing, and mumbling do I praise the God who is my God.
target_text: With singing, weeping, laughing, and mumbling do I praise the God who is my God.

source_text: But what dost thou bring us as a gift?
target_text: But what dost thou bring us as a gift?

source_text: When Zarathustra had heard these words, he bowed to the saint and said:
target_text: When Zarathustra had heard these words, he bowed to the saint and said:

source_text: What should I have to give thee!
target_text: What should I have to give thee!

source_text: Let me rather hurry hence lest I take aught away from thee!
target_text: Let me rather hurry hence lest I take aught away from thee!

source_text: And thus they parted from one another, the old man and Zarathustra, laughing like schoolboys.
target_text: And thus they parted from one another, the old man and Zarathustra, laughing like schoolboys.

source_text: When Zarathustra was alone, however, he said to his heart:
target_text: When Zarathustra was alone, however, he said to his heart:

source_text: Could it be possible!
target_text: Could it be possible!

source_text: This old saint in the forest hath not yet heard of it, that GOD IS DEAD!
target_text: This old saint in the forest hath not yet heard of it, that GOD IS DEAD!

source_text: When Zarathustra arrived at the nearest town which adjoineth the forest, he found many people assembled in the market-place;
target_text: When Zarathustra arrived at the nearest town which adjoineth the forest, he found many people assembled in the market-place;

source_text: for it had been announced that a rope-dancer would give a performance.
target_text: for it had been announced that a rope-dancer would give a performance.

source_text: And Zarathustra spake thus unto the people:
target_text: And Zarathustra spake thus unto the people:

source_text: I TEACH YOU THE SUPERMAN. Man is something that is to be surpassed.
target_text: I TEACH YOU THE SUPERMAN. Man is something that is to be surpassed.

source_text: What have ye done to surpass man?
target_text: What have ye done to surpass man?

source_text: All beings hitherto have created something beyond themselves:
target_text: All beings hitherto have created something beyond themselves:

source_text: What is the ape to man?
target_text: What is the ape to man?

source_text: A laughing-stock, a thing of shame.
target_text: A laughing-stock, a thing of shame.

source_text: And just the same shall man be to the Superman:
target_text: And just the same shall man be to the Superman:

source_text: a laughing-stock, a thing of shame.
target_text: a laughing-stock, a thing of shame.

source_text: Ye have made your way from the worm to man, and much within you is still worm.
target_text: Ye have made your way from the worm to man, and much within you is still worm.

source_text: Once were ye apes, and even yet man is more of an ape than any of the apes.
target_text: Once were ye apes, and even yet man is more of an ape than any of the apes.

source_text: Even the wisest among you is only a disharmony and hybrid of plant and phantom.
target_text: Even the wisest among you is only a disharmony and hybrid of plant and phantom.

source_text: But do I bid you become phantoms or plants?
target_text: But do I bid you become phantoms or plants?

source_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman!
target_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman!

source_text: The Superman is the meaning of the earth.
target_text: The Superman is the meaning of the earth.

source_text: Let your will say: The Superman SHALL BE the meaning of the earth!
target_text: Let your will say: The Superman SHALL BE the meaning of the earth!

source_text: Poisoners are they, whether they know it or not.
target_text: Poisoners are they, whether they know it or not.

source_text: Despisers of life are they, decaying ones and poisoned ones themselves, of whom the earth is weary:
target_text: Despisers of life are they, decaying ones and poisoned ones themselves, of whom the earth is weary:

source_text: so away with them!
target_text: so away with them!

source_text: Once blasphemy against God was the greatest blasphemy;
target_text: Once blasphemy against God was the greatest blasphemy;

source_text: but God died, and therewith also those blasphemers.
target_text: but God died, and therewith also those blasphemers.

source_text: Once the soul looked contemptuously on the body, and then that contempt was the supreme thing:
target_text: Once the soul looked contemptuously on the body, and then that contempt was the supreme thing:

source_text: Thus it thought to escape from the body and the earth.
target_text: Thus it thought to escape from the body and the earth.

source_text: and cruelty was the delight of that soul!
target_text: and cruelty was the delight of that soul!

source_text: But ye, also, my brethren, tell me:
target_text: But ye, also, my brethren, tell me:

source_text: What doth your body say about your soul?
target_text: What doth your body say about your soul?

source_text: Is your soul not poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency?
target_text: Is your soul not poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency?

source_text: Verily, a polluted stream is man.
target_text: Verily, a polluted stream is man.

source_text: One must be a sea, to receive a polluted stream without becoming impure.
target_text: One must be a sea, to receive a polluted stream without becoming impure.

source_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman: he is that sea;
target_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman: he is that sea;

source_text: in him can your great contempt be submerged.
target_text: in him can your great contempt be submerged.

source_text: What is the greatest thing ye can experience?
target_text: What is the greatest thing ye can experience?

source_text: It is the hour of great contempt.
target_text: It is the hour of great contempt.

source_text: The hour when ye say:
target_text: The hour when ye say:

source_text: What good is my happiness!
target_text: What good is my happiness!

source_text: It is poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency.
target_text: It is poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency.

source_text: But my happiness should justify existence itself!
target_text: But my happiness should justify existence itself!

source_text: The hour when ye say:
target_text: The hour when ye say:

source_text: What good is my reason!
target_text: What good is my reason!

source_text: Doth it long for knowledge as the lion for his food?
target_text: Doth it long for knowledge as the lion for his food?

source_text: It is poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency!
target_text: It is poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency!

source_text: The hour when ye say:
target_text: The hour when ye say:

source_text: What good is my virtue!
target_text: What good is my virtue!

source_text: As yet it hath not made me passionate.
target_text: As yet it hath not made me passionate.

source_text: How weary I am of my good and my bad!
target_text: How weary I am of my good and my bad!

source_text: It is all poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency!
target_text: It is all poverty and pollution and wretched self-complacency!

source_text: The hour when ye say:
target_text: The hour when ye say:

source_text: What good is my justice!
target_text: What good is my justice!

source_text: The hour when ye say:
target_text: The hour when ye say:

source_text: What good is my pity!
target_text: What good is my pity!

source_text: Is not pity the cross on which he is nailed who loveth man?
target_text: Is not pity the cross on which he is nailed who loveth man?

source_text: But my pity is not a crucifixion.
target_text: But my pity is not a crucifixion.

source_text: would that I had heard you crying thus!
target_text: would that I had heard you crying thus!

source_text: It is not your sin -
target_text: It is not your sin -

source_text: Where is the lightning to lick you with its tongue?
target_text: Where is the lightning to lick you with its tongue?

source_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman: he is that lightning, he is that frenzy!
target_text: Lo, I teach you the Superman: he is that lightning, he is that frenzy!

source_text: When Zarathustra had thus spoken, one of the people called out:
target_text: When Zarathustra had thus spoken, one of the people called out:

source_text: We have now heard enough of the rope-dancer;
target_text: We have now heard enough of the rope-dancer;

source_text: it is time now for us to see him!
target_text: it is time now for us to see him!

source_text: And all the people laughed at Zarathustra.
target_text: And all the people laughed at Zarathustra.

source_text: But the rope-dancer, who thought the words applied to him, began his performance.
target_text: But the rope-dancer, who thought the words applied to him, began his performance.

source_text: Zarathustra, however, looked at the people and wondered.
target_text: Zarathustra, however, looked at the people and wondered.

source_text: Then he spake thus:
target_text: Then he spake thus:

source_text: Man is a rope stretched between the animal and the Superman -
target_text: Man is a rope stretched between the animal and the Superman -

source_text: a rope over an abyss.
target_text: a rope over an abyss.

source_text: A dangerous crossing, a dangerous wayfaring, a dangerous looking-back, a dangerous trembling and halting.
target_text: A dangerous crossing, a dangerous wayfaring, a dangerous looking-back, a dangerous trembling and halting.

source_text: What is great in man is that he is a bridge and not a goal:
target_text: What is great in man is that he is a bridge and not a goal:

source_text: I love the great despisers, because they are the great adorers, and arrows of longing for the other shore.
target_text: I love the great despisers, because they are the great adorers, and arrows of longing for the other shore.

source_text: I love those who do not first seek a reason beyond the stars for going down and being sacrifices, but sacrifice themselves to the earth, that the earth of the Superman may hereafter arrive.
target_text: I love those who do not first seek a reason beyond the stars for going down and being sacrifices, but sacrifice themselves to the earth, that the earth of the Superman may hereafter arrive.

source_text: I love him who liveth in order to know, and seeketh to know in order that the Superman may hereafter live.
target_text: I love him who liveth in order to know, and seeketh to know in order that the Superman may hereafter live.

source_text: Thus seeketh he his own down-going.
target_text: Thus seeketh he his own down-going.

source_text: I love him who loveth his virtue:
target_text: I love him who loveth his virtue:

source_text: for virtue is the will to down-going, and an arrow of longing.
target_text: for virtue is the will to down-going, and an arrow of longing.

source_text: I love him who reserveth no share of spirit for himself, but wanteth to be wholly the spirit of his virtue:
target_text: I love him who reserveth no share of spirit for himself, but wanteth to be wholly the spirit of his virtue:

source_text: thus walketh he as spirit over the bridge.
target_text: thus walketh he as spirit over the bridge.

source_text: thus, for the sake of his virtue, he is willing to live on, or live no more.
target_text: thus, for the sake of his virtue, he is willing to live on, or live no more.

source_text: I love him who desireth not too many virtues.
target_text: I love him who desireth not too many virtues.

source_text: One virtue is more of a virtue than two, because it is more of a knot for one's destiny to cling to.
target_text: One virtue is more of a virtue than two, because it is more of a knot for one's destiny to cling to.

source_text: I love him whose soul is lavish, who wanteth no thanks and doth not give back:
target_text: I love him whose soul is lavish, who wanteth no thanks and doth not give back:

source_text: for he always bestoweth, and desireth not to keep for himself.
target_text: for he always bestoweth, and desireth not to keep for himself.

source_text: I love him who is ashamed when the dice fall in his favour, and who then asketh:
target_text: I love him who is ashamed when the dice fall in his favour, and who then asketh:

source_text: for he is willing to succumb.
target_text: for he is willing to succumb.

source_text: I love him who scattereth golden words in advance of his deeds, and always doeth more than he promiseth:
target_text: I love him who scattereth golden words in advance of his deeds, and always doeth more than he promiseth:

source_text: for he is willing to succumb through the present ones.
target_text: for he is willing to succumb through the present ones.

source_text: for he must succumb through the wrath of his God.
target_text: for he must succumb through the wrath of his God.

source_text: I love him whose soul is deep even in the wounding, and may succumb through a small matter:
target_text: I love him whose soul is deep even in the wounding, and may succumb through a small matter:

source_text: thus goeth he willingly over the bridge.
target_text: thus goeth he willingly over the bridge.

source_text: I love him who is of a free spirit and a free heart:
target_text: I love him who is of a free spirit and a free heart:

source_text: thus is his head only the bowels of his heart;
target_text: thus is his head only the bowels of his heart;

source_text: they herald the coming of the lightning, and succumb as heralds.
target_text: they herald the coming of the lightning, and succumb as heralds.

source_text: the lightning, however, is the SUPERMAN. -
target_text: the lightning, however, is the SUPERMAN. -

source_text: When Zarathustra had spoken these words, he again looked at the people, and was silent.
target_text: When Zarathustra had spoken these words, he again looked at the people, and was silent.

source_text: "There they stand,"
target_text: "There they stand,"

source_text: said he to his heart;
target_text: said he to his heart;

source_text: there they laugh: they understand me not;
target_text: there they laugh: they understand me not;

source_text: Must one first batter their ears, that they may learn to hear with their eyes?
target_text: Must one first batter their ears, that they may learn to hear with their eyes?

source_text: They have something whereof they are proud.
target_text: They have something whereof they are proud.

source_text: What do they call it, that which maketh them proud?
target_text: What do they call it, that which maketh them proud?

source_text: Culture, they call it; it distinguisheth them from the goatherds.
target_text: Culture, they call it; it distinguisheth them from the goatherds.

source_text: So I will appeal to their pride.
target_text: So I will appeal to their pride.

source_text: I will speak unto them of the most contemptible thing:
target_text: I will speak unto them of the most contemptible thing:

source_text: that, however, is THE LAST MAN!
target_text: that, however, is THE LAST MAN!

source_text: And thus spake Zarathustra unto the people:
target_text: And thus spake Zarathustra unto the people:

source_text: Still is his soil rich enough for it.
target_text: Still is his soil rich enough for it.

source_text: But that soil will one day be poor and exhausted, and no lofty tree will any longer be able to grow thereon.
target_text: But that soil will one day be poor and exhausted, and no lofty tree will any longer be able to grow thereon.

source_text: there cometh the time when man will no longer launch the arrow of his longing beyond man -
target_text: there cometh the time when man will no longer launch the arrow of his longing beyond man -

source_text: I tell you:
target_text: I tell you:

source_text: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.
target_text: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star.

source_text: I tell you: ye have still chaos in you.
target_text: I tell you: ye have still chaos in you.

source_text: Alas!
target_text: Alas!

source_text: There cometh the time when man will no longer give birth to any star.
target_text: There cometh the time when man will no longer give birth to any star.

source_text: I show you THE LAST MAN.
target_text: I show you THE LAST MAN.

source_text: What is love?
target_text: What is love?

source_text: What is creation?
target_text: What is creation?

source_text: What is longing?
target_text: What is longing?

source_text: What is a star?
target_text: What is a star?

source_text: so asketh the last man and blinketh.
target_text: so asketh the last man and blinketh.

source_text: the last man liveth longest.
target_text: the last man liveth longest.

source_text: "We have discovered happiness"
target_text: "We have discovered happiness"

source_text: say the last men, and blink thereby.
target_text: say the last men, and blink thereby.

source_text: They have left the regions where it is hard to live;
target_text: They have left the regions where it is hard to live;

source_text: for they need warmth.
target_text: for they need warmth.

source_text: One still loveth one's neighbour and rubbeth against him;
target_text: One still loveth one's neighbour and rubbeth against him;

source_text: for one needeth warmth.
target_text: for one needeth warmth.

source_text: Turning ill and being distrustful, they consider sinful:
target_text: Turning ill and being distrustful, they consider sinful:

source_text: they walk warily.
target_text: they walk warily.

source_text: A little poison now and then: that maketh pleasant dreams.
target_text: A little poison now and then: that maketh pleasant dreams.

source_text: And much poison at last for a pleasant death.
target_text: And much poison at last for a pleasant death.

source_text: One still worketh, for work is a pastime.
target_text: One still worketh, for work is a pastime.

source_text: One no longer becometh poor or rich; both are too burdensome.
target_text: One no longer becometh poor or rich; both are too burdensome.

source_text: Who still wanteth to obey?
target_text: Who still wanteth to obey?

source_text: Both are too burdensome.
target_text: Both are too burdensome.

source_text: he who hath other sentiments goeth voluntarily into the madhouse.
target_text: he who hath other sentiments goeth voluntarily into the madhouse.

source_text: "Formerly all the world was insane,"
target_text: "Formerly all the world was insane,"

source_text: say the subtlest of them, and blink thereby.
target_text: say the subtlest of them, and blink thereby.

source_text: They are clever and know all that hath happened:
target_text: They are clever and know all that hath happened:

source_text: so there is no end to their raillery.
target_text: so there is no end to their raillery.

source_text: People still fall out, but are soon reconciled -
target_text: People still fall out, but are soon reconciled -

source_text: otherwise it spoileth their stomachs.
target_text: otherwise it spoileth their stomachs.

source_text: They have their little pleasures for the day, and their little pleasures for the night, but they have a regard for health.
target_text: They have their little pleasures for the day, and their little pleasures for the night, but they have a regard for health.

source_text: "We have discovered happiness,"
target_text: "We have discovered happiness,"

source_text: say the last men, and blink thereby.
target_text: say the last men, and blink thereby.

source_text: And here ended the first discourse of Zarathustra, which is also called
target_text: And here ended the first discourse of Zarathustra, which is also called

source_text: "The Prologue"
target_text: "The Prologue"

source_text: for at this point the shouting and mirth of the multitude interrupted him.
target_text: for at this point the shouting and mirth of the multitude interrupted him.

source_text: "Give us this last man, O Zarathustra,"
target_text: "Give us this last man, O Zarathustra,"

source_text: they called out -
target_text: they called out -

source_text: make us into these last men!
target_text: make us into these last men!

source_text: And all the people exulted and smacked their lips.
target_text: And all the people exulted and smacked their lips.

source_text: Zarathustra, however, turned sad, and said to his heart:
target_text: Zarathustra, however, turned sad, and said to his heart:

source_text: They understand me not: I am not the mouth for these ears.
target_text: They understand me not: I am not the mouth for these ears.

source_text: Too long, perhaps, have I lived in the mountains;
target_text: Too long, perhaps, have I lived in the mountains;

source_text: too much have I hearkened unto the brooks and trees:
target_text: too much have I hearkened unto the brooks and trees:

source_text: Calm is my soul, and clear, like the mountains in the morning.
target_text: Calm is my soul, and clear, like the mountains in the morning.

source_text: But they think me cold, and a mocker with terrible jests.
target_text: But they think me cold, and a mocker with terrible jests.

source_text: And now do they look at me and laugh:
target_text: And now do they look at me and laugh:

source_text: and while they laugh they hate me too.
target_text: and while they laugh they hate me too.

source_text: There is ice in their laughter.
target_text: There is ice in their laughter.

source_text: Then, however, something happened which made every mouth mute and every eye fixed.
target_text: Then, however, something happened which made every mouth mute and every eye fixed.

source_text: In the meantime, of course, the rope-dancer had commenced his performance:
target_text: In the meantime, of course, the rope-dancer had commenced his performance:

source_text: he had come out at a little door, and was going along the rope which was stretched between two towers, so that it hung above the market-place and the people.
target_text: he had come out at a little door, and was going along the rope which was stretched between two towers, so that it hung above the market-place and the people.

source_text: When he was just midway across, the little door opened once more, and a gaudily-dressed fellow like a buffoon sprang out, and went rapidly after the first one.
target_text: When he was just midway across, the little door opened once more, and a gaudily-dressed fellow like a buffoon sprang out, and went rapidly after the first one.

source_text: "Go on, halt-foot,"
target_text: "Go on, halt-foot,"

source_text: cried his frightful voice,
target_text: cried his frightful voice,

source_text: lest I tickle thee with my heel!
target_text: lest I tickle thee with my heel!

source_text: In the tower is the place for thee, thou shouldst be locked up;
target_text: In the tower is the place for thee, thou shouldst be locked up;

source_text: And with every word he came nearer and nearer the first one.
target_text: And with every word he came nearer and nearer the first one.

source_text: When, however, he was but a step behind, there happened the frightful thing which made every mouth mute and every eye fixed -
target_text: When, however, he was but a step behind, there happened the frightful thing which made every mouth mute and every eye fixed -

source_text: he uttered a yell like a devil, and jumped over the other who was in his way.
target_text: he uttered a yell like a devil, and jumped over the other who was in his way.

source_text: The latter, however, when he thus saw his rival triumph, lost at the same time his head and his footing on the rope;
target_text: The latter, however, when he thus saw his rival triumph, lost at the same time his head and his footing on the rope;

source_text: he threw his pole away, and shot downwards faster than it, like an eddy of arms and legs, into the depth.
target_text: he threw his pole away, and shot downwards faster than it, like an eddy of arms and legs, into the depth.

source_text: The market-place and the people were like the sea when the storm cometh on:
target_text: The market-place and the people were like the sea when the storm cometh on:

source_text: Zarathustra, however, remained standing, and just beside him fell the body, badly injured and disfigured, but not yet dead.
target_text: Zarathustra, however, remained standing, and just beside him fell the body, badly injured and disfigured, but not yet dead.

source_text: After a while consciousness returned to the shattered man, and he saw Zarathustra kneeling beside him.
target_text: After a while consciousness returned to the shattered man, and he saw Zarathustra kneeling beside him.

source_text: said he at last,
target_text: said he at last,

source_text: I knew long ago that the devil would trip me up.
target_text: I knew long ago that the devil would trip me up.

source_text: Now he draggeth me to hell: wilt thou prevent him?
target_text: Now he draggeth me to hell: wilt thou prevent him?

source_text: "On mine honour, my friend,"
target_text: "On mine honour, my friend,"

source_text: answered Zarathustra,
target_text: answered Zarathustra,

source_text: there is nothing of all that whereof thou speakest:
target_text: there is nothing of all that whereof thou speakest:

source_text: there is no devil and no hell.
target_text: there is no devil and no hell.

source_text: fear, therefore, nothing any more!
target_text: fear, therefore, nothing any more!

source_text: The man looked up distrustfully.
target_text: The man looked up distrustfully.

source_text: "If thou speakest the truth,"
target_text: "If thou speakest the truth,"

source_text: said he,
target_text: said he,

source_text: I lose nothing when I lose my life.
target_text: I lose nothing when I lose my life.

source_text: I am not much more than an animal which hath been taught to dance by blows and scanty fare.
target_text: I am not much more than an animal which hath been taught to dance by blows and scanty fare.

source_text: said Zarathustra,
target_text: said Zarathustra,

source_text: thou hast made danger thy calling;
target_text: thou hast made danger thy calling;

source_text: therein there is nothing contemptible.
target_text: therein there is nothing contemptible.

source_text: Now thou perishest by thy calling:
target_text: Now thou perishest by thy calling:

source_text: therefore will I bury thee with mine own hands.
target_text: therefore will I bury thee with mine own hands.

source_text: When Zarathustra had said this the dying one did not reply further;
target_text: When Zarathustra had said this the dying one did not reply further;

source_text: but he moved his hand as if he sought the hand of Zarathustra in gratitude.
target_text: but he moved his hand as if he sought the hand of Zarathustra in gratitude.

source_text: Meanwhile the evening came on, and the market-place veiled itself in gloom.
target_text: Meanwhile the evening came on, and the market-place veiled itself in gloom.

source_text: Zarathustra, however, still sat beside the dead man on the ground, absorbed in thought:
target_text: Zarathustra, however, still sat beside the dead man on the ground, absorbed in thought:

source_text: so he forgot the time.
target_text: so he forgot the time.

source_text: But at last it became night, and a cold wind blew upon the lonely one.
target_text: But at last it became night, and a cold wind blew upon the lonely one.

source_text: Then arose Zarathustra and said to his heart:
target_text: Then arose Zarathustra and said to his heart:

source_text: Verily, a fine catch of fish hath Zarathustra made to-day!
target_text: Verily, a fine catch of fish hath Zarathustra made to-day!

source_text: It is not a man he hath caught, but a corpse.
target_text: It is not a man he hath caught, but a corpse.

source_text: I want to teach men the sense of their existence, which is the Superman, the lightning out of the dark cloud -
target_text: I want to teach men the sense of their existence, which is the Superman, the lightning out of the dark cloud -

source_text: But still am I far from them, and my sense speaketh not unto their sense.
target_text: But still am I far from them, and my sense speaketh not unto their sense.

source_text: To men I am still something between a fool and a corpse.
target_text: To men I am still something between a fool and a corpse.

source_text: Come, thou cold and stiff companion!
target_text: Come, thou cold and stiff companion!

source_text: I carry thee to the place where I shall bury thee with mine own hands.
target_text: I carry thee to the place where I shall bury thee with mine own hands.

source_text: When Zarathustra had said this to his heart, he put the corpse upon his shoulders and set out on his way.
target_text: When Zarathustra had said this to his heart, he put the corpse upon his shoulders and set out on his way.

source_text: and lo!
target_text: and lo!

source_text: he that spake was the buffoon from the tower.
target_text: he that spake was the buffoon from the tower.

source_text: "Leave this town, O Zarathustra,"
target_text: "Leave this town, O Zarathustra,"

source_text: said he,
target_text: said he,

source_text: there are too many here who hate thee.
target_text: there are too many here who hate thee.

source_text: the believers in the orthodox belief hate thee, and call thee a danger to the multitude.
target_text: the believers in the orthodox belief hate thee, and call thee a danger to the multitude.

source_text: It was thy good fortune to be laughed at:
target_text: It was thy good fortune to be laughed at:

source_text: It was thy good fortune to associate with the dead dog;
target_text: It was thy good fortune to associate with the dead dog;

source_text: by so humiliating thyself thou hast saved thy life to-day.
target_text: by so humiliating thyself thou hast saved thy life to-day.

source_text: Depart, however, from this town, -
target_text: Depart, however, from this town, -

source_text: And when he had said this, the buffoon vanished;
target_text: And when he had said this, the buffoon vanished;

source_text: Zarathustra, however, went on through the dark streets.
target_text: Zarathustra, however, went on through the dark streets.

source_text: At the gate of the town the grave-diggers met him:
target_text: At the gate of the town the grave-diggers met him:

source_text: a fine thing that Zarathustra hath turned a grave-digger!
target_text: a fine thing that Zarathustra hath turned a grave-digger!

source_text: For our hands are too cleanly for that roast.
target_text: For our hands are too cleanly for that roast.

source_text: Well then, good luck to the repast!
target_text: Well then, good luck to the repast!

source_text: If only the devil is not a better thief than Zarathustra!
target_text: If only the devil is not a better thief than Zarathustra!

source_text: he will steal them both, he will eat them both!
target_text: he will steal them both, he will eat them both!

source_text: And they laughed among themselves, and put their heads together.
target_text: And they laughed among themselves, and put their heads together.

source_text: When he had gone on for two hours, past forests and swamps, he had heard too much of the hungry howling of the wolves, and he himself became a-hungry.
target_text: When he had gone on for two hours, past forests and swamps, he had heard too much of the hungry howling of the wolves, and he himself became a-hungry.

source_text: So he halted at a lonely house in which a light was burning.
target_text: So he halted at a lonely house in which a light was burning.

source_text: "Hunger attacketh me,"
target_text: "Hunger attacketh me,"

source_text: said Zarathustra,
target_text: said Zarathustra,

source_text: like a robber.
target_text: like a robber.

source_text: Among forests and swamps my hunger attacketh me, and late in the night.
target_text: Among forests and swamps my hunger attacketh me, and late in the night.

source_text: Strange humours hath my hunger.
target_text: Strange humours hath my hunger.

source_text: Often it cometh to me only after a repast, and all day it hath failed to come:
target_text: Often it cometh to me only after a repast, and all day it hath failed to come:

source_text: where hath it been?
target_text: where hath it been?

source_text: And thereupon Zarathustra knocked at the door of the house.
target_text: And thereupon Zarathustra knocked at the door of the house.

source_text: An old man appeared, who carried a light, and asked:
target_text: An old man appeared, who carried a light, and asked:

source_text: "Who cometh unto me and my bad sleep?"
target_text: "Who cometh unto me and my bad sleep?"

source_text: "A living man and a dead one,"
target_text: "A living man and a dead one,"

source_text: said Zarathustra.
target_text: said Zarathustra.

source_text: Give me something to eat and drink, I forgot it during the day.
target_text: Give me something to eat and drink, I forgot it during the day.

source_text: He that feedeth the hungry refresheth his own soul, saith wisdom.
target_text: He that feedeth the hungry refresheth his own soul, saith wisdom.

source_text: The old man withdrew, but came back immediately and offered Zarathustra bread and wine.
target_text: The old man withdrew, but came back immediately and offered Zarathustra bread and wine.

source_text: said he;
target_text: said he;

source_text: that is why I live here.
target_text: that is why I live here.

source_text: Animal and man come unto me, the anchorite.
target_text: Animal and man come unto me, the anchorite.

source_text: But bid thy companion eat and drink also, he is wearier than thou.
target_text: But bid thy companion eat and drink also, he is wearier than thou.

source_text: Zarathustra answered:
target_text: Zarathustra answered:

source_text: My companion is dead; I shall hardly be able to persuade him to eat.
target_text: My companion is dead; I shall hardly be able to persuade him to eat.

source_text: "That doth not concern me,"
target_text: "That doth not concern me,"

source_text: said the old man sullenly;
target_text: said the old man sullenly;

source_text: he that knocketh at my door must take what I offer him.
target_text: he that knocketh at my door must take what I offer him.

source_text: Eat, and fare ye well!
target_text: Eat, and fare ye well!

source_text: Thereafter Zarathustra again went on for two hours, trusting to the path and the light of the stars:
target_text: Thereafter Zarathustra again went on for two hours, trusting to the path and the light of the stars:

source_text: for he was an experienced night-walker, and liked to look into the face of all that slept.
target_text: for he was an experienced night-walker, and liked to look into the face of all that slept.

source_text: When the morning dawned, however, Zarathustra found himself in a thick forest, and no path was any longer visible.
target_text: When the morning dawned, however, Zarathustra found himself in a thick forest, and no path was any longer visible.

source_text: He then put the dead man in a hollow tree at his head -
target_text: He then put the dead man in a hollow tree at his head -

source_text: for he wanted to protect him from the wolves -
target_text: for he wanted to protect him from the wolves -

source_text: and laid himself down on the ground and moss.
target_text: and laid himself down on the ground and moss.

source_text: And immediately he fell asleep, tired in body, but with a tranquil soul.
target_text: And immediately he fell asleep, tired in body, but with a tranquil soul.

source_text: Long slept Zarathustra;
target_text: Long slept Zarathustra;

source_text: and not only the rosy dawn passed over his head, but also the morning.
target_text: and not only the rosy dawn passed over his head, but also the morning.

source_text: At last, however, his eyes opened, and amazedly he gazed into the forest and the stillness, amazedly he gazed into himself.
target_text: At last, however, his eyes opened, and amazedly he gazed into the forest and the stillness, amazedly he gazed into himself.

source_text: Then he arose quickly, like a seafarer who all at once seeth the land;
target_text: Then he arose quickly, like a seafarer who all at once seeth the land;

source_text: and he shouted for joy: for he saw a new truth.
target_text: and he shouted for joy: for he saw a new truth.

source_text: And he spake thus to his heart:
target_text: And he spake thus to his heart:

source_text: A light hath dawned upon me:
target_text: A light hath dawned upon me:

source_text: I need companions -
target_text: I need companions -

source_text: not dead companions and corpses, which I carry with me where I will.
target_text: not dead companions and corpses, which I carry with me where I will.

source_text: But I need living companions, who will follow me because they want to follow themselves -
target_text: But I need living companions, who will follow me because they want to follow themselves -

source_text: and to the place where I will.
target_text: and to the place where I will.

source_text: A light hath dawned upon me.
target_text: A light hath dawned upon me.

source_text: Not to the people is Zarathustra to speak, but to companions!
target_text: Not to the people is Zarathustra to speak, but to companions!

source_text: To allure many from the herd - for that purpose have I come.
target_text: To allure many from the herd - for that purpose have I come.

source_text: The people and the herd must be angry with me:
target_text: The people and the herd must be angry with me:

source_text: Herdsmen, I say, but they call themselves the good and just.
target_text: Herdsmen, I say, but they call themselves the good and just.

source_text: Herdsmen, I say, but they call themselves the believers in the orthodox belief.
target_text: Herdsmen, I say, but they call themselves the believers in the orthodox belief.

source_text: Behold the good and just!
target_text: Behold the good and just!

source_text: Whom do they hate most?
target_text: Whom do they hate most?

source_text: he, however, is the creator.
target_text: he, however, is the creator.

source_text: Behold the believers of all beliefs!
target_text: Behold the believers of all beliefs!

source_text: Whom do they hate most?
target_text: Whom do they hate most?

source_text: he, however, is the creator.
target_text: he, however, is the creator.

source_text: Companions, the creator seeketh, not corpses -
target_text: Companions, the creator seeketh, not corpses -

source_text: and not herds or believers either.
target_text: and not herds or believers either.

source_text: Fellow-creators the creator seeketh -
target_text: Fellow-creators the creator seeketh -

source_text: those who grave new values on new tables.
target_text: those who grave new values on new tables.

source_text: for everything is ripe for the harvest with him.
target_text: for everything is ripe for the harvest with him.

source_text: But he lacketh the hundred sickles:
target_text: But he lacketh the hundred sickles:

source_text: so he plucketh the ears of corn and is vexed.
target_text: so he plucketh the ears of corn and is vexed.

source_text: Destroyers, will they be called, and despisers of good and evil.
target_text: Destroyers, will they be called, and despisers of good and evil.

source_text: But they are the reapers and rejoicers.
target_text: But they are the reapers and rejoicers.

source_text: what hath he to do with herds and herdsmen and corpses!
target_text: what hath he to do with herds and herdsmen and corpses!

source_text: And thou, my first companion, rest in peace!
target_text: And thou, my first companion, rest in peace!

source_text: Well have I buried thee in thy hollow tree;
target_text: Well have I buried thee in thy hollow tree;

source_text: well have I hid thee from the wolves.
target_text: well have I hid thee from the wolves.

source_text: But I part from thee; the time hath arrived.
target_text: But I part from thee; the time hath arrived.

source_text: I am not to be a herdsman, I am not to be a grave-digger.
target_text: I am not to be a herdsman, I am not to be a grave-digger.

source_text: Not any more will I discourse unto the people;
target_text: Not any more will I discourse unto the people;

source_text: With the creators, the reapers, and the rejoicers will I associate:
target_text: With the creators, the reapers, and the rejoicers will I associate:

source_text: the rainbow will I show them, and all the stairs to the Superman.
target_text: the rainbow will I show them, and all the stairs to the Superman.

source_text: To the lone-dwellers will I sing my song, and to the twain-dwellers;
target_text: To the lone-dwellers will I sing my song, and to the twain-dwellers;

source_text: I make for my goal, I follow my course;
target_text: I make for my goal, I follow my course;

source_text: Then he looked inquiringly aloft, -
target_text: Then he looked inquiringly aloft, -

source_text: for he heard above him the sharp call of a bird.
target_text: for he heard above him the sharp call of a bird.

source_text: And behold!
target_text: And behold!

source_text: An eagle swept through the air in wide circles, and on it hung a serpent, not like a prey, but like a friend:
target_text: An eagle swept through the air in wide circles, and on it hung a serpent, not like a prey, but like a friend:

source_text: for it kept itself coiled round the eagle's neck.
target_text: for it kept itself coiled round the eagle's neck.

source_text: "They are mine animals,"
target_text: "They are mine animals,"

source_text: said Zarathustra, and rejoiced in his heart.
target_text: said Zarathustra, and rejoiced in his heart.

source_text: The proudest animal under the sun, and the wisest animal under the sun, -
target_text: The proudest animal under the sun, and the wisest animal under the sun, -

source_text: they have come out to reconnoitre.
target_text: they have come out to reconnoitre.

source_text: They want to know whether Zarathustra still liveth.
target_text: They want to know whether Zarathustra still liveth.

source_text: Verily, do I still live?
target_text: Verily, do I still live?

source_text: More dangerous have I found it among men than among animals;
target_text: More dangerous have I found it among men than among animals;

source_text: When Zarathustra had said this, he remembered the words of the saint in the forest.
target_text: When Zarathustra had said this, he remembered the words of the saint in the forest.

source_text: Then he sighed and spake thus to his heart: Would that I were wiser!
target_text: Then he sighed and spake thus to his heart: Would that I were wiser!

source_text: Would that I were wise from the very heart, like my serpent!
target_text: Would that I were wise from the very heart, like my serpent!

source_text: But I am asking the impossible.
target_text: But I am asking the impossible.

source_text: Therefore do I ask my pride to go always with my wisdom!
target_text: Therefore do I ask my pride to go always with my wisdom!

source_text: And if my wisdom should some day forsake me: - alas!
target_text: And if my wisdom should some day forsake me: - alas!

source_text: it loveth to fly away!
target_text: it loveth to fly away!

source_text: may my pride then fly with my folly!
target_text: may my pride then fly with my folly!

source_text: Thus began Zarathustra's down-going.
target_text: Thus began Zarathustra's down-going.

source_text: Three metamorphoses of the spirit do I designate to you:
target_text: Three metamorphoses of the spirit do I designate to you:

source_text: how the spirit becometh a camel, the camel a lion, and the lion at last a child.
target_text: how the spirit becometh a camel, the camel a lion, and the lion at last a child.

source_text: Many heavy things are there for the spirit, the strong load-bearing spirit in which reverence dwelleth:
target_text: Many heavy things are there for the spirit, the strong load-bearing spirit in which reverence dwelleth:

source_text: for the heavy and the heaviest longeth its strength.
target_text: for the heavy and the heaviest longeth its strength.

source_text: What is heavy?
target_text: What is heavy?

source_text: so asketh the load-bearing spirit;
target_text: so asketh the load-bearing spirit;

source_text: then kneeleth it down like the camel, and wanteth to be well laden.
target_text: then kneeleth it down like the camel, and wanteth to be well laden.

source_text: What is the heaviest thing, ye heroes?
target_text: What is the heaviest thing, ye heroes?

source_text: To exhibit one's folly in order to mock at one's wisdom?
target_text: To exhibit one's folly in order to mock at one's wisdom?

source_text: Or is it this: To desert our cause when it celebrateth its triumph?
target_text: Or is it this: To desert our cause when it celebrateth its triumph?

source_text: To ascend high mountains to tempt the tempter?
target_text: To ascend high mountains to tempt the tempter?

source_text: Or is it this:
target_text: Or is it this:

source_text: To feed on the acorns and grass of knowledge, and for the sake of truth to suffer hunger of soul?
target_text: To feed on the acorns and grass of knowledge, and for the sake of truth to suffer hunger of soul?

source_text: Or is it this:
target_text: Or is it this:

source_text: To be sick and dismiss comforters, and make friends of the deaf, who never hear thy requests?
target_text: To be sick and dismiss comforters, and make friends of the deaf, who never hear thy requests?

source_text: Or is it this:
target_text: Or is it this:

source_text: To go into foul water when it is the water of truth, and not disclaim cold frogs and hot toads?
target_text: To go into foul water when it is the water of truth, and not disclaim cold frogs and hot toads?

source_text: Or is it this:
target_text: Or is it this:

source_text: To love those who despise us, and give one's hand to the phantom when it is going to frighten us?
target_text: To love those who despise us, and give one's hand to the phantom when it is going to frighten us?

source_text: All these heaviest things the load-bearing spirit taketh upon itself:
target_text: All these heaviest things the load-bearing spirit taketh upon itself:

source_text: and like the camel, which, when laden, hasteneth into the wilderness, so hasteneth the spirit into its wilderness.
target_text: and like the camel, which, when laden, hasteneth into the wilderness, so hasteneth the spirit into its wilderness.

source_text: But in the loneliest wilderness happeneth the second metamorphosis:
target_text: But in the loneliest wilderness happeneth the second metamorphosis:

source_text: here the spirit becometh a lion;
target_text: here the spirit becometh a lion;

source_text: for victory will it struggle with the great dragon.
target_text: for victory will it struggle with the great dragon.

source_text: is the great dragon called.
target_text: is the great dragon called.

source_text: But the spirit of the lion saith,
target_text: But the spirit of the lion saith,

source_text: lieth in its path, sparkling with gold - a scale-covered beast;
target_text: lieth in its path, sparkling with gold - a scale-covered beast;

source_text: and on every scale glittereth golden,
target_text: and on every scale glittereth golden,

source_text: The values of a thousand years glitter on those scales, and thus speaketh the mightiest of all dragons:
target_text: The values of a thousand years glitter on those scales, and thus speaketh the mightiest of all dragons:

source_text: All values have already been created, and all created values -
target_text: All values have already been created, and all created values -

source_text: do I represent.
target_text: do I represent.

source_text: Thus speaketh the dragon.
target_text: Thus speaketh the dragon.

source_text: My brethren, wherefore is there need of the lion in the spirit?
target_text: My brethren, wherefore is there need of the lion in the spirit?

source_text: Why sufficeth not the beast of burden, which renounceth and is reverent?
target_text: Why sufficeth not the beast of burden, which renounceth and is reverent?

source_text: To create new values -
target_text: To create new values -

source_text: that, even the lion cannot yet accomplish:
target_text: that, even the lion cannot yet accomplish:

source_text: but to create itself freedom for new creating -
target_text: but to create itself freedom for new creating -

source_text: that can the might of the lion do.
target_text: that can the might of the lion do.

source_text: To create itself freedom, and give a holy Nay even unto duty:
target_text: To create itself freedom, and give a holy Nay even unto duty:

source_text: for that, my brethren, there is need of the lion.
target_text: for that, my brethren, there is need of the lion.

source_text: To assume the right to new values -
target_text: To assume the right to new values -

source_text: that is the most formidable assumption for a load-bearing and reverent spirit.
target_text: that is the most formidable assumption for a load-bearing and reverent spirit.

source_text: the lion is needed for this capture.
target_text: the lion is needed for this capture.

source_text: But tell me, my brethren, what the child can do, which even the lion could not do?
target_text: But tell me, my brethren, what the child can do, which even the lion could not do?

source_text: Innocence is the child, and forgetfulness, a new beginning, a game, a self-rolling wheel, a first movement, a holy Yea.
target_text: Innocence is the child, and forgetfulness, a new beginning, a game, a self-rolling wheel, a first movement, a holy Yea.

source_text: Aye, for the game of creating, my brethren, there is needed a holy Yea unto life:
target_text: Aye, for the game of creating, my brethren, there is needed a holy Yea unto life:

source_text: ITS OWN will, willeth now the spirit;
target_text: ITS OWN will, willeth now the spirit;

source_text: Three metamorphoses of the spirit have I designated to you:
target_text: Three metamorphoses of the spirit have I designated to you:

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: And at that time he abode in the town which is called The Pied Cow.
target_text: And at that time he abode in the town which is called The Pied Cow.

source_text: People commended unto Zarathustra a wise man, as one who could discourse well about sleep and virtue:
target_text: People commended unto Zarathustra a wise man, as one who could discourse well about sleep and virtue:

source_text: To him went Zarathustra, and sat among the youths before his chair.
target_text: To him went Zarathustra, and sat among the youths before his chair.

source_text: And thus spake the wise man: Respect and modesty in presence of sleep!
target_text: And thus spake the wise man: Respect and modesty in presence of sleep!

source_text: That is the first thing!
target_text: That is the first thing!

source_text: And to go out of the way of all who sleep badly and keep awake at night!
target_text: And to go out of the way of all who sleep badly and keep awake at night!

source_text: Modest is even the thief in presence of sleep:
target_text: Modest is even the thief in presence of sleep:

source_text: he always stealeth softly through the night.
target_text: he always stealeth softly through the night.

source_text: Immodest, however, is the night-watchman;
target_text: Immodest, however, is the night-watchman;

source_text: immodestly he carrieth his horn.
target_text: immodestly he carrieth his horn.

source_text: No small art is it to sleep:
target_text: No small art is it to sleep:

source_text: it is necessary for that purpose to keep awake all day.
target_text: it is necessary for that purpose to keep awake all day.

source_text: Ten times a day must thou overcome thyself:
target_text: Ten times a day must thou overcome thyself:

source_text: Ten times must thou reconcile again with thyself;
target_text: Ten times must thou reconcile again with thyself;

source_text: for overcoming is bitterness, and badly sleep the unreconciled.
target_text: for overcoming is bitterness, and badly sleep the unreconciled.

source_text: Ten truths must thou find during the day;
target_text: Ten truths must thou find during the day;

source_text: otherwise wilt thou seek truth during the night, and thy soul will have been hungry.
target_text: otherwise wilt thou seek truth during the night, and thy soul will have been hungry.

source_text: Ten times must thou laugh during the day, and be cheerful;
target_text: Ten times must thou laugh during the day, and be cheerful;

source_text: otherwise thy stomach, the father of affliction, will disturb thee in the night.
target_text: otherwise thy stomach, the father of affliction, will disturb thee in the night.

source_text: Few people know it, but one must have all the virtues in order to sleep well.
target_text: Few people know it, but one must have all the virtues in order to sleep well.

source_text: Shall I commit adultery?
target_text: Shall I commit adultery?

source_text: Shall I covet my neighbour's maidservant?
target_text: Shall I covet my neighbour's maidservant?

source_text: All that would ill accord with good sleep.
target_text: All that would ill accord with good sleep.

source_text: And even if one have all the virtues, there is still one thing needful:
target_text: And even if one have all the virtues, there is still one thing needful:

source_text: to send the virtues themselves to sleep at the right time.
target_text: to send the virtues themselves to sleep at the right time.

source_text: That they may not quarrel with one another, the good females!
target_text: That they may not quarrel with one another, the good females!

source_text: And about thee, thou unhappy one!
target_text: And about thee, thou unhappy one!

source_text: Peace with God and thy neighbour: so desireth good sleep.
target_text: Peace with God and thy neighbour: so desireth good sleep.

source_text: And peace also with thy neighbour's devil!
target_text: And peace also with thy neighbour's devil!

source_text: Honour to the government, and obedience, and also to the crooked government!
target_text: Honour to the government, and obedience, and also to the crooked government!

source_text: How can I help it, if power like to walk on crooked legs?
target_text: How can I help it, if power like to walk on crooked legs?

source_text: He who leadeth his sheep to the greenest pasture, shall always be for me the best shepherd:
target_text: He who leadeth his sheep to the greenest pasture, shall always be for me the best shepherd:

source_text: so doth it accord with good sleep.
target_text: so doth it accord with good sleep.

source_text: Many honours I want not, nor great treasures: they excite the spleen.
target_text: Many honours I want not, nor great treasures: they excite the spleen.

source_text: But it is bad sleeping without a good name and a little treasure.
target_text: But it is bad sleeping without a good name and a little treasure.

source_text: A small company is more welcome to me than a bad one:
target_text: A small company is more welcome to me than a bad one:

source_text: So doth it accord with good sleep.
target_text: So doth it accord with good sleep.

source_text: Well, also, do the poor in spirit please me: they promote sleep.
target_text: Well, also, do the poor in spirit please me: they promote sleep.

source_text: Thus passeth the day unto the virtuous.
target_text: Thus passeth the day unto the virtuous.

source_text: When night cometh, then take I good care not to summon sleep.
target_text: When night cometh, then take I good care not to summon sleep.

source_text: It disliketh to be summoned - sleep, the lord of the virtues!
target_text: It disliketh to be summoned - sleep, the lord of the virtues!

source_text: But I think of what I have done and thought during the day.
target_text: But I think of what I have done and thought during the day.

source_text: Thus ruminating, patient as a cow, I ask myself:
target_text: Thus ruminating, patient as a cow, I ask myself:

source_text: What were thy ten overcomings?
target_text: What were thy ten overcomings?

source_text: And what were the ten reconciliations, and the ten truths, and the ten laughters with which my heart enjoyed itself?
target_text: And what were the ten reconciliations, and the ten truths, and the ten laughters with which my heart enjoyed itself?

source_text: sleep, the unsummoned, the lord of the virtues.
target_text: sleep, the unsummoned, the lord of the virtues.

source_text: Sleep tappeth on mine eye, and it turneth heavy.
target_text: Sleep tappeth on mine eye, and it turneth heavy.

source_text: Sleep toucheth my mouth, and it remaineth open.
target_text: Sleep toucheth my mouth, and it remaineth open.

source_text: stupid do I then stand, like this academic chair.
target_text: stupid do I then stand, like this academic chair.

source_text: But not much longer do I then stand: I already lie.
target_text: But not much longer do I then stand: I already lie.

source_text: When Zarathustra heard the wise man thus speak, he laughed in his heart:
target_text: When Zarathustra heard the wise man thus speak, he laughed in his heart:

source_text: for thereby had a light dawned upon him.
target_text: for thereby had a light dawned upon him.

source_text: And thus spake he to his heart:
target_text: And thus spake he to his heart:

source_text: A fool seemeth this wise man with his forty thoughts:
target_text: A fool seemeth this wise man with his forty thoughts:

source_text: but I believe he knoweth well how to sleep.
target_text: but I believe he knoweth well how to sleep.

source_text: Happy even is he who liveth near this wise man!
target_text: Happy even is he who liveth near this wise man!

source_text: Such sleep is contagious - even through a thick wall it is contagious.
target_text: Such sleep is contagious - even through a thick wall it is contagious.

source_text: A magic resideth even in his academic chair.
target_text: A magic resideth even in his academic chair.

source_text: His wisdom is to keep awake in order to sleep well.
target_text: His wisdom is to keep awake in order to sleep well.

source_text: And verily, if life had no sense, and had I to choose nonsense, this would be the desirablest nonsense for me also.
target_text: And verily, if life had no sense, and had I to choose nonsense, this would be the desirablest nonsense for me also.

source_text: Now know I well what people sought formerly above all else when they sought teachers of virtue.
target_text: Now know I well what people sought formerly above all else when they sought teachers of virtue.

source_text: they knew no higher significance of life.
target_text: they knew no higher significance of life.

source_text: And not much longer do they stand: there they already lie.
target_text: And not much longer do they stand: there they already lie.

source_text: Blessed are those drowsy ones: for they shall soon nod to sleep.
target_text: Blessed are those drowsy ones: for they shall soon nod to sleep.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: The work of a suffering and tortured God, did the world then seem to me.
target_text: The work of a suffering and tortured God, did the world then seem to me.

source_text: The dream - and diction - of a God, did the world then seem to me;
target_text: The dream - and diction - of a God, did the world then seem to me;

source_text: Good and evil, and joy and woe, and I and thou -
target_text: Good and evil, and joy and woe, and I and thou -

source_text: The creator wished to look away from himself, -
target_text: The creator wished to look away from himself, -

source_text: thereupon he created the world.
target_text: thereupon he created the world.

source_text: Intoxicating joy is it for the sufferer to look away from his suffering and forget himself.
target_text: Intoxicating joy is it for the sufferer to look away from his suffering and forget himself.

source_text: Intoxicating joy and self-forgetting, did the world once seem to me.
target_text: Intoxicating joy and self-forgetting, did the world once seem to me.

source_text: This world, the eternally imperfect, an eternal contradiction's image and imperfect image -
target_text: This world, the eternally imperfect, an eternal contradiction's image and imperfect image -

source_text: thus did the world once seem to me.
target_text: thus did the world once seem to me.

source_text: Thus, once on a time, did I also cast my fancy beyond man, like all backworldsmen.
target_text: Thus, once on a time, did I also cast my fancy beyond man, like all backworldsmen.

source_text: Beyond man, forsooth?
target_text: Beyond man, forsooth?

source_text: A man was he, and only a poor fragment of a man and ego.
target_text: A man was he, and only a poor fragment of a man and ego.

source_text: Out of mine own ashes and glow it came unto me, that phantom.
target_text: Out of mine own ashes and glow it came unto me, that phantom.

source_text: And verily, it came not unto me from the beyond!
target_text: And verily, it came not unto me from the beyond!

source_text: What happened, my brethren?
target_text: What happened, my brethren?

source_text: I surpassed myself, the suffering one;
target_text: I surpassed myself, the suffering one;

source_text: a brighter flame I contrived for myself.
target_text: a brighter flame I contrived for myself.

source_text: Thereupon the phantom WITHDREW from me!
target_text: Thereupon the phantom WITHDREW from me!

source_text: To me the convalescent would it now be suffering and torment to believe in such phantoms:
target_text: To me the convalescent would it now be suffering and torment to believe in such phantoms:

source_text: suffering would it now be to me, and humiliation.
target_text: suffering would it now be to me, and humiliation.

source_text: and the short madness of happiness, which only the greatest sufferer experienceth.
target_text: and the short madness of happiness, which only the greatest sufferer experienceth.

source_text: Weariness, which seeketh to get to the ultimate with one leap, with a death-leap;
target_text: Weariness, which seeketh to get to the ultimate with one leap, with a death-leap;

source_text: that created all Gods and backworlds.
target_text: that created all Gods and backworlds.

source_text: Believe me, my brethren!
target_text: Believe me, my brethren!

source_text: It was the body which despaired of the body -
target_text: It was the body which despaired of the body -

source_text: it groped with the fingers of the infatuated spirit at the ultimate walls.
target_text: it groped with the fingers of the infatuated spirit at the ultimate walls.

source_text: Believe me, my brethren!
target_text: Believe me, my brethren!

source_text: It was the body which despaired of the earth -
target_text: It was the body which despaired of the earth -

source_text: it heard the bowels of existence speaking unto it.
target_text: it heard the bowels of existence speaking unto it.

source_text: And then it sought to get through the ultimate walls with its head -
target_text: And then it sought to get through the ultimate walls with its head -

source_text: and not with its head only -
target_text: and not with its head only -

source_text: the other world.
target_text: the other world.

source_text: But that
target_text: But that

source_text: "other world"
target_text: "other world"

source_text: and the bowels of existence do not speak unto man, except as man.
target_text: and the bowels of existence do not speak unto man, except as man.

source_text: Verily, it is difficult to prove all being, and hard to make it speak.
target_text: Verily, it is difficult to prove all being, and hard to make it speak.

source_text: Tell me, ye brethren, is not the strangest of all things best proved?
target_text: Tell me, ye brethren, is not the strangest of all things best proved?

source_text: Yea, this ego, with its contradiction and perplexity, speaketh most uprightly of its being -
target_text: Yea, this ego, with its contradiction and perplexity, speaketh most uprightly of its being -

source_text: And this most upright existence, the ego -
target_text: And this most upright existence, the ego -

source_text: it speaketh of the body, and still implieth the body, even when it museth and raveth and fluttereth with broken wings.
target_text: it speaketh of the body, and still implieth the body, even when it museth and raveth and fluttereth with broken wings.

source_text: Always more uprightly learneth it to speak, the ego;
target_text: Always more uprightly learneth it to speak, the ego;

source_text: and the more it learneth, the more doth it find titles and honours for the body and the earth.
target_text: and the more it learneth, the more doth it find titles and honours for the body and the earth.

source_text: no longer to thrust one's head into the sand of celestial things, but to carry it freely, a terrestrial head, which giveth meaning to the earth!
target_text: no longer to thrust one's head into the sand of celestial things, but to carry it freely, a terrestrial head, which giveth meaning to the earth!

source_text: A new will teach I unto men:
target_text: A new will teach I unto men:

source_text: to choose that path which man hath followed blindly, and to approve of it -
target_text: to choose that path which man hath followed blindly, and to approve of it -

source_text: and no longer to slink aside from it, like the sick and perishing!
target_text: and no longer to slink aside from it, like the sick and perishing!

source_text: The sick and perishing -
target_text: The sick and perishing -

source_text: it was they who despised the body and the earth, and invented the heavenly world, and the redeeming blood-drops;
target_text: it was they who despised the body and the earth, and invented the heavenly world, and the redeeming blood-drops;

source_text: but even those sweet and sad poisons they borrowed from the body and the earth!
target_text: but even those sweet and sad poisons they borrowed from the body and the earth!

source_text: From their misery they sought escape, and the stars were too remote for them.
target_text: From their misery they sought escape, and the stars were too remote for them.

source_text: Then they sighed:
target_text: Then they sighed:

source_text: Then they contrived for themselves their by-paths and bloody draughts!
target_text: Then they contrived for themselves their by-paths and bloody draughts!

source_text: Beyond the sphere of their body and this earth they now fancied themselves transported, these ungrateful ones.
target_text: Beyond the sphere of their body and this earth they now fancied themselves transported, these ungrateful ones.

source_text: But to what did they owe the convulsion and rapture of their transport?
target_text: But to what did they owe the convulsion and rapture of their transport?

source_text: To their body and this earth.
target_text: To their body and this earth.

source_text: Verily, he is not indignant at their modes of consolation and ingratitude.
target_text: Verily, he is not indignant at their modes of consolation and ingratitude.

source_text: but sickness and a sick frame remain even in his tears.
target_text: but sickness and a sick frame remain even in his tears.

source_text: Many sickly ones have there always been among those who muse, and languish for God;
target_text: Many sickly ones have there always been among those who muse, and languish for God;

source_text: violently they hate the discerning ones, and the latest of virtues, which is uprightness.
target_text: violently they hate the discerning ones, and the latest of virtues, which is uprightness.

source_text: Backward they always gaze toward dark ages:
target_text: Backward they always gaze toward dark ages:

source_text: Too well do I know those godlike ones:
target_text: Too well do I know those godlike ones:

source_text: they insist on being believed in, and that doubt is sin.
target_text: they insist on being believed in, and that doubt is sin.

source_text: Too well, also, do I know what they themselves most believe in.
target_text: Too well, also, do I know what they themselves most believe in.

source_text: Verily, not in backworlds and redeeming blood-drops:
target_text: Verily, not in backworlds and redeeming blood-drops:

source_text: but in the body do they also believe most;
target_text: but in the body do they also believe most;

source_text: and their own body is for them the thing-in-itself.
target_text: and their own body is for them the thing-in-itself.

source_text: But it is a sickly thing to them, and gladly would they get out of their skin.
target_text: But it is a sickly thing to them, and gladly would they get out of their skin.

source_text: Therefore hearken they to the preachers of death, and themselves preach backworlds.
target_text: Therefore hearken they to the preachers of death, and themselves preach backworlds.

source_text: Hearken rather, my brethren, to the voice of the healthy body;
target_text: Hearken rather, my brethren, to the voice of the healthy body;

source_text: it is a more upright and pure voice.
target_text: it is a more upright and pure voice.

source_text: More uprightly and purely speaketh the healthy body, perfect and square-built;
target_text: More uprightly and purely speaketh the healthy body, perfect and square-built;

source_text: and it speaketh of the meaning of the earth.
target_text: and it speaketh of the meaning of the earth.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: I wish them neither to learn afresh, nor teach anew, but only to bid farewell to their own bodies, -
target_text: I wish them neither to learn afresh, nor teach anew, but only to bid farewell to their own bodies, -

source_text: "Body am I, and soul"
target_text: "Body am I, and soul"

source_text: so saith the child.
target_text: so saith the child.

source_text: And why should one not speak like children?
target_text: And why should one not speak like children?

source_text: But the awakened one, the knowing one, saith:
target_text: But the awakened one, the knowing one, saith:

source_text: and soul is only the name of something in the body.
target_text: and soul is only the name of something in the body.

source_text: a little instrument and plaything of thy big sagacity.
target_text: a little instrument and plaything of thy big sagacity.

source_text: sayest thou, and art proud of that word.
target_text: sayest thou, and art proud of that word.

source_text: But the greater thing -
target_text: But the greater thing -

source_text: in which thou art unwilling to believe -
target_text: in which thou art unwilling to believe -

source_text: is thy body with its big sagacity;
target_text: is thy body with its big sagacity;

source_text: But sense and spirit would fain persuade thee that they are the end of all things:
target_text: But sense and spirit would fain persuade thee that they are the end of all things:

source_text: so vain are they.
target_text: so vain are they.

source_text: behind them there is still the Self.
target_text: behind them there is still the Self.

source_text: The Self seeketh with the eyes of the senses, it hearkeneth also with the ears of the spirit.
target_text: The Self seeketh with the eyes of the senses, it hearkeneth also with the ears of the spirit.

source_text: Ever hearkeneth the Self, and seeketh;
target_text: Ever hearkeneth the Self, and seeketh;

source_text: it compareth, mastereth, conquereth, and destroyeth.
target_text: it compareth, mastereth, conquereth, and destroyeth.

source_text: Behind thy thoughts and feelings, my brother, there is a mighty lord, an unknown sage -
target_text: Behind thy thoughts and feelings, my brother, there is a mighty lord, an unknown sage -

source_text: it is called Self;
target_text: it is called Self;

source_text: it dwelleth in thy body, it is thy body.
target_text: it dwelleth in thy body, it is thy body.

source_text: There is more sagacity in thy body than in thy best wisdom.
target_text: There is more sagacity in thy body than in thy best wisdom.

source_text: And who then knoweth why thy body requireth just thy best wisdom?
target_text: And who then knoweth why thy body requireth just thy best wisdom?

source_text: "What are these prancings and flights of thought unto me?"
target_text: "What are these prancings and flights of thought unto me?"

source_text: it saith to itself.
target_text: it saith to itself.
