target_text: downward into the valleys will I hurl my speech.

source_text: And let the stream of my love sweep into unfrequented channels!
target_text: And let the stream of my love sweep into unfrequented channels!

source_text: How should a stream not finally find its way to the sea!
target_text: How should a stream not finally find its way to the sea!

source_text: Forsooth, there is a lake in me, sequestered and self-sufficing;
target_text: Forsooth, there is a lake in me, sequestered and self-sufficing;

source_text: but the stream of my love beareth this along with it, down -
target_text: but the stream of my love beareth this along with it, down -

source_text: tired have I become - like all creators - of the old tongues.
target_text: tired have I become - like all creators - of the old tongues.

source_text: Too slowly runneth all speaking for me: -
target_text: Too slowly runneth all speaking for me: -

source_text: And even thee will I whip with my spite!
target_text: And even thee will I whip with my spite!

source_text: And mine enemies amongst them!
target_text: And mine enemies amongst them!

source_text: How I now love every one unto whom I may but speak!
target_text: How I now love every one unto whom I may but speak!

source_text: Even mine enemies pertain to my bliss.
target_text: Even mine enemies pertain to my bliss.

source_text: And when I want to mount my wildest horse, then doth my spear always help me up best:
target_text: And when I want to mount my wildest horse, then doth my spear always help me up best:

source_text: it is my foot's ever ready servant:
target_text: it is my foot's ever ready servant:

source_text: The spear which I hurl at mine enemies!
target_text: The spear which I hurl at mine enemies!

source_text: How grateful am I to mine enemies that I may at last hurl it!
target_text: How grateful am I to mine enemies that I may at last hurl it!

source_text: Too great hath been the tension of my cloud:
target_text: Too great hath been the tension of my cloud:

source_text: Violently will my breast then heave;
target_text: Violently will my breast then heave;

source_text: violently will it blow its storm over the mountains:
target_text: violently will it blow its storm over the mountains:

source_text: Verily, like a storm cometh my happiness, and my freedom!
target_text: Verily, like a storm cometh my happiness, and my freedom!

source_text: But mine enemies shall think that THE EVIL ONE roareth over their heads.
target_text: But mine enemies shall think that THE EVIL ONE roareth over their heads.

source_text: Yea, ye also, my friends, will be alarmed by my wild wisdom;
target_text: Yea, ye also, my friends, will be alarmed by my wild wisdom;

source_text: and perhaps ye will flee therefrom, along with mine enemies.
target_text: and perhaps ye will flee therefrom, along with mine enemies.

source_text: Ah, that my lioness wisdom would learn to roar softly!
target_text: Ah, that my lioness wisdom would learn to roar softly!

source_text: And much have we already learned with one another!
target_text: And much have we already learned with one another!

source_text: My wild wisdom became pregnant on the lonesome mountains;
target_text: My wild wisdom became pregnant on the lonesome mountains;

source_text: on the rough stones did she bear the youngest of her young.
target_text: on the rough stones did she bear the youngest of her young.

source_text: Now runneth she foolishly in the arid wilderness, and seeketh and seeketh the soft sward -
target_text: Now runneth she foolishly in the arid wilderness, and seeketh and seeketh the soft sward -

source_text: mine old, wild wisdom!
target_text: mine old, wild wisdom!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: and in falling the red skins of them break.
target_text: and in falling the red skins of them break.

source_text: A north wind am I to ripe figs.
target_text: A north wind am I to ripe figs.

source_text: Thus, like figs, do these doctrines fall for you, my friends:
target_text: Thus, like figs, do these doctrines fall for you, my friends:

source_text: It is autumn all around, and clear sky, and afternoon.
target_text: It is autumn all around, and clear sky, and afternoon.

source_text: And out of the midst of superabundance, it is delightful to look out upon distant seas.
target_text: And out of the midst of superabundance, it is delightful to look out upon distant seas.

source_text: Once did people say God, when they looked out upon distant seas;
target_text: Once did people say God, when they looked out upon distant seas;

source_text: now, however, have I taught you to say, Superman.
target_text: now, however, have I taught you to say, Superman.

source_text: God is a conjecture:
target_text: God is a conjecture:

source_text: but I do not wish your conjecturing to reach beyond your creating will.
target_text: but I do not wish your conjecturing to reach beyond your creating will.

source_text: Could ye CREATE a God?
target_text: Could ye CREATE a God?

source_text: Then, I pray you, be silent about all Gods!
target_text: Then, I pray you, be silent about all Gods!

source_text: But into fathers and forefathers of the Superman could ye transform yourselves:
target_text: But into fathers and forefathers of the Superman could ye transform yourselves:

source_text: and let that be your best creating!
target_text: and let that be your best creating!

source_text: God is a conjecture:
target_text: God is a conjecture:

source_text: but I should like your conjecturing restricted to the conceivable.
target_text: but I should like your conjecturing restricted to the conceivable.

source_text: Could ye CONCEIVE a God?
target_text: Could ye CONCEIVE a God?

source_text: But let this mean Will to Truth unto you, that everything be transformed into the humanly conceivable, the humanly visible, the humanly sensible!
target_text: But let this mean Will to Truth unto you, that everything be transformed into the humanly conceivable, the humanly visible, the humanly sensible!

source_text: Your own discernment shall ye follow out to the end!
target_text: Your own discernment shall ye follow out to the end!

source_text: And what ye have called the world shall but be created by you:
target_text: And what ye have called the world shall but be created by you:

source_text: your reason, your likeness, your will, your love, shall it itself become!
target_text: your reason, your likeness, your will, your love, shall it itself become!

source_text: But that I may reveal my heart entirely unto you, my friends:
target_text: But that I may reveal my heart entirely unto you, my friends:

source_text: IF there were gods, how could I endure it to be no God!
target_text: IF there were gods, how could I endure it to be no God!

source_text: THEREFORE there are no Gods.
target_text: THEREFORE there are no Gods.

source_text: Yea, I have drawn the conclusion; now, however, doth it draw me.
target_text: Yea, I have drawn the conclusion; now, however, doth it draw me.

source_text: God is a conjecture:
target_text: God is a conjecture:

source_text: but who could drink all the bitterness of this conjecture without dying?
target_text: but who could drink all the bitterness of this conjecture without dying?

source_text: God is a thought -
target_text: God is a thought -

source_text: it maketh all the straight crooked, and all that standeth reel.
target_text: it maketh all the straight crooked, and all that standeth reel.

source_text: What?
target_text: What?

source_text: Time would be gone, and all the perishable would be but a lie?
target_text: Time would be gone, and all the perishable would be but a lie?

source_text: To think this is giddiness and vertigo to human limbs, and even vomiting to the stomach:
target_text: To think this is giddiness and vertigo to human limbs, and even vomiting to the stomach:

source_text: verily, the reeling sickness do I call it, to conjecture such a thing.
target_text: verily, the reeling sickness do I call it, to conjecture such a thing.

source_text: Evil do I call it and misanthropic:
target_text: Evil do I call it and misanthropic:

source_text: All the imperishable -
target_text: All the imperishable -

source_text: that's but a simile, and the poets lie too much.
target_text: that's but a simile, and the poets lie too much.

source_text: a praise shall they be, and a justification of all perishableness!
target_text: a praise shall they be, and a justification of all perishableness!

source_text: that is the great salvation from suffering, and life's alleviation.
target_text: that is the great salvation from suffering, and life's alleviation.

source_text: But for the creator to appear, suffering itself is needed, and much transformation.
target_text: But for the creator to appear, suffering itself is needed, and much transformation.

source_text: Yea, much bitter dying must there be in your life, ye creators!
target_text: Yea, much bitter dying must there be in your life, ye creators!

source_text: Thus are ye advocates and justifiers of all perishableness.
target_text: Thus are ye advocates and justifiers of all perishableness.

source_text: Many a farewell have I taken; I know the heart-breaking last hours.
target_text: Many a farewell have I taken; I know the heart-breaking last hours.

source_text: But so willeth it my creating Will, my fate.
target_text: But so willeth it my creating Will, my fate.

source_text: Or, to tell you it more candidly: just such a fate - willeth my Will.
target_text: Or, to tell you it more candidly: just such a fate - willeth my Will.

source_text: All FEELING suffereth in me, and is in prison:
target_text: All FEELING suffereth in me, and is in prison:

source_text: but my WILLING ever cometh to me as mine emancipator and comforter.
target_text: but my WILLING ever cometh to me as mine emancipator and comforter.

source_text: Willing emancipateth:
target_text: Willing emancipateth:

source_text: that is the true doctrine of will and emancipation -
target_text: that is the true doctrine of will and emancipation -

source_text: so teacheth you Zarathustra.
target_text: so teacheth you Zarathustra.

source_text: No longer willing, and no longer valuing, and no longer creating!
target_text: No longer willing, and no longer valuing, and no longer creating!

source_text: and if there be innocence in my knowledge, it is because there is will to procreation in it.
target_text: and if there be innocence in my knowledge, it is because there is will to procreation in it.

source_text: Away from God and Gods did this will allure me;
target_text: Away from God and Gods did this will allure me;

source_text: But to man doth it ever impel me anew, my fervent creative will;
target_text: But to man doth it ever impel me anew, my fervent creative will;

source_text: Ah, that it should slumber in the hardest, ugliest stone!
target_text: Ah, that it should slumber in the hardest, ugliest stone!

source_text: Now rageth my hammer ruthlessly against its prison.
target_text: Now rageth my hammer ruthlessly against its prison.

source_text: From the stone fly the fragments: what's that to me?
target_text: From the stone fly the fragments: what's that to me?

source_text: I will complete it: for a shadow came unto me -
target_text: I will complete it: for a shadow came unto me -

source_text: the stillest and lightest of all things once came unto me!
target_text: the stillest and lightest of all things once came unto me!

source_text: The beauty of the Superman came unto me as a shadow.
target_text: The beauty of the Superman came unto me as a shadow.

source_text: Of what account now are - the Gods to me!
target_text: Of what account now are - the Gods to me!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: Behold Zarathustra!
target_text: Behold Zarathustra!

source_text: Walketh he not amongst us as if amongst animals?
target_text: Walketh he not amongst us as if amongst animals?

source_text: But it is better said in this wise:
target_text: But it is better said in this wise:

source_text: The discerning one walketh amongst men AS amongst animals.
target_text: The discerning one walketh amongst men AS amongst animals.

source_text: Man himself is to the discerning one: the animal with red cheeks.
target_text: Man himself is to the discerning one: the animal with red cheeks.

source_text: Thus speaketh the discerning one: shame, shame, shame -
target_text: Thus speaketh the discerning one: shame, shame, shame -

source_text: that is the history of man!
target_text: that is the history of man!

source_text: And on that account doth the noble one enjoin upon himself not to abash:
target_text: And on that account doth the noble one enjoin upon himself not to abash:

source_text: Verily, I like them not, the merciful ones, whose bliss is in their pity:
target_text: Verily, I like them not, the merciful ones, whose bliss is in their pity:

source_text: If I must be pitiful, I dislike to be called so;
target_text: If I must be pitiful, I dislike to be called so;

source_text: and if I be so, it is preferably at a distance.
target_text: and if I be so, it is preferably at a distance.

source_text: and thus do I bid you do, my friends!
target_text: and thus do I bid you do, my friends!

source_text: May my destiny ever lead unafflicted ones like you across my path, and those with whom I MAY have hope and repast and honey in common!
target_text: May my destiny ever lead unafflicted ones like you across my path, and those with whom I MAY have hope and repast and honey in common!

source_text: Verily, I have done this and that for the afflicted:
target_text: Verily, I have done this and that for the afflicted:

source_text: but something better did I always seem to do when I had learned to enjoy myself better.
target_text: but something better did I always seem to do when I had learned to enjoy myself better.

source_text: Since humanity came into being, man hath enjoyed himself too little:
target_text: Since humanity came into being, man hath enjoyed himself too little:

source_text: that alone, my brethren, is our original sin!
target_text: that alone, my brethren, is our original sin!

source_text: And when we learn better to enjoy ourselves, then do we unlearn best to give pain unto others, and to contrive pain.
target_text: And when we learn better to enjoy ourselves, then do we unlearn best to give pain unto others, and to contrive pain.

source_text: Therefore do I wash the hand that hath helped the sufferer;
target_text: Therefore do I wash the hand that hath helped the sufferer;

source_text: therefore do I wipe also my soul.
target_text: therefore do I wipe also my soul.

source_text: For in seeing the sufferer suffering -
target_text: For in seeing the sufferer suffering -

source_text: thereof was I ashamed on account of his shame;
target_text: thereof was I ashamed on account of his shame;

source_text: and in helping him, sorely did I wound his pride.
target_text: and in helping him, sorely did I wound his pride.

source_text: Great obligations do not make grateful, but revengeful;
target_text: Great obligations do not make grateful, but revengeful;

source_text: Be shy in accepting!
target_text: Be shy in accepting!

source_text: Distinguish by accepting!
target_text: Distinguish by accepting!

source_text: Strangers, however, and the poor, may pluck for themselves the fruit from my tree:
target_text: Strangers, however, and the poor, may pluck for themselves the fruit from my tree:

source_text: thus doth it cause less shame.
target_text: thus doth it cause less shame.

source_text: Beggars, however, one should entirely do away with!
target_text: Beggars, however, one should entirely do away with!

source_text: And likewise sinners and bad consciences!
target_text: And likewise sinners and bad consciences!

source_text: Believe me, my friends: the sting of conscience teacheth one to sting.
target_text: Believe me, my friends: the sting of conscience teacheth one to sting.

source_text: The worst things, however, are the petty thoughts.
target_text: The worst things, however, are the petty thoughts.

source_text: To be sure, ye say:
target_text: To be sure, ye say:

source_text: But here one should not wish to be sparing.
target_text: But here one should not wish to be sparing.

source_text: it itcheth and irritateth and breaketh forth -
target_text: it itcheth and irritateth and breaketh forth -

source_text: it speaketh honourably.
target_text: it speaketh honourably.

source_text: saith the evil deed: that is its honourableness.
target_text: saith the evil deed: that is its honourableness.

source_text: But like infection is the petty thought:
target_text: But like infection is the petty thought:

source_text: until the whole body is decayed and withered by the petty infection.
target_text: until the whole body is decayed and withered by the petty infection.

source_text: To him however, who is possessed of a devil, I would whisper this word in the ear:
target_text: To him however, who is possessed of a devil, I would whisper this word in the ear:

source_text: Better for thee to rear up thy devil!
target_text: Better for thee to rear up thy devil!

source_text: Even for thee there is still a path to greatness!
target_text: Even for thee there is still a path to greatness!

source_text: Ah, my brethren!
target_text: Ah, my brethren!

source_text: One knoweth a little too much about every one!
target_text: One knoweth a little too much about every one!

source_text: And many a one becometh transparent to us, but still we can by no means penetrate him.
target_text: And many a one becometh transparent to us, but still we can by no means penetrate him.

source_text: It is difficult to live among men because silence is so difficult.
target_text: It is difficult to live among men because silence is so difficult.

source_text: And not to him who is offensive to us are we most unfair, but to him who doth not concern us at all.
target_text: And not to him who is offensive to us are we most unfair, but to him who doth not concern us at all.

source_text: like a hard bed, however, a camp-bed: thus wilt thou serve him best.
target_text: like a hard bed, however, a camp-bed: thus wilt thou serve him best.

source_text: And if a friend doeth thee wrong, then say:
target_text: And if a friend doeth thee wrong, then say:

source_text: I forgive thee what thou hast done unto me;
target_text: I forgive thee what thou hast done unto me;

source_text: that thou hast done it unto THYSELF, however -
target_text: that thou hast done it unto THYSELF, however -

source_text: how could I forgive that!
target_text: how could I forgive that!

source_text: Thus speaketh all great love: it surpasseth even forgiveness and pity.
target_text: Thus speaketh all great love: it surpasseth even forgiveness and pity.

source_text: One should hold fast one's heart;
target_text: One should hold fast one's heart;

source_text: for when one letteth it go, how quickly doth one's head run away!
target_text: for when one letteth it go, how quickly doth one's head run away!

source_text: Ah, where in the world have there been greater follies than with the pitiful?
target_text: Ah, where in the world have there been greater follies than with the pitiful?

source_text: And what in the world hath caused more suffering than the follies of the pitiful?
target_text: And what in the world hath caused more suffering than the follies of the pitiful?

source_text: Thus spake the devil unto me, once on a time:
target_text: Thus spake the devil unto me, once on a time:

source_text: Even God hath his hell: it is his love for man.
target_text: Even God hath his hell: it is his love for man.

source_text: And lately, did I hear him say these words:
target_text: And lately, did I hear him say these words:

source_text: God is dead: of his pity for man hath God died.
target_text: God is dead: of his pity for man hath God died.

source_text: FROM THENCE there yet cometh unto men a heavy cloud!
target_text: FROM THENCE there yet cometh unto men a heavy cloud!

source_text: Verily, I understand weather-signs!
target_text: Verily, I understand weather-signs!

source_text: But attend also to this word:
target_text: But attend also to this word:

source_text: All great love is above all its pity:
target_text: All great love is above all its pity:

source_text: for it seeketh -
target_text: for it seeketh -

source_text: to create what is loved!
target_text: to create what is loved!

source_text: "Myself do I offer unto my love, AND MY NEIGHBOUR AS MYSELF"
target_text: "Myself do I offer unto my love, AND MY NEIGHBOUR AS MYSELF"

source_text: such is the language of all creators.
target_text: such is the language of all creators.

source_text: All creators, however, are hard.
target_text: All creators, however, are hard.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: And one day Zarathustra made a sign to his disciples, and spake these words unto them:
target_text: And one day Zarathustra made a sign to his disciples, and spake these words unto them:

source_text: but although they are mine enemies, pass them quietly and with sleeping swords!
target_text: but although they are mine enemies, pass them quietly and with sleeping swords!

source_text: Even among them there are heroes;
target_text: Even among them there are heroes;

source_text: many of them have suffered too much -
target_text: many of them have suffered too much -

source_text: so they want to make others suffer.
target_text: so they want to make others suffer.

source_text: Bad enemies are they: nothing is more revengeful than their meekness.
target_text: Bad enemies are they: nothing is more revengeful than their meekness.

source_text: And readily doth he soil himself who toucheth them.
target_text: And readily doth he soil himself who toucheth them.

source_text: But my blood is related to theirs;
target_text: But my blood is related to theirs;

source_text: and I want withal to see my blood honoured in theirs.
target_text: and I want withal to see my blood honoured in theirs.

source_text: And when they had passed, a pain attacked Zarathustra;
target_text: And when they had passed, a pain attacked Zarathustra;

source_text: but not long had he struggled with the pain, when he began to speak thus:
target_text: but not long had he struggled with the pain, when he began to speak thus:

source_text: It moveth my heart for those priests.
target_text: It moveth my heart for those priests.

source_text: They also go against my taste;
target_text: They also go against my taste;

source_text: but that is the smallest matter unto me, since I am among men.
target_text: but that is the smallest matter unto me, since I am among men.

source_text: But I suffer and have suffered with them:
target_text: But I suffer and have suffered with them:

source_text: He whom they call Saviour put them in fetters: -
target_text: He whom they call Saviour put them in fetters: -

source_text: Oh, that some one would save them from their Saviour!
target_text: Oh, that some one would save them from their Saviour!

source_text: On an isle they once thought they had landed, when the sea tossed them about;
target_text: On an isle they once thought they had landed, when the sea tossed them about;

source_text: but behold, it was a slumbering monster!
target_text: but behold, it was a slumbering monster!

source_text: False values and fatuous words:
target_text: False values and fatuous words:

source_text: these are the worst monsters for mortals -
target_text: these are the worst monsters for mortals -

source_text: long slumbereth and waiteth the fate that is in them.
target_text: long slumbereth and waiteth the fate that is in them.

source_text: Oh, just look at those tabernacles which those priests have built themselves!
target_text: Oh, just look at those tabernacles which those priests have built themselves!

source_text: Churches, they call their sweet-smelling caves!
target_text: Churches, they call their sweet-smelling caves!

source_text: Oh, that falsified light, that mustified air!
target_text: Oh, that falsified light, that mustified air!

source_text: But so enjoineth their belief:
target_text: But so enjoineth their belief:

source_text: "On your knees, up the stair, ye sinners!"
target_text: "On your knees, up the stair, ye sinners!"

source_text: Verily, rather would I see a shameless one than the distorted eyes of their shame and devotion!
target_text: Verily, rather would I see a shameless one than the distorted eyes of their shame and devotion!

source_text: Was it not those who sought to conceal themselves, and were ashamed under the clear sky?
target_text: Was it not those who sought to conceal themselves, and were ashamed under the clear sky?

source_text: will I again turn my heart to the seats of this God.
target_text: will I again turn my heart to the seats of this God.

source_text: They called God that which opposed and afflicted them:
target_text: They called God that which opposed and afflicted them:

source_text: and verily, there was much hero-spirit in their worship!
target_text: and verily, there was much hero-spirit in their worship!

source_text: And they knew not how to love their God otherwise than by nailing men to the cross!
target_text: And they knew not how to love their God otherwise than by nailing men to the cross!

source_text: Better songs would they have to sing, for me to believe in their Saviour:
target_text: Better songs would they have to sing, for me to believe in their Saviour:

source_text: more like saved ones would his disciples have to appear unto me!
target_text: more like saved ones would his disciples have to appear unto me!

source_text: Naked, would I like to see them:
target_text: Naked, would I like to see them:

source_text: for beauty alone should preach penitence.
target_text: for beauty alone should preach penitence.

source_text: But whom would that disguised affliction convince!
target_text: But whom would that disguised affliction convince!

source_text: Verily, they themselves never trod the carpets of knowledge!
target_text: Verily, they themselves never trod the carpets of knowledge!

source_text: Of defects did the spirit of those Saviours consist;
target_text: Of defects did the spirit of those Saviours consist;

source_text: In their pity was their spirit drowned;
target_text: In their pity was their spirit drowned;

source_text: as if there were but one foot-bridge to the future!
target_text: as if there were but one foot-bridge to the future!

source_text: Verily, those shepherds also were still of the flock!
target_text: Verily, those shepherds also were still of the flock!

source_text: Small spirits and spacious souls had those shepherds:
target_text: Small spirits and spacious souls had those shepherds:

source_text: but, my brethren, what small domains have even the most spacious souls hitherto been!
target_text: but, my brethren, what small domains have even the most spacious souls hitherto been!

source_text: Characters of blood did they write on the way they went, and their folly taught that truth is proved by blood.
target_text: Characters of blood did they write on the way they went, and their folly taught that truth is proved by blood.

source_text: But blood is the very worst witness to truth;
target_text: But blood is the very worst witness to truth;

source_text: And when a person goeth through fire for his teaching -
target_text: And when a person goeth through fire for his teaching -

source_text: what doth that prove!
target_text: what doth that prove!

source_text: It is more, verily, when out of one's own burning cometh one's own teaching!
target_text: It is more, verily, when out of one's own burning cometh one's own teaching!

source_text: Sultry heart and cold head;
target_text: Sultry heart and cold head;

source_text: where these meet, there ariseth the blusterer, the
target_text: where these meet, there ariseth the blusterer, the

source_text: Greater ones, verily, have there been, and higher-born ones, than those whom the people call Saviours, those rapturous blusterers!
target_text: Greater ones, verily, have there been, and higher-born ones, than those whom the people call Saviours, those rapturous blusterers!

source_text: And by still greater ones than any of the Saviours must ye be saved, my brethren, if ye would find the way to freedom!
target_text: And by still greater ones than any of the Saviours must ye be saved, my brethren, if ye would find the way to freedom!

source_text: Never yet hath there been a Superman.
target_text: Never yet hath there been a Superman.

source_text: Naked have I seen both of them, the greatest man and the smallest man:
target_text: Naked have I seen both of them, the greatest man and the smallest man:

source_text: All-too-similar are they still to each other.
target_text: All-too-similar are they still to each other.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: But beauty's voice speaketh gently:
target_text: But beauty's voice speaketh gently:

source_text: it appealeth only to the most awakened souls.
target_text: it appealeth only to the most awakened souls.

source_text: Gently vibrated and laughed unto me to-day my buckler;
target_text: Gently vibrated and laughed unto me to-day my buckler;

source_text: At you, ye virtuous ones, laughed my beauty to-day.
target_text: At you, ye virtuous ones, laughed my beauty to-day.

source_text: And thus came its voice unto me:
target_text: And thus came its voice unto me:

source_text: "They want - to be paid besides!"
target_text: "They want - to be paid besides!"

source_text: Ye want to be paid besides, ye virtuous ones!
target_text: Ye want to be paid besides, ye virtuous ones!

source_text: And verily, I do not even teach that virtue is its own reward.
target_text: And verily, I do not even teach that virtue is its own reward.

source_text: this is my sorrow:
target_text: this is my sorrow:

source_text: into the basis of things have reward and punishment been insinuated -
target_text: into the basis of things have reward and punishment been insinuated -

source_text: and now even into the basis of your souls, ye virtuous ones!
target_text: and now even into the basis of your souls, ye virtuous ones!

source_text: All the secrets of your heart shall be brought to light;
target_text: All the secrets of your heart shall be brought to light;

source_text: and when ye lie in the sun, grubbed up and broken, then will also your falsehood be separated from your truth.
target_text: and when ye lie in the sun, grubbed up and broken, then will also your falsehood be separated from your truth.

source_text: For this is your truth:
target_text: For this is your truth:

source_text: ye are TOO PURE for the filth of the words:
target_text: ye are TOO PURE for the filth of the words:

source_text: vengeance, punishment, recompense, retribution.
target_text: vengeance, punishment, recompense, retribution.

source_text: but when did one hear of a mother wanting to be paid for her love?
target_text: but when did one hear of a mother wanting to be paid for her love?

source_text: It is your dearest Self, your virtue.
target_text: It is your dearest Self, your virtue.

source_text: The ring's thirst is in you:
target_text: The ring's thirst is in you:

source_text: to reach itself again struggleth every ring, and turneth itself.
target_text: to reach itself again struggleth every ring, and turneth itself.

source_text: And like the star that goeth out, so is every work of your virtue:
target_text: And like the star that goeth out, so is every work of your virtue:

source_text: and when will it cease to be on its way?
target_text: and when will it cease to be on its way?

source_text: Thus is the light of your virtue still on its way, even when its work is done.
target_text: Thus is the light of your virtue still on its way, even when its work is done.

source_text: Be it forgotten and dead, still its ray of light liveth and travelleth.
target_text: Be it forgotten and dead, still its ray of light liveth and travelleth.

source_text: But sure enough there are those to whom virtue meaneth writhing under the lash:
target_text: But sure enough there are those to whom virtue meaneth writhing under the lash:

source_text: and ye have hearkened too much unto their crying!
target_text: and ye have hearkened too much unto their crying!

source_text: And others are there who call virtue the slothfulness of their vices;
target_text: And others are there who call virtue the slothfulness of their vices;

source_text: And others are there who are drawn downwards: their devils draw them.
target_text: And others are there who are drawn downwards: their devils draw them.

source_text: their crying also hath reached your ears, ye virtuous ones:
target_text: their crying also hath reached your ears, ye virtuous ones:

source_text: "What I am NOT, that, that is God to me, and virtue!"
target_text: "What I am NOT, that, that is God to me, and virtue!"

source_text: And others are there who go along heavily and creakingly, like carts taking stones downhill:
target_text: And others are there who go along heavily and creakingly, like carts taking stones downhill:

source_text: they talk much of dignity and virtue -
target_text: they talk much of dignity and virtue -

source_text: their drag they call virtue!
target_text: their drag they call virtue!

source_text: And others are there who are like eight-day clocks when wound up;
target_text: And others are there who are like eight-day clocks when wound up;

source_text: they tick, and want people to call ticking - virtue.
target_text: they tick, and want people to call ticking - virtue.

source_text: Verily, in those have I mine amusement:
target_text: Verily, in those have I mine amusement:

source_text: so that the world is drowned in their unrighteousness.
target_text: so that the world is drowned in their unrighteousness.

source_text: how ineptly cometh the word
target_text: how ineptly cometh the word

source_text: out of their mouth!
target_text: out of their mouth!

source_text: "I am just,"
target_text: "I am just,"

source_text: it always soundeth like:
target_text: it always soundeth like:

source_text: With their virtues they want to scratch out the eyes of their enemies;
target_text: With their virtues they want to scratch out the eyes of their enemies;

source_text: and they elevate themselves only that they may lower others.
target_text: and they elevate themselves only that they may lower others.

source_text: And again there are those who sit in their swamp, and speak thus from among the bulrushes:
target_text: And again there are those who sit in their swamp, and speak thus from among the bulrushes:

source_text: Virtue - that is to sit quietly in the swamp.
target_text: Virtue - that is to sit quietly in the swamp.

source_text: We bite no one, and go out of the way of him who would bite;
target_text: We bite no one, and go out of the way of him who would bite;

source_text: And again there are those who love attitudes, and think that virtue is a sort of attitude.
target_text: And again there are those who love attitudes, and think that virtue is a sort of attitude.

source_text: Their knees continually adore, and their hands are eulogies of virtue, but their heart knoweth naught thereof.
target_text: Their knees continually adore, and their hands are eulogies of virtue, but their heart knoweth naught thereof.

source_text: "Virtue is necessary"
target_text: "Virtue is necessary"

source_text: but after all they believe only that policemen are necessary.
target_text: but after all they believe only that policemen are necessary.

source_text: thus calleth he his evil eye virtue.
target_text: thus calleth he his evil eye virtue.

source_text: And some want to be edified and raised up, and call it virtue:
target_text: And some want to be edified and raised up, and call it virtue:

source_text: and likewise call it virtue.
target_text: and likewise call it virtue.

source_text: And thus do almost all think that they participate in virtue;
target_text: And thus do almost all think that they participate in virtue;

source_text: and at least every one claimeth to be an authority on
target_text: and at least every one claimeth to be an authority on

source_text: "good"
target_text: "good"

source_text: What do YE know of virtue!
target_text: What do YE know of virtue!

source_text: What COULD ye know of virtue!
target_text: What COULD ye know of virtue!

source_text: But that ye, my friends, might become weary of the old words which ye have learned from the fools and liars:
target_text: But that ye, my friends, might become weary of the old words which ye have learned from the fools and liars:

source_text: That ye might become weary of the words
target_text: That ye might become weary of the words

source_text: "punishment,"
target_text: "punishment,"

source_text: righteous vengeance.
target_text: righteous vengeance.

source_text: my friends!
target_text: my friends!

source_text: That YOUR very Self be in your action, as the mother is in the child:
target_text: That YOUR very Self be in your action, as the mother is in the child:

source_text: let that be YOUR formula of virtue!
target_text: let that be YOUR formula of virtue!

source_text: They played by the sea -
target_text: They played by the sea -

source_text: then came there a wave and swept their playthings into the deep:
target_text: then came there a wave and swept their playthings into the deep:

source_text: and now do they cry.
target_text: and now do they cry.

source_text: But the same wave shall bring them new playthings, and spread before them new speckled shells!
target_text: But the same wave shall bring them new playthings, and spread before them new speckled shells!

source_text: Thus will they be comforted;
target_text: Thus will they be comforted;

source_text: and new speckled shells!
target_text: and new speckled shells!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: but where the rabble also drink, there all fountains are poisoned.
target_text: but where the rabble also drink, there all fountains are poisoned.

source_text: To everything cleanly am I well disposed;
target_text: To everything cleanly am I well disposed;

source_text: but I hate to see the grinning mouths and the thirst of the unclean.
target_text: but I hate to see the grinning mouths and the thirst of the unclean.

source_text: They cast their eye down into the fountain:
target_text: They cast their eye down into the fountain:

source_text: and now glanceth up to me their odious smile out of the fountain.
target_text: and now glanceth up to me their odious smile out of the fountain.

source_text: The holy water have they poisoned with their lustfulness;
target_text: The holy water have they poisoned with their lustfulness;

source_text: and when they called their filthy dreams delight, then poisoned they also the words.
target_text: and when they called their filthy dreams delight, then poisoned they also the words.

source_text: unsteady, and withered at the top, doth their look make the fruit-tree.
target_text: unsteady, and withered at the top, doth their look make the fruit-tree.

source_text: And many a one who hath turned away from life, hath only turned away from the rabble:
target_text: And many a one who hath turned away from life, hath only turned away from the rabble:

source_text: he hated to share with them fountain, flame, and fruit.
target_text: he hated to share with them fountain, flame, and fruit.

source_text: And many a one who hath gone into the wilderness and suffered thirst with beasts of prey, disliked only to sit at the cistern with filthy camel-drivers.
target_text: And many a one who hath gone into the wilderness and suffered thirst with beasts of prey, disliked only to sit at the cistern with filthy camel-drivers.

source_text: And it is not the mouthful which hath most choked me, to know that life itself requireth enmity and death and torture-crosses:
target_text: And it is not the mouthful which hath most choked me, to know that life itself requireth enmity and death and torture-crosses:

source_text: But I asked once, and suffocated almost with my question: What?
target_text: But I asked once, and suffocated almost with my question: What?

source_text: is the rabble also NECESSARY for life?
target_text: is the rabble also NECESSARY for life?

source_text: Are poisoned fountains necessary, and stinking fires, and filthy dreams, and maggots in the bread of life?
target_text: Are poisoned fountains necessary, and stinking fires, and filthy dreams, and maggots in the bread of life?

source_text: Not my hatred, but my loathing, gnawed hungrily at my life!
target_text: Not my hatred, but my loathing, gnawed hungrily at my life!

source_text: And on the rulers turned I my back, when I saw what they now call ruling:
target_text: And on the rulers turned I my back, when I saw what they now call ruling:

source_text: to traffic and bargain for power -
target_text: to traffic and bargain for power -

source_text: with the rabble!
target_text: with the rabble!

source_text: Amongst peoples of a strange language did I dwell, with stopped ears:
target_text: Amongst peoples of a strange language did I dwell, with stopped ears:

source_text: And holding my nose, I went morosely through all yesterdays and to-days:
target_text: And holding my nose, I went morosely through all yesterdays and to-days:

source_text: Like a cripple become deaf, and blind, and dumb -
target_text: Like a cripple become deaf, and blind, and dumb -

source_text: thus have I lived long;
target_text: thus have I lived long;

source_text: that I might not live with the power-rabble, the scribe-rabble, and the pleasure-rabble.
target_text: that I might not live with the power-rabble, the scribe-rabble, and the pleasure-rabble.

source_text: alms of delight were its refreshment;
target_text: alms of delight were its refreshment;

source_text: What hath happened unto me?
target_text: What hath happened unto me?

source_text: How have I freed myself from loathing?
target_text: How have I freed myself from loathing?

source_text: Who hath rejuvenated mine eye?
target_text: Who hath rejuvenated mine eye?

source_text: How have I flown to the height where no rabble any longer sit at the wells?
target_text: How have I flown to the height where no rabble any longer sit at the wells?

source_text: Did my loathing itself create for me wings and fountain-divining powers?
target_text: Did my loathing itself create for me wings and fountain-divining powers?

source_text: Verily, to the loftiest height had I to fly, to find again the well of delight!
target_text: Verily, to the loftiest height had I to fly, to find again the well of delight!

source_text: Oh, I have found it, my brethren!
target_text: Oh, I have found it, my brethren!

source_text: Almost too violently dost thou flow for me, thou fountain of delight!
target_text: Almost too violently dost thou flow for me, thou fountain of delight!

source_text: And often emptiest thou the goblet again, in wanting to fill it!
target_text: And often emptiest thou the goblet again, in wanting to fill it!

source_text: And yet must I learn to approach thee more modestly:
target_text: And yet must I learn to approach thee more modestly:

source_text: My heart on which my summer burneth, my short, hot, melancholy, over-happy summer:
target_text: My heart on which my summer burneth, my short, hot, melancholy, over-happy summer:

source_text: Past, the lingering distress of my spring!
target_text: Past, the lingering distress of my spring!

source_text: Summer have I become entirely, and summer-noontide!
target_text: Summer have I become entirely, and summer-noontide!

source_text: A summer on the loftiest height, with cold fountains and blissful stillness:
target_text: A summer on the loftiest height, with cold fountains and blissful stillness:

source_text: oh, come, my friends, that the stillness may become more blissful!
target_text: oh, come, my friends, that the stillness may become more blissful!

source_text: For this is OUR height and our home:
target_text: For this is OUR height and our home:

source_text: too high and steep do we here dwell for all uncleanly ones and their thirst.
target_text: too high and steep do we here dwell for all uncleanly ones and their thirst.

source_text: Cast but your pure eyes into the well of my delight, my friends!
target_text: Cast but your pure eyes into the well of my delight, my friends!

source_text: How could it become turbid thereby!
target_text: How could it become turbid thereby!

source_text: It shall laugh back to you with ITS purity.
target_text: It shall laugh back to you with ITS purity.

source_text: Verily, no food of which the impure could be fellow-partakers!
target_text: Verily, no food of which the impure could be fellow-partakers!

source_text: Fire, would they think they devoured, and burn their mouths!
target_text: Fire, would they think they devoured, and burn their mouths!

source_text: Verily, no abodes do we here keep ready for the impure!
target_text: Verily, no abodes do we here keep ready for the impure!

source_text: An ice-cave to their bodies would our happiness be, and to their spirits!
target_text: An ice-cave to their bodies would our happiness be, and to their spirits!

source_text: thus live the strong winds.
target_text: thus live the strong winds.

source_text: And like a wind will I one day blow amongst them, and with my spirit, take the breath from their spirit:
target_text: And like a wind will I one day blow amongst them, and with my spirit, take the breath from their spirit:

source_text: thus willeth my future.
target_text: thus willeth my future.

source_text: Verily, a strong wind is Zarathustra to all low places;
target_text: Verily, a strong wind is Zarathustra to all low places;

source_text: "Take care not to spit AGAINST the wind!"
target_text: "Take care not to spit AGAINST the wind!"

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: Wouldst thou see the tarantula itself?
target_text: Wouldst thou see the tarantula itself?

source_text: Here hangeth its web: touch this, so that it may tremble.
target_text: Here hangeth its web: touch this, so that it may tremble.

source_text: Black on thy back is thy triangle and symbol;
target_text: Black on thy back is thy triangle and symbol;

source_text: and I know also what is in thy soul.
target_text: and I know also what is in thy soul.

source_text: Revenge is in thy soul:
target_text: Revenge is in thy soul:

source_text: wherever thou bitest, there ariseth black scab;
target_text: wherever thou bitest, there ariseth black scab;

source_text: with revenge, thy poison maketh the soul giddy!
target_text: with revenge, thy poison maketh the soul giddy!

source_text: But I will soon bring your hiding-places to the light:
target_text: But I will soon bring your hiding-places to the light:

source_text: therefore do I laugh in your face my laughter of the height.
target_text: therefore do I laugh in your face my laughter of the height.

source_text: Therefore do I tear at your web, that your rage may lure you out of your den of lies, and that your revenge may leap forth from behind your word
target_text: Therefore do I tear at your web, that your rage may lure you out of your den of lies, and that your revenge may leap forth from behind your word

source_text: Because, FOR MAN TO BE REDEEMED FROM REVENGE -
target_text: Because, FOR MAN TO BE REDEEMED FROM REVENGE -

source_text: that is for me the bridge to the highest hope, and a rainbow after long storms.
target_text: that is for me the bridge to the highest hope, and a rainbow after long storms.

source_text: Otherwise, however, would the tarantulas have it.
target_text: Otherwise, however, would the tarantulas have it.

source_text: thus do they talk to one another.
target_text: thus do they talk to one another.

source_text: "Vengeance will we use, and insult, against all who are not like us"
target_text: "Vengeance will we use, and insult, against all who are not like us"

source_text: that itself shall henceforth be the name of virtue;
target_text: that itself shall henceforth be the name of virtue;

source_text: your most secret tyrant-longings disguise themselves thus in virtue-words!
target_text: your most secret tyrant-longings disguise themselves thus in virtue-words!

source_text: Fretted conceit and suppressed envy -
target_text: Fretted conceit and suppressed envy -

source_text: in you break they forth as flame and frenzy of vengeance.
target_text: in you break they forth as flame and frenzy of vengeance.

source_text: Inspired ones they resemble:
target_text: Inspired ones they resemble:

source_text: but it is not the heart that inspireth them -
target_text: but it is not the heart that inspireth them -

source_text: but vengeance.
target_text: but vengeance.

source_text: And when they become subtle and cold, it is not spirit, but envy, that maketh them so.
target_text: And when they become subtle and cold, it is not spirit, but envy, that maketh them so.

source_text: and this is the sign of their jealousy -
target_text: and this is the sign of their jealousy -

source_text: they always go too far:
target_text: they always go too far:

source_text: so that their fatigue hath at last to go to sleep on the snow.
target_text: so that their fatigue hath at last to go to sleep on the snow.

source_text: and being judge seemeth to them bliss.
target_text: and being judge seemeth to them bliss.

source_text: But thus do I counsel you, my friends:
target_text: But thus do I counsel you, my friends:

source_text: distrust all in whom the impulse to punish is powerful!
target_text: distrust all in whom the impulse to punish is powerful!

source_text: They are people of bad race and lineage;
target_text: They are people of bad race and lineage;

source_text: out of their countenances peer the hangman and the sleuth-hound.
target_text: out of their countenances peer the hangman and the sleuth-hound.

source_text: Distrust all those who talk much of their justice!
target_text: Distrust all those who talk much of their justice!

source_text: Verily, in their souls not only honey is lacking.
target_text: Verily, in their souls not only honey is lacking.

source_text: And when they call themselves
target_text: And when they call themselves

source_text: "the good and just,"
target_text: "the good and just,"

source_text: forget not, that for them to be Pharisees, nothing is lacking but -
target_text: forget not, that for them to be Pharisees, nothing is lacking but -

source_text: My friends, I will not be mixed up and confounded with others.
target_text: My friends, I will not be mixed up and confounded with others.

source_text: is because they would thereby do injury.
target_text: is because they would thereby do injury.

source_text: To those would they thereby do injury who have power at present:
target_text: To those would they thereby do injury who have power at present:

source_text: for with those the preaching of death is still most at home.
target_text: for with those the preaching of death is still most at home.

source_text: and they themselves were formerly the best world-maligners and heretic-burners.
target_text: and they themselves were formerly the best world-maligners and heretic-burners.

source_text: With these preachers of equality will I not be mixed up and confounded.
target_text: With these preachers of equality will I not be mixed up and confounded.

source_text: For thus speaketh justice UNTO ME:
target_text: For thus speaketh justice UNTO ME:

source_text: Men are not equal.
target_text: Men are not equal.

source_text: And neither shall they become so!
target_text: And neither shall they become so!

source_text: thus doth my great love make me speak!
target_text: thus doth my great love make me speak!

source_text: Inventors of figures and phantoms shall they be in their hostilities;
target_text: Inventors of figures and phantoms shall they be in their hostilities;

source_text: and with those figures and phantoms shall they yet fight with each other the supreme fight!
target_text: and with those figures and phantoms shall they yet fight with each other the supreme fight!

source_text: Good and evil, and rich and poor, and high and low, and all names of values:
target_text: Good and evil, and rich and poor, and high and low, and all names of values:

source_text: weapons shall they be, and sounding signs, that life must again and again surpass itself!
target_text: weapons shall they be, and sounding signs, that life must again and again surpass itself!

source_text: Aloft will it build itself with columns and stairs -
target_text: Aloft will it build itself with columns and stairs -

source_text: life itself:
target_text: life itself:

source_text: THEREFORE doth it require elevation!
target_text: THEREFORE doth it require elevation!

source_text: And just behold, my friends!
target_text: And just behold, my friends!

source_text: just behold it with enlightened eyes!
target_text: just behold it with enlightened eyes!

source_text: Verily, he who here towered aloft his thoughts in stone, knew as well as the wisest ones about the secret of life!
target_text: Verily, he who here towered aloft his thoughts in stone, knew as well as the wisest ones about the secret of life!

source_text: That there is struggle and inequality even in beauty, and war for power and supremacy:
target_text: That there is struggle and inequality even in beauty, and war for power and supremacy:

source_text: that doth he here teach us in the plainest parable.
target_text: that doth he here teach us in the plainest parable.

source_text: How divinely do vault and arch here contrast in the struggle:
target_text: How divinely do vault and arch here contrast in the struggle:

source_text: how with light and shade they strive against each other, the divinely striving ones.
target_text: how with light and shade they strive against each other, the divinely striving ones.

source_text: Thus, steadfast and beautiful, let us also be enemies, my friends!
target_text: Thus, steadfast and beautiful, let us also be enemies, my friends!

source_text: Divinely will we strive AGAINST one another!
target_text: Divinely will we strive AGAINST one another!

source_text: There hath the tarantula bit me myself, mine old enemy!
target_text: There hath the tarantula bit me myself, mine old enemy!

source_text: Divinely steadfast and beautiful, it hath bit me on the finger!
target_text: Divinely steadfast and beautiful, it hath bit me on the finger!

source_text: "Punishment must there be, and justice"
target_text: "Punishment must there be, and justice"

source_text: Yea, it hath revenged itself!
target_text: Yea, it hath revenged itself!

source_text: And alas!
target_text: And alas!

source_text: now will it make my soul also dizzy with revenge!
target_text: now will it make my soul also dizzy with revenge!

source_text: That I may NOT turn dizzy, however, bind me fast, my friends, to this pillar!
target_text: That I may NOT turn dizzy, however, bind me fast, my friends, to this pillar!

source_text: Rather will I be a pillar-saint than a whirl of vengeance!
target_text: Rather will I be a pillar-saint than a whirl of vengeance!

source_text: Verily, no cyclone or whirlwind is Zarathustra:
target_text: Verily, no cyclone or whirlwind is Zarathustra:

source_text: and if he be a dancer, he is not at all a tarantula-dancer!
target_text: and if he be a dancer, he is not at all a tarantula-dancer!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: NOT the truth!
target_text: NOT the truth!

source_text: And just on that account did they pay you reverence.
target_text: And just on that account did they pay you reverence.

source_text: And on that account also did they tolerate your unbelief, because it was a pleasantry and a by-path for the people.
target_text: And on that account also did they tolerate your unbelief, because it was a pleasantry and a by-path for the people.

source_text: Thus doth the master give free scope to his slaves, and even enjoyeth their presumptuousness.
target_text: Thus doth the master give free scope to his slaves, and even enjoyeth their presumptuousness.

source_text: But he who is hated by the people, as the wolf by the dogs -
target_text: But he who is hated by the people, as the wolf by the dogs -

source_text: is the free spirit, the enemy of fetters, the non-adorer, the dweller in the woods.
target_text: is the free spirit, the enemy of fetters, the non-adorer, the dweller in the woods.

source_text: To hunt him out of his lair - that was always called
target_text: To hunt him out of his lair - that was always called

source_text: "sense of right"
target_text: "sense of right"

source_text: For there the truth is, where the people are!
target_text: For there the truth is, where the people are!

source_text: Woe, woe to the seeking ones!
target_text: Woe, woe to the seeking ones!

source_text: thus hath it echoed through all time.
target_text: thus hath it echoed through all time.

source_text: Your people would ye justify in their reverence: that called ye
target_text: Your people would ye justify in their reverence: that called ye

source_text: "Will to Truth,"
target_text: "Will to Truth,"

source_text: And your heart hath always said to itself:
target_text: And your heart hath always said to itself:

source_text: From the people have I come:
target_text: From the people have I come:

source_text: from thence came to me also the voice of God.
target_text: from thence came to me also the voice of God.

source_text: Stiff-necked and artful, like the ass, have ye always been, as the advocates of the people.
target_text: Stiff-necked and artful, like the ass, have ye always been, as the advocates of the people.

source_text: And many a powerful one who wanted to run well with the people, hath harnessed in front of his horses -
target_text: And many a powerful one who wanted to run well with the people, hath harnessed in front of his horses -

source_text: a donkey, a famous wise man.
target_text: a donkey, a famous wise man.

source_text: And now, ye famous wise ones, I would have you finally throw off entirely the skin of the lion!
target_text: And now, ye famous wise ones, I would have you finally throw off entirely the skin of the lion!

source_text: The skin of the beast of prey, the speckled skin, and the dishevelled locks of the investigator, the searcher, and the conqueror!
target_text: The skin of the beast of prey, the speckled skin, and the dishevelled locks of the investigator, the searcher, and the conqueror!

source_text: for me to learn to believe in your
target_text: for me to learn to believe in your

source_text: "conscientiousness,"
target_text: "conscientiousness,"

source_text: ye would first have to break your venerating will.
target_text: ye would first have to break your venerating will.

source_text: In the yellow sands and burnt by the sun, he doubtless peereth thirstily at the isles rich in fountains, where life reposeth under shady trees.
target_text: In the yellow sands and burnt by the sun, he doubtless peereth thirstily at the isles rich in fountains, where life reposeth under shady trees.

source_text: But his thirst doth not persuade him to become like those comfortable ones:
target_text: But his thirst doth not persuade him to become like those comfortable ones:

source_text: Hungry, fierce, lonesome, God-forsaken:
target_text: Hungry, fierce, lonesome, God-forsaken:

source_text: so doth the lion-will wish itself.
target_text: so doth the lion-will wish itself.

source_text: so is the will of the conscientious.
target_text: so is the will of the conscientious.

source_text: In the wilderness have ever dwelt the conscientious, the free spirits, as lords of the wilderness;
target_text: In the wilderness have ever dwelt the conscientious, the free spirits, as lords of the wilderness;

source_text: but in the cities dwell the well-foddered, famous wise ones -
target_text: but in the cities dwell the well-foddered, famous wise ones -

source_text: For, always, do they draw, as asses - the PEOPLE'S carts!
target_text: For, always, do they draw, as asses - the PEOPLE'S carts!

source_text: Not that I on that account upbraid them:
target_text: Not that I on that account upbraid them:

source_text: And often have they been good servants and worthy of their hire.
target_text: And often have they been good servants and worthy of their hire.

source_text: For thus saith virtue:
target_text: For thus saith virtue:

source_text: If thou must be a servant, seek him unto whom thy service is most useful!
target_text: If thou must be a servant, seek him unto whom thy service is most useful!

source_text: The spirit and virtue of thy master shall advance by thou being his servant:
target_text: The spirit and virtue of thy master shall advance by thou being his servant:

source_text: thus wilt thou thyself advance with his spirit and virtue!
target_text: thus wilt thou thyself advance with his spirit and virtue!

source_text: And verily, ye famous wise ones, ye servants of the people!
target_text: And verily, ye famous wise ones, ye servants of the people!

source_text: Ye yourselves have advanced with the people's spirit and virtue -
target_text: Ye yourselves have advanced with the people's spirit and virtue -

source_text: and the people by you!
target_text: and the people by you!

source_text: But the people ye remain for me, even with your virtues, the people with purblind eyes -
target_text: But the people ye remain for me, even with your virtues, the people with purblind eyes -

source_text: the people who know not what SPIRIT is!
target_text: the people who know not what SPIRIT is!

source_text: by its own torture doth it increase its own knowledge, -
target_text: by its own torture doth it increase its own knowledge, -

source_text: did ye know that before?
target_text: did ye know that before?

source_text: And the spirit's happiness is this:
target_text: And the spirit's happiness is this:

source_text: to be anointed and consecrated with tears as a sacrificial victim, -
target_text: to be anointed and consecrated with tears as a sacrificial victim, -

source_text: did ye know that before?
target_text: did ye know that before?

source_text: It is a small thing for the spirit to remove mountains, -
target_text: It is a small thing for the spirit to remove mountains, -

source_text: did ye know that before?
target_text: did ye know that before?

source_text: Ye know only the sparks of the spirit:
target_text: Ye know only the sparks of the spirit:

source_text: but ye do not see the anvil which it is, and the cruelty of its hammer!
target_text: but ye do not see the anvil which it is, and the cruelty of its hammer!

source_text: Verily, ye know not the spirit's pride!
target_text: Verily, ye know not the spirit's pride!

source_text: But still less could ye endure the spirit's humility, should it ever want to speak!
target_text: But still less could ye endure the spirit's humility, should it ever want to speak!

source_text: And never yet could ye cast your spirit into a pit of snow:
target_text: And never yet could ye cast your spirit into a pit of snow:

source_text: ye are not hot enough for that!
target_text: ye are not hot enough for that!

source_text: Thus are ye unaware, also, of the delight of its coldness.
target_text: Thus are ye unaware, also, of the delight of its coldness.

source_text: In all respects, however, ye make too familiar with the spirit;
target_text: In all respects, however, ye make too familiar with the spirit;

source_text: Ye are not eagles:
target_text: Ye are not eagles:

source_text: thus have ye never experienced the happiness of the alarm of the spirit.
target_text: thus have ye never experienced the happiness of the alarm of the spirit.

source_text: And he who is not a bird should not camp above abysses.
target_text: And he who is not a bird should not camp above abysses.

source_text: Ice-cold are the innermost wells of the spirit:
target_text: Ice-cold are the innermost wells of the spirit:

source_text: a refreshment to hot hands and handlers.
target_text: a refreshment to hot hands and handlers.

source_text: Like the sail trembling with the violence of the spirit, doth my wisdom cross the sea -
target_text: Like the sail trembling with the violence of the spirit, doth my wisdom cross the sea -

source_text: my wild wisdom!
target_text: my wild wisdom!

source_text: how COULD ye go with me!
target_text: how COULD ye go with me!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: And my soul also is a gushing fountain.
target_text: And my soul also is a gushing fountain.

source_text: And my soul also is the song of a loving one.
target_text: And my soul also is the song of a loving one.

source_text: A craving for love is within me, which speaketh itself the language of love.
target_text: A craving for love is within me, which speaketh itself the language of love.

source_text: Light am I: ah, that I were night!
target_text: Light am I: ah, that I were night!

source_text: But it is my lonesomeness to be begirt with light!
target_text: But it is my lonesomeness to be begirt with light!

source_text: Ah, that I were dark and nightly!
target_text: Ah, that I were dark and nightly!

source_text: How would I suck at the breasts of light!
target_text: How would I suck at the breasts of light!

source_text: And you yourselves would I bless, ye twinkling starlets and glow-worms aloft!
target_text: And you yourselves would I bless, ye twinkling starlets and glow-worms aloft!

source_text: and would rejoice in the gifts of your light.
target_text: and would rejoice in the gifts of your light.

source_text: But I live in mine own light, I drink again into myself the flames that break forth from me.
target_text: But I live in mine own light, I drink again into myself the flames that break forth from me.

source_text: I know not the happiness of the receiver;
target_text: I know not the happiness of the receiver;

source_text: and oft have I dreamt that stealing must be more blessed than receiving.
target_text: and oft have I dreamt that stealing must be more blessed than receiving.

source_text: It is my poverty that my hand never ceaseth bestowing;
target_text: It is my poverty that my hand never ceaseth bestowing;

source_text: it is mine envy that I see waiting eyes and the brightened nights of longing.
target_text: it is mine envy that I see waiting eyes and the brightened nights of longing.

source_text: Oh, the misery of all bestowers!
target_text: Oh, the misery of all bestowers!

source_text: They take from me: but do I yet touch their soul?
target_text: They take from me: but do I yet touch their soul?

source_text: and the smallest gap hath finally to be bridged over.
target_text: and the smallest gap hath finally to be bridged over.

source_text: A hunger ariseth out of my beauty:
target_text: A hunger ariseth out of my beauty:

source_text: I should like to injure those I illumine;
target_text: I should like to injure those I illumine;

source_text: I should like to rob those I have gifted: -
target_text: I should like to rob those I have gifted: -

source_text: thus do I hunger for wickedness.
target_text: thus do I hunger for wickedness.

source_text: Withdrawing my hand when another hand already stretcheth out to it;
target_text: Withdrawing my hand when another hand already stretcheth out to it;

source_text: thus do I hunger for wickedness!
target_text: thus do I hunger for wickedness!

source_text: Such revenge doth mine abundance think of:
target_text: Such revenge doth mine abundance think of:

source_text: such mischief welleth out of my lonesomeness.
target_text: such mischief welleth out of my lonesomeness.

source_text: My happiness in bestowing died in bestowing;
target_text: My happiness in bestowing died in bestowing;

source_text: my virtue became weary of itself by its abundance!
target_text: my virtue became weary of itself by its abundance!

source_text: Mine eye no longer overfloweth for the shame of suppliants;
target_text: Mine eye no longer overfloweth for the shame of suppliants;

source_text: my hand hath become too hard for the trembling of filled hands.
target_text: my hand hath become too hard for the trembling of filled hands.

source_text: Whence have gone the tears of mine eye, and the down of my heart?
target_text: Whence have gone the tears of mine eye, and the down of my heart?

source_text: Oh, the lonesomeness of all bestowers!
target_text: Oh, the lonesomeness of all bestowers!

source_text: Many suns circle in desert space:
target_text: Many suns circle in desert space:

source_text: to all that is dark do they speak with their light -
target_text: to all that is dark do they speak with their light -

source_text: but to me they are silent.
target_text: but to me they are silent.

source_text: Oh, this is the hostility of light to the shining one:
target_text: Oh, this is the hostility of light to the shining one:

source_text: unpityingly doth it pursue its course.
target_text: unpityingly doth it pursue its course.

source_text: Unfair to the shining one in its innermost heart, cold to the suns: -
target_text: Unfair to the shining one in its innermost heart, cold to the suns: -

source_text: Like a storm do the suns pursue their courses:
target_text: Like a storm do the suns pursue their courses:

source_text: Their inexorable will do they follow: that is their coldness.
target_text: Their inexorable will do they follow: that is their coldness.

source_text: Oh, ye only is it, ye dark, nightly ones, that extract warmth from the shining ones!
target_text: Oh, ye only is it, ye dark, nightly ones, that extract warmth from the shining ones!

source_text: And thirst for the nightly!
target_text: And thirst for the nightly!

source_text: And lonesomeness!
target_text: And lonesomeness!

source_text: for speech do I long.

target_text: But Zarathustra also is a poet.

target_text: Believest thou that he there spake the truth?

source_text: Why dost thou believe it?
target_text: Why dost thou believe it?

source_text: The disciple answered:
target_text: The disciple answered:

target_text: I believe in Zarathustra.

source_text: But Zarathustra shook his head and smiled.
target_text: But Zarathustra shook his head and smiled.

source_text: Belief doth not sanctify me, said he, least of all the belief in myself.
target_text: Belief doth not sanctify me, said he, least of all the belief in myself.

source_text: he was right -
target_text: he was right -

source_text: WE do lie too much.
target_text: WE do lie too much.

source_text: We also know too little, and are bad learners:
target_text: We also know too little, and are bad learners:

source_text: so we are obliged to lie.
target_text: so we are obliged to lie.

source_text: And which of us poets hath not adulterated his wine?
target_text: And which of us poets hath not adulterated his wine?

source_text: many an indescribable thing hath there been done.
target_text: many an indescribable thing hath there been done.

source_text: And because we know little, therefore are we pleased from the heart with the poor in spirit, especially when they are young women!
target_text: And because we know little, therefore are we pleased from the heart with the poor in spirit, especially when they are young women!

source_text: And even of those things are we desirous, which old women tell one another in the evening.
target_text: And even of those things are we desirous, which old women tell one another in the evening.

source_text: This do we call the eternally feminine in us.
target_text: This do we call the eternally feminine in us.

source_text: This, however, do all poets believe:
target_text: This, however, do all poets believe:

source_text: that whoever pricketh up his ears when lying in the grass or on lonely slopes, learneth something of the things that are betwixt heaven and earth.
target_text: that whoever pricketh up his ears when lying in the grass or on lonely slopes, learneth something of the things that are betwixt heaven and earth.

source_text: And if there come unto them tender emotions, then do the poets always think that nature herself is in love with them:
target_text: And if there come unto them tender emotions, then do the poets always think that nature herself is in love with them:

source_text: And that she stealeth to their ear to whisper secrets into it, and amorous flatteries:
target_text: And that she stealeth to their ear to whisper secrets into it, and amorous flatteries:

source_text: of this do they plume and pride themselves, before all mortals!
target_text: of this do they plume and pride themselves, before all mortals!

source_text: And especially ABOVE the heavens:
target_text: And especially ABOVE the heavens:

source_text: Verily, ever are we drawn aloft -
target_text: Verily, ever are we drawn aloft -

source_text: that is, to the realm of the clouds:
target_text: that is, to the realm of the clouds:

target_text: on these do we set our gaudy puppets, and then call them Gods and Supermen:

target_text: Are not they light enough for those chairs!

source_text: all these Gods and Supermen?
target_text: all these Gods and Supermen?

source_text: Ah, how I am weary of the poets!
target_text: Ah, how I am weary of the poets!

source_text: When Zarathustra so spake, his disciple resented it, but was silent.
target_text: When Zarathustra so spake, his disciple resented it, but was silent.

source_text: and his eye directed itself inwardly, as if it gazed into the far distance.
target_text: and his eye directed itself inwardly, as if it gazed into the far distance.

source_text: At last he sighed and drew breath.
target_text: At last he sighed and drew breath.

source_text: but something is in me that is of the morrow, and the day following, and the hereafter.
target_text: but something is in me that is of the morrow, and the day following, and the hereafter.

source_text: I became weary of the poets, of the old and of the new:
target_text: I became weary of the poets, of the old and of the new:

source_text: superficial are they all unto me, and shallow seas.
target_text: superficial are they all unto me, and shallow seas.

source_text: They did not think sufficiently into the depth;
target_text: They did not think sufficiently into the depth;

source_text: therefore their feeling did not reach to the bottom.
target_text: therefore their feeling did not reach to the bottom.

source_text: Some sensation of voluptuousness and some sensation of tedium:
target_text: Some sensation of voluptuousness and some sensation of tedium:

source_text: these have as yet been their best contemplation.
target_text: these have as yet been their best contemplation.

source_text: Ghost-breathing and ghost-whisking, seemeth to me all the jingle-jangling of their harps;
target_text: Ghost-breathing and ghost-whisking, seemeth to me all the jingle-jangling of their harps;

source_text: They are also not pure enough for me:
target_text: They are also not pure enough for me:

source_text: they all muddle their water that it may seem deep.
target_text: they all muddle their water that it may seem deep.

source_text: And fain would they thereby prove themselves reconcilers:
target_text: And fain would they thereby prove themselves reconcilers:

source_text: Ah, I cast indeed my net into their sea, and meant to catch good fish;
target_text: Ah, I cast indeed my net into their sea, and meant to catch good fish;

source_text: but always did I draw up the head of some ancient God.
target_text: but always did I draw up the head of some ancient God.

source_text: Thus did the sea give a stone to the hungry one.
target_text: Thus did the sea give a stone to the hungry one.

source_text: And they themselves may well originate from the sea.
target_text: And they themselves may well originate from the sea.

source_text: Certainly, one findeth pearls in them:
target_text: Certainly, one findeth pearls in them:

source_text: And instead of a soul, I have often found in them salt slime.
target_text: And instead of a soul, I have often found in them salt slime.

source_text: They have learned from the sea also its vanity:
target_text: They have learned from the sea also its vanity:

source_text: is not the sea the peacock of peacocks?
target_text: is not the sea the peacock of peacocks?

source_text: never doth it tire of its lace-fan of silver and silk.
target_text: never doth it tire of its lace-fan of silver and silk.

source_text: Disdainfully doth the buffalo glance thereat, nigh to the sand with its soul, nigher still to the thicket, nighest, however, to the swamp.
target_text: Disdainfully doth the buffalo glance thereat, nigh to the sand with its soul, nigher still to the thicket, nighest, however, to the swamp.

source_text: This parable I speak unto the poets.
target_text: This parable I speak unto the poets.

source_text: Verily, their spirit itself is the peacock of peacocks, and a sea of vanity!
target_text: Verily, their spirit itself is the peacock of peacocks, and a sea of vanity!

source_text: Spectators, seeketh the spirit of the poet -
target_text: Spectators, seeketh the spirit of the poet -

source_text: But of this spirit became I weary;
target_text: But of this spirit became I weary;

source_text: and I see the time coming when it will become weary of itself.
target_text: and I see the time coming when it will become weary of itself.

source_text: they grew out of the poets.
target_text: they grew out of the poets.

target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

target_text: not far from the Happy Isles of Zarathustra -

source_text: on which a volcano ever smoketh;
target_text: on which a volcano ever smoketh;

target_text: It is the highest time!

target_text: said the old helmsman,

target_text: and when his friends were asked about it, they said that he had gone on board a ship by night, without saying whither he was going.

source_text: Thus there arose some uneasiness.
target_text: Thus there arose some uneasiness.

source_text: After three days, however, there came the story of the ship's crew in addition to this uneasiness -
target_text: After three days, however, there came the story of the ship's crew in addition to this uneasiness -

target_text: and then did all the people say that the devil had taken Zarathustra.

source_text: His disciples laughed, sure enough, at this talk;
target_text: His disciples laughed, sure enough, at this talk;

source_text: and one of them said even:
target_text: and one of them said even:

target_text: Sooner would I believe that Zarathustra hath taken the devil.

source_text: But at the bottom of their hearts they were all full of anxiety and longing:

target_text: so their joy was great when on the fifth day Zarathustra appeared amongst them.

target_text: And this is the account of Zarathustra's interview with the fire-dog:
