target_text: The earth, said he, hath a skin;

source_text: One of these diseases, for example, is called
target_text: One of these diseases, for example, is called

source_text: concerning HIM men have greatly deceived themselves, and let themselves be deceived.
target_text: concerning HIM men have greatly deceived themselves, and let themselves be deceived.

source_text: To fathom this mystery did I go o'er the sea;
target_text: To fathom this mystery did I go o'er the sea;

source_text: Now do I know how it is concerning the fire-dog;
target_text: Now do I know how it is concerning the fire-dog;

source_text: and likewise concerning all the spouting and subversive devils, of which not only old women are afraid.
target_text: and likewise concerning all the spouting and subversive devils, of which not only old women are afraid.

source_text: cried I,
target_text: cried I,

source_text: Whence cometh that which thou snortest up?
target_text: Whence cometh that which thou snortest up?

source_text: Thou drinkest copiously at the sea:
target_text: Thou drinkest copiously at the sea:

source_text: In sooth, for a dog of the depth, thou takest thy nourishment too much from the surface!
target_text: In sooth, for a dog of the depth, thou takest thy nourishment too much from the surface!

source_text: and ever, when I have heard subversive and spouting devils speak, I have found them like thee:
target_text: and ever, when I have heard subversive and spouting devils speak, I have found them like thee:

source_text: Ye understand how to roar and obscure with ashes!
target_text: Ye understand how to roar and obscure with ashes!

source_text: Where ye are, there must always be dregs at hand, and much that is spongy, hollow, and compressed:
target_text: Where ye are, there must always be dregs at hand, and much that is spongy, hollow, and compressed:

source_text: it wanteth to have freedom.
target_text: it wanteth to have freedom.

source_text: The greatest events - are not our noisiest, but our stillest hours.
target_text: The greatest events - are not our noisiest, but our stillest hours.

source_text: INAUDIBLY it revolveth.
target_text: INAUDIBLY it revolveth.

source_text: And just own to it!
target_text: And just own to it!

source_text: Little had ever taken place when thy noise and smoke passed away.
target_text: Little had ever taken place when thy noise and smoke passed away.

target_text: What, if a city did become a mummy, and a statue lay in the mud!

source_text: It is certainly the greatest folly to throw salt into the sea, and statues into the mud.
target_text: It is certainly the greatest folly to throw salt into the sea, and statues into the mud.

source_text: In the mud of your contempt lay the statue:
target_text: In the mud of your contempt lay the statue:

source_text: but it is just its law, that out of contempt, its life and living beauty grow again!
target_text: but it is just its law, that out of contempt, its life and living beauty grow again!

source_text: then did he interrupt me sullenly, and asked:
target_text: then did he interrupt me sullenly, and asked:

source_text: What is that?
target_text: What is that?

source_text: answered I,
target_text: answered I,

source_text: that is a kind of state, and indeed the most mendacious.
target_text: that is a kind of state, and indeed the most mendacious.

source_text: But remain quiet, thou dissembling dog!
target_text: But remain quiet, thou dissembling dog!

source_text: Thou surely knowest thine own species best!
target_text: Thou surely knowest thine own species best!

source_text: Like thyself the state is a dissembling dog;
target_text: Like thyself the state is a dissembling dog;

source_text: like thee doth it like to speak with smoke and roaring -
target_text: like thee doth it like to speak with smoke and roaring -

source_text: For it seeketh by all means to be the most important creature on earth, the state;
target_text: For it seeketh by all means to be the most important creature on earth, the state;

source_text: and people think it so.
target_text: and people think it so.

source_text: When I had said this, the fire-dog acted as if mad with envy.
target_text: When I had said this, the fire-dog acted as if mad with envy.

source_text: cried he,
target_text: cried he,

source_text: the most important creature on earth?
target_text: the most important creature on earth?

source_text: And people think it so?
target_text: And people think it so?

target_text: And so much vapour and terrible voices came out of his throat, that I thought he would choke with vexation and envy.

target_text: At last he became calmer and his panting subsided;

target_text: as soon, however, as he was quiet, I said laughingly:

target_text: Thou art angry, fire-dog: so I am in the right about thee!

target_text: And that I may also maintain the right, hear the story of another fire-dog;

target_text: he speaketh actually out of the heart of the earth.

target_text: The gold, however, and the laughter -

source_text: these doth he take out of the heart of the earth:
target_text: these doth he take out of the heart of the earth:

source_text: When the fire-dog heard this, he could no longer endure to listen to me.
target_text: When the fire-dog heard this, he could no longer endure to listen to me.

source_text: in a cowed voice, and crept down into his cave.
target_text: in a cowed voice, and crept down into his cave.

source_text: Thus told Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus told Zarathustra.

source_text: His disciples, however, hardly listened to him:
target_text: His disciples, however, hardly listened to him:

source_text: so great was their eagerness to tell him about the sailors, the rabbits, and the flying man.
target_text: so great was their eagerness to tell him about the sailors, the rabbits, and the flying man.

source_text: said Zarathustra.
target_text: said Zarathustra.

source_text: Am I indeed a ghost?
target_text: Am I indeed a ghost?

source_text: But it may have been my shadow.
target_text: But it may have been my shadow.

source_text: Ye have surely heard something of the Wanderer and his Shadow?
target_text: Ye have surely heard something of the Wanderer and his Shadow?

source_text: One thing, however, is certain: I must keep a tighter hold of it;
target_text: One thing, however, is certain: I must keep a tighter hold of it;

source_text: otherwise it will spoil my reputation.
target_text: otherwise it will spoil my reputation.

target_text: And once more Zarathustra shook his head and wondered.

source_text: "What am I to think of it!"
target_text: "What am I to think of it!"

target_text: said he once more.

target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: The best turned weary of their works.
target_text: The best turned weary of their works.

target_text: A doctrine appeared, a faith ran beside it:

target_text: but why have all our fruits become rotten and brown?

source_text: and fire falling upon us, then do we turn dust like ashes: -
target_text: and fire falling upon us, then do we turn dust like ashes: -

target_text: All our fountains have dried up, even the sea hath receded.

target_text: All the ground trieth to gape, but the depth will not swallow!

source_text: across shallow swamps.
target_text: across shallow swamps.

source_text: Verily, even for dying have we become too weary;
target_text: Verily, even for dying have we become too weary;

source_text: and the foreboding touched his heart and transformed him.
target_text: and the foreboding touched his heart and transformed him.

source_text: Sorrowfully did he go about and wearily;
target_text: Sorrowfully did he go about and wearily;

source_text: and he became like unto those of whom the soothsayer had spoken.
target_text: and he became like unto those of whom the soothsayer had spoken.

target_text: Verily, said he unto his disciples, a little while, and there cometh the long twilight.

source_text: Alas, how shall I preserve my light through it!
target_text: Alas, how shall I preserve my light through it!

source_text: That it may not smother in this sorrowfulness!
target_text: That it may not smother in this sorrowfulness!

source_text: Thus did Zarathustra go about grieved in his heart, and for three days he did not take any meat or drink:
target_text: Thus did Zarathustra go about grieved in his heart, and for three days he did not take any meat or drink:

target_text: he had no rest, and lost his speech.

source_text: At last it came to pass that he fell into a deep sleep.
target_text: At last it came to pass that he fell into a deep sleep.

source_text: His disciples, however, sat around him in long night-watches, and waited anxiously to see if he would awake, and speak again, and recover from his affliction.
target_text: His disciples, however, sat around him in long night-watches, and waited anxiously to see if he would awake, and speak again, and recover from his affliction.

source_text: And this is the discourse that Zarathustra spake when he awoke;
target_text: And this is the discourse that Zarathustra spake when he awoke;

source_text: his voice, however, came unto his disciples as from afar:
target_text: his voice, however, came unto his disciples as from afar:

source_text: A riddle is it still unto me, this dream;
target_text: A riddle is it still unto me, this dream;

source_text: All life had I renounced, so I dreamed.
target_text: All life had I renounced, so I dreamed.

source_text: Night-watchman and grave-guardian had I become, aloft, in the lone mountain-fortress of Death.
target_text: Night-watchman and grave-guardian had I become, aloft, in the lone mountain-fortress of Death.

source_text: There did I guard his coffins:
target_text: There did I guard his coffins:

source_text: full stood the musty vaults of those trophies of victory.
target_text: full stood the musty vaults of those trophies of victory.

source_text: The odour of dust-covered eternities did I breathe:
target_text: The odour of dust-covered eternities did I breathe:

source_text: sultry and dust-covered lay my soul.
target_text: sultry and dust-covered lay my soul.

source_text: And who could have aired his soul there!
target_text: And who could have aired his soul there!

source_text: Brightness of midnight was ever around me;
target_text: Brightness of midnight was ever around me;

source_text: Keys did I carry, the rustiest of all keys;
target_text: Keys did I carry, the rustiest of all keys;

source_text: and I knew how to open with them the most creaking of all gates.
target_text: and I knew how to open with them the most creaking of all gates.

target_text: Like a bitterly angry croaking ran the sound through the long corridors when the leaves of the gate opened:

target_text: ungraciously did this bird cry, unwillingly was it awakened.

source_text: But more frightful even, and more heart-strangling was it, when it again became silent and still all around, and I alone sat in that malignant silence.
target_text: But more frightful even, and more heart-strangling was it, when it again became silent and still all around, and I alone sat in that malignant silence.

target_text: Thus did time pass with me, and slip by, if time there still was:

target_text: what do I know thereof!

target_text: But not a finger's-breadth was it yet open:

target_text: Then did a roaring wind tear the folds apart:

target_text: And in the roaring, and whistling, and whizzing the coffin burst up, and spouted out a thousand peals of laughter.

target_text: And a thousand caricatures of children, angels, owls, fools, and child-sized butterflies laughed and mocked, and roared at me.

target_text: Fearfully was I terrified thereby: it prostrated me.

target_text: But mine own crying awoke me: - and I came to myself.

target_text: Thus did Zarathustra relate his dream, and then was silent:

target_text: Thy life itself interpreteth unto us this dream, O Zarathustra!

source_text: Art thou not thyself the coffin full of many-hued malices and angel-caricatures of life?
target_text: Art thou not thyself the coffin full of many-hued malices and angel-caricatures of life?

target_text: With thy laughter wilt thou frighten and prostrate them:

source_text: fainting and recovering will demonstrate thy power over them.
target_text: fainting and recovering will demonstrate thy power over them.

target_text: And when the long twilight cometh and the mortal weariness, even then wilt thou not disappear from our firmament, thou advocate of life!

source_text: New stars hast thou made us see, and new nocturnal glories:
target_text: New stars hast thou made us see, and new nocturnal glories:

target_text: verily, laughter itself hast thou spread out over us like a many-hued canopy.

target_text: Now will children's laughter ever from coffins flow;

target_text: of this thou art thyself the pledge and the prophet!

target_text: Verily, THEY THEMSELVES DIDST THOU DREAM, thine enemies:

source_text: and come unto thee!

target_text: Zarathustra, however, sat upright on his couch, with an absent look.

target_text: And I wept and trembled like a child, and said:

source_text: Ah, I would indeed, but how can I do it!
target_text: Ah, I would indeed, but how can I do it!

source_text: Exempt me only from this!
target_text: Exempt me only from this!

source_text: It is beyond my power!
target_text: It is beyond my power!

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: Ah, is it MY word?
target_text: Ah, is it MY word?

source_text: I await the worthier one; I am not worthy even to succumb by it.
target_text: I await the worthier one; I am not worthy even to succumb by it.

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: Humility hath the hardest skin.
target_text: Humility hath the hardest skin.

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: What hath not the skin of my humility endured!
target_text: What hath not the skin of my humility endured!

source_text: At the foot of my height do I dwell:
target_text: At the foot of my height do I dwell:

source_text: how high are my summits, no one hath yet told me.
target_text: how high are my summits, no one hath yet told me.

source_text: But well do I know my valleys.
target_text: But well do I know my valleys.

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: As yet hath my word not removed mountains, and what I have spoken hath not reached man.
target_text: As yet hath my word not removed mountains, and what I have spoken hath not reached man.

source_text: I went, indeed, unto men, but not yet have I attained unto them.
target_text: I went, indeed, unto men, but not yet have I attained unto them.

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: What knowest thou THEREOF!
target_text: What knowest thou THEREOF!

source_text: The dew falleth on the grass when the night is most silent.
target_text: The dew falleth on the grass when the night is most silent.

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: and certainly did my feet then tremble.
target_text: and certainly did my feet then tremble.

source_text: And thus did they speak unto me:
target_text: And thus did they speak unto me:

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: What matter about their mockery!
target_text: What matter about their mockery!

source_text: Thou art one who hast unlearned to obey: now shalt thou command!
target_text: Thou art one who hast unlearned to obey: now shalt thou command!

source_text: Knowest thou not who is most needed by all?
target_text: Knowest thou not who is most needed by all?

source_text: To execute great things is difficult:
target_text: To execute great things is difficult:

source_text: This is thy most unpardonable obstinacy:
target_text: This is thy most unpardonable obstinacy:

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: I lack the lion's voice for all commanding.
target_text: I lack the lion's voice for all commanding.

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me as a whispering:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me as a whispering:

source_text: It is the stillest words which bring the storm.
target_text: It is the stillest words which bring the storm.

source_text: O Zarathustra, thou shalt go as a shadow of that which is to come:
target_text: O Zarathustra, thou shalt go as a shadow of that which is to come:

source_text: thus wilt thou command, and in commanding go foremost.
target_text: thus wilt thou command, and in commanding go foremost.

source_text: And I answered:
target_text: And I answered:

source_text: I am ashamed.
target_text: I am ashamed.

source_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:
target_text: Then was there again spoken unto me without voice:

source_text: Thou must yet become a child, and be without shame.
target_text: Thou must yet become a child, and be without shame.

source_text: The pride of youth is still upon thee;
target_text: The pride of youth is still upon thee;

source_text: late hast thou become young:
target_text: late hast thou become young:

source_text: And I considered a long while, and trembled.
target_text: And I considered a long while, and trembled.

source_text: At last, however, did I say what I had said at first.
target_text: At last, however, did I say what I had said at first.

source_text: I will not.
target_text: I will not.

source_text: Then did a laughing take place all around me.
target_text: Then did a laughing take place all around me.

source_text: Alas, how that laughing lacerated my bowels and cut into my heart!
target_text: Alas, how that laughing lacerated my bowels and cut into my heart!

source_text: And there was spoken unto me for the last time:
target_text: And there was spoken unto me for the last time:

source_text: So must thou go again into solitude: for thou shalt yet become mellow.
target_text: So must thou go again into solitude: for thou shalt yet become mellow.

source_text: I lay, however, on the ground, and the sweat flowed from my limbs.
target_text: I lay, however, on the ground, and the sweat flowed from my limbs.

source_text: Now have ye heard all, and why I have to return into my solitude.
target_text: Now have ye heard all, and why I have to return into my solitude.

source_text: Nothing have I kept hidden from you, my friends.
target_text: Nothing have I kept hidden from you, my friends.

source_text: But even this have ye heard from me, WHO is still the most reserved of men -
target_text: But even this have ye heard from me, WHO is still the most reserved of men -

source_text: and will be so!
target_text: and will be so!

source_text: I should have something more to say unto you!
target_text: I should have something more to say unto you!

source_text: I should have something more to give unto you!
target_text: I should have something more to give unto you!

source_text: Why do I not give it?
target_text: Why do I not give it?

source_text: Am I then a niggard?
target_text: Am I then a niggard?

source_text: and no one knew how to console him.
target_text: and no one knew how to console him.

source_text: In the night, however, he went away alone and left his friends.
target_text: In the night, however, he went away alone and left his friends.

source_text: because there he meant to embark.
target_text: because there he meant to embark.

source_text: For there was a good roadstead there, in which foreign ships also liked to anchor:
target_text: For there was a good roadstead there, in which foreign ships also liked to anchor:

source_text: those ships took many people with them, who wished to cross over from the Happy Isles.
target_text: those ships took many people with them, who wished to cross over from the Happy Isles.

source_text: So when Zarathustra thus ascended the mountain, he thought on the way of his many solitary wanderings from youth onwards, and how many mountains and ridges and summits he had already climbed.
target_text: So when Zarathustra thus ascended the mountain, he thought on the way of his many solitary wanderings from youth onwards, and how many mountains and ridges and summits he had already climbed.

source_text: I am a wanderer and mountain-climber, said he to his heart, I love not the plains, and it seemeth I cannot long sit still.
target_text: I am a wanderer and mountain-climber, said he to his heart, I love not the plains, and it seemeth I cannot long sit still.

source_text: And whatever may still overtake me as fate and experience -
target_text: And whatever may still overtake me as fate and experience -

source_text: a wandering will be therein, and a mountain-climbing:
target_text: a wandering will be therein, and a mountain-climbing:

source_text: and what COULD now fall to my lot which would not already be mine own!
target_text: and what COULD now fall to my lot which would not already be mine own!

source_text: It returneth only, it cometh home to me at last -
target_text: It returneth only, it cometh home to me at last -

source_text: mine own Self, and such of it as hath been long abroad, and scattered among things and accidents.
target_text: mine own Self, and such of it as hath been long abroad, and scattered among things and accidents.

source_text: And one thing more do I know:
target_text: And one thing more do I know:

source_text: I stand now before my last summit, and before that which hath been longest reserved for me.
target_text: I stand now before my last summit, and before that which hath been longest reserved for me.

source_text: Ah, my hardest path must I ascend!
target_text: Ah, my hardest path must I ascend!

source_text: Ah, I have begun my lonesomest wandering!
target_text: Ah, I have begun my lonesomest wandering!

source_text: He, however, who is of my nature doth not avoid such an hour:
target_text: He, however, who is of my nature doth not avoid such an hour:

source_text: the hour that saith unto him:
target_text: the hour that saith unto him:

source_text: Now only dost thou go the way to thy greatness!
target_text: Now only dost thou go the way to thy greatness!

source_text: Summit and abyss - these are now comprised together!
target_text: Summit and abyss - these are now comprised together!

source_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:
target_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:

source_text: now hath it become thy last refuge, what was hitherto thy last danger!
target_text: now hath it become thy last refuge, what was hitherto thy last danger!

source_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:
target_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:

source_text: it must now be thy best courage that there is no longer any path behind thee!
target_text: it must now be thy best courage that there is no longer any path behind thee!

source_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:
target_text: Thou goest the way to thy greatness:

source_text: here shall no one steal after thee!
target_text: here shall no one steal after thee!

source_text: Impossibility.
target_text: Impossibility.

source_text: how couldst thou mount upward otherwise?
target_text: how couldst thou mount upward otherwise?

source_text: Upon thine own head, and beyond thine own heart!
target_text: Upon thine own head, and beyond thine own heart!

source_text: Now must the gentlest in thee become the hardest.
target_text: Now must the gentlest in thee become the hardest.

source_text: He who hath always much-indulged himself, sickeneth at last by his much-indulgence.
target_text: He who hath always much-indulged himself, sickeneth at last by his much-indulgence.

source_text: I do not praise the land where butter and honey - flow!
target_text: I do not praise the land where butter and honey - flow!

source_text: this hardiness is needed by every mountain-climber.
target_text: this hardiness is needed by every mountain-climber.

source_text: He, however, who is obtrusive with his eyes as a discerner, how can he ever see more of anything than its foreground!
target_text: He, however, who is obtrusive with his eyes as a discerner, how can he ever see more of anything than its foreground!

source_text: But thou, O Zarathustra, wouldst view the ground of everything, and its background:
target_text: But thou, O Zarathustra, wouldst view the ground of everything, and its background:

source_text: thus must thou mount even above thyself -
target_text: thus must thou mount even above thyself -

source_text: up, upwards, until thou hast even thy stars UNDER thee!
target_text: up, upwards, until thou hast even thy stars UNDER thee!

source_text: To look down upon myself, and even upon my stars:
target_text: To look down upon myself, and even upon my stars:

source_text: that only would I call my SUMMIT, that hath remained for me as my LAST summit!
target_text: that only would I call my SUMMIT, that hath remained for me as my LAST summit!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra to himself while ascending, comforting his heart with harsh maxims:
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra to himself while ascending, comforting his heart with harsh maxims:

source_text: for he was sore at heart as he had never been before.
target_text: for he was sore at heart as he had never been before.

source_text: And when he had reached the top of the mountain-ridge, behold, there lay the other sea spread out before him:
target_text: And when he had reached the top of the mountain-ridge, behold, there lay the other sea spread out before him:

source_text: and he stood still and was long silent.
target_text: and he stood still and was long silent.

source_text: The night, however, was cold at this height, and clear and starry.
target_text: The night, however, was cold at this height, and clear and starry.

source_text: Well!
target_text: Well!

source_text: Now hath my last lonesomeness begun.
target_text: Now hath my last lonesomeness begun.

source_text: Ah, this sombre, sad sea, below me!
target_text: Ah, this sombre, sad sea, below me!

source_text: Ah, this sombre nocturnal vexation!
target_text: Ah, this sombre nocturnal vexation!

source_text: To you must I now GO DOWN!
target_text: To you must I now GO DOWN!

source_text: Before my highest mountain do I stand, and before my longest wandering:
target_text: Before my highest mountain do I stand, and before my longest wandering:

source_text: So willeth my fate.
target_text: So willeth my fate.

source_text: Well!
target_text: Well!

source_text: I am ready.
target_text: I am ready.

source_text: Whence come the highest mountains?
target_text: Whence come the highest mountains?

source_text: so did I once ask.
target_text: so did I once ask.

source_text: Then did I learn that they come out of the sea.
target_text: Then did I learn that they come out of the sea.

source_text: That testimony is inscribed on their stones, and on the walls of their summits.
target_text: That testimony is inscribed on their stones, and on the walls of their summits.

source_text: Out of the deepest must the highest come to its height.
target_text: Out of the deepest must the highest come to its height.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra on the ridge of the mountain where it was cold:
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra on the ridge of the mountain where it was cold:

source_text: when, however, he came into the vicinity of the sea, and at last stood alone amongst the cliffs, then had he become weary on his way, and eagerer than ever before.
target_text: when, however, he came into the vicinity of the sea, and at last stood alone amongst the cliffs, then had he become weary on his way, and eagerer than ever before.

source_text: Everything as yet sleepeth, said he; even the sea sleepeth.
target_text: Everything as yet sleepeth, said he; even the sea sleepeth.

source_text: But it breatheth warmly - I feel it.
target_text: But it breatheth warmly - I feel it.

source_text: And I feel also that it dreameth.
target_text: And I feel also that it dreameth.

source_text: It tosseth about dreamily on hard pillows.
target_text: It tosseth about dreamily on hard pillows.

source_text: Or evil expectations?
target_text: Or evil expectations?

source_text: Ah, I am sad along with thee, thou dusky monster, and angry with myself even for thy sake.
target_text: Ah, I am sad along with thee, thou dusky monster, and angry with myself even for thy sake.

source_text: Ah, that my hand hath not strength enough!
target_text: Ah, that my hand hath not strength enough!

source_text: Gladly, indeed, would I free thee from evil dreams!
target_text: Gladly, indeed, would I free thee from evil dreams!

source_text: And while Zarathustra thus spake, he laughed at himself with melancholy and bitterness.
target_text: And while Zarathustra thus spake, he laughed at himself with melancholy and bitterness.

source_text: What!
target_text: What!

source_text: Zarathustra, said he, wilt thou even sing consolation to the sea?
target_text: Zarathustra, said he, wilt thou even sing consolation to the sea?

source_text: Ah, thou amiable fool, Zarathustra, thou too-blindly confiding one!
target_text: Ah, thou amiable fool, Zarathustra, thou too-blindly confiding one!

source_text: But thus hast thou ever been:
target_text: But thus hast thou ever been:

source_text: ever hast thou approached confidently all that is terrible.
target_text: ever hast thou approached confidently all that is terrible.

source_text: Every monster wouldst thou caress.
target_text: Every monster wouldst thou caress.

source_text: and immediately wert thou ready to love and lure it.
target_text: and immediately wert thou ready to love and lure it.

source_text: LOVE is the danger of the lonesomest one, love to anything, IF IT ONLY LIVE!
target_text: LOVE is the danger of the lonesomest one, love to anything, IF IT ONLY LIVE!

source_text: Laughable, verily, is my folly and my modesty in love!
target_text: Laughable, verily, is my folly and my modesty in love!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and laughed thereby a second time.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and laughed thereby a second time.

source_text: Then, however, he thought of his abandoned friends -
target_text: Then, however, he thought of his abandoned friends -

source_text: and as if he had done them a wrong with his thoughts, he upbraided himself because of his thoughts.
target_text: and as if he had done them a wrong with his thoughts, he upbraided himself because of his thoughts.

source_text: with anger and longing wept Zarathustra bitterly.
target_text: with anger and longing wept Zarathustra bitterly.

source_text: When it got abroad among the sailors that Zarathustra was on board the ship -
target_text: When it got abroad among the sailors that Zarathustra was on board the ship -

source_text: for a man who came from the Happy Isles had gone on board along with him, -
target_text: for a man who came from the Happy Isles had gone on board along with him, -

source_text: there was great curiosity and expectation.
target_text: there was great curiosity and expectation.

source_text: But Zarathustra kept silent for two days, and was cold and deaf with sadness;
target_text: But Zarathustra kept silent for two days, and was cold and deaf with sadness;

source_text: so that he neither answered looks nor questions.
target_text: so that he neither answered looks nor questions.

source_text: On the evening of the second day, however, he again opened his ears, though he still kept silent:
target_text: On the evening of the second day, however, he again opened his ears, though he still kept silent:

source_text: for there were many curious and dangerous things to be heard on board the ship, which came from afar, and was to go still further.
target_text: for there were many curious and dangerous things to be heard on board the ship, which came from afar, and was to go still further.

source_text: Zarathustra, however, was fond of all those who make distant voyages, and dislike to live without danger.
target_text: Zarathustra, however, was fond of all those who make distant voyages, and dislike to live without danger.

source_text: And behold!
target_text: And behold!

source_text: when listening, his own tongue was at last loosened, and the ice of his heart broke.
target_text: when listening, his own tongue was at last loosened, and the ice of his heart broke.

source_text: Then did he begin to speak thus:
target_text: Then did he begin to speak thus:

source_text: To you, the daring venturers and adventurers, and whoever hath embarked with cunning sails upon frightful seas, -
target_text: To you, the daring venturers and adventurers, and whoever hath embarked with cunning sails upon frightful seas, -

source_text: For ye dislike to grope at a thread with cowardly hand;
target_text: For ye dislike to grope at a thread with cowardly hand;

source_text: To you only do I tell the enigma that I SAW -
target_text: To you only do I tell the enigma that I SAW -

source_text: the vision of the lonesomest one.
target_text: the vision of the lonesomest one.

source_text: gloomily and sternly, with compressed lips.
target_text: gloomily and sternly, with compressed lips.

source_text: Mutely marching over the scornful clinking of pebbles, trampling the stone that let it slip:
target_text: Mutely marching over the scornful clinking of pebbles, trampling the stone that let it slip:

source_text: thus did my foot force its way upwards.
target_text: thus did my foot force its way upwards.

source_text: Upwards: - although it sat upon me, half-dwarf, half-mole;
target_text: Upwards: - although it sat upon me, half-dwarf, half-mole;

source_text: dripping lead in mine ear, and thoughts like drops of lead into my brain.
target_text: dripping lead in mine ear, and thoughts like drops of lead into my brain.

source_text: it whispered scornfully, syllable by syllable,
target_text: it whispered scornfully, syllable by syllable,

source_text: thou stone of wisdom!
target_text: thou stone of wisdom!

source_text: Condemned of thyself, and to thine own stoning:
target_text: Condemned of thyself, and to thine own stoning:

source_text: but upon THYSELF will it recoil!
target_text: but upon THYSELF will it recoil!

source_text: Then was the dwarf silent; and it lasted long.
target_text: Then was the dwarf silent; and it lasted long.

source_text: The silence, however, oppressed me;
target_text: The silence, however, oppressed me;

source_text: and to be thus in pairs, one is verily lonesomer than when alone!
target_text: and to be thus in pairs, one is verily lonesomer than when alone!

source_text: I ascended, I ascended, I dreamt, I thought, -
target_text: I ascended, I ascended, I dreamt, I thought, -

source_text: but everything oppressed me.
target_text: but everything oppressed me.

source_text: A sick one did I resemble, whom bad torture wearieth, and a worse dream reawakeneth out of his first sleep.
target_text: A sick one did I resemble, whom bad torture wearieth, and a worse dream reawakeneth out of his first sleep.

source_text: But there is something in me which I call courage:
target_text: But there is something in me which I call courage:

source_text: it hath hitherto slain for me every dejection.
target_text: it hath hitherto slain for me every dejection.

source_text: This courage at last bade me stand still and say:
target_text: This courage at last bade me stand still and say:

source_text: Or I!
target_text: Or I!

source_text: For courage is the best slayer, -
target_text: For courage is the best slayer, -

source_text: courage which ATTACKETH: for in every attack there is sound of triumph.
target_text: courage which ATTACKETH: for in every attack there is sound of triumph.

source_text: Man, however, is the most courageous animal:
target_text: Man, however, is the most courageous animal:

source_text: thereby hath he overcome every animal.
target_text: thereby hath he overcome every animal.

source_text: With sound of triumph hath he overcome every pain;
target_text: With sound of triumph hath he overcome every pain;

source_text: human pain, however, is the sorest pain.
target_text: human pain, however, is the sorest pain.

source_text: Courage slayeth also giddiness at abysses:
target_text: Courage slayeth also giddiness at abysses:

source_text: and where doth man not stand at abysses!
target_text: and where doth man not stand at abysses!

source_text: Is not seeing itself - seeing abysses?
target_text: Is not seeing itself - seeing abysses?

source_text: Courage is the best slayer: courage slayeth also fellow-suffering.
target_text: Courage is the best slayer: courage slayeth also fellow-suffering.

source_text: Fellow-suffering, however, is the deepest abyss:
target_text: Fellow-suffering, however, is the deepest abyss:

source_text: as deeply as man looketh into life, so deeply also doth he look into suffering.
target_text: as deeply as man looketh into life, so deeply also doth he look into suffering.

source_text: Courage, however, is the best slayer, courage which attacketh:
target_text: Courage, however, is the best slayer, courage which attacketh:

source_text: it slayeth even death itself;
target_text: it slayeth even death itself;

source_text: for it saith:
target_text: for it saith:

source_text: WAS THAT life?
target_text: WAS THAT life?

source_text: Well!
target_text: Well!

source_text: In such speech, however, there is much sound of triumph.
target_text: In such speech, however, there is much sound of triumph.

source_text: "Halt, dwarf!"
target_text: "Halt, dwarf!"

source_text: said I.
target_text: said I.

source_text: Either I - or thou!
target_text: Either I - or thou!

source_text: I, however, am the stronger of the two: -
target_text: I, however, am the stronger of the two: -

source_text: IT - couldst thou not endure!
target_text: IT - couldst thou not endure!

source_text: Then happened that which made me lighter:
target_text: Then happened that which made me lighter:

source_text: for the dwarf sprang from my shoulder, the prying sprite!
target_text: for the dwarf sprang from my shoulder, the prying sprite!

source_text: And it squatted on a stone in front of me.
target_text: And it squatted on a stone in front of me.

source_text: There was however a gateway just where we halted.
target_text: There was however a gateway just where we halted.

source_text: Look at this gateway!
target_text: Look at this gateway!

source_text: I continued,
target_text: I continued,

source_text: it hath two faces.
target_text: it hath two faces.

source_text: Two roads come together here: these hath no one yet gone to the end of.
target_text: Two roads come together here: these hath no one yet gone to the end of.

source_text: This long lane backwards: it continueth for an eternity.
target_text: This long lane backwards: it continueth for an eternity.

source_text: And that long lane forward - that is another eternity.
target_text: And that long lane forward - that is another eternity.

source_text: They are antithetical to one another, these roads;
target_text: They are antithetical to one another, these roads;

source_text: they directly abut on one another: -
target_text: they directly abut on one another: -

source_text: and it is here, at this gateway, that they come together.
target_text: and it is here, at this gateway, that they come together.

source_text: and ever further and further on, thinkest thou, dwarf, that these roads would be eternally antithetical?
target_text: and ever further and further on, thinkest thou, dwarf, that these roads would be eternally antithetical?

source_text: "Everything straight lieth,"
target_text: "Everything straight lieth,"

source_text: murmured the dwarf, contemptuously.
target_text: murmured the dwarf, contemptuously.

source_text: All truth is crooked; time itself is a circle.
target_text: All truth is crooked; time itself is a circle.

source_text: "Thou spirit of gravity!"
target_text: "Thou spirit of gravity!"

source_text: said I wrathfully,
target_text: said I wrathfully,

source_text: do not take it too lightly!
target_text: do not take it too lightly!

source_text: and I carried thee HIGH!
target_text: and I carried thee HIGH!

source_text: continued I,
target_text: continued I,

source_text: This Moment!
target_text: This Moment!

source_text: behind us lieth an eternity.
target_text: behind us lieth an eternity.

source_text: Must not whatever CAN run its course of all things, have already run along that lane?
target_text: Must not whatever CAN run its course of all things, have already run along that lane?

source_text: Must not whatever CAN happen of all things have already happened, resulted, and gone by?
target_text: Must not whatever CAN happen of all things have already happened, resulted, and gone by?

source_text: And if everything have already existed, what thinkest thou, dwarf, of This Moment?
target_text: And if everything have already existed, what thinkest thou, dwarf, of This Moment?

source_text: Must not this gateway also - have already existed?
target_text: Must not this gateway also - have already existed?

source_text: And are not all things closely bound together in such wise that This Moment draweth all coming things after it?
target_text: And are not all things closely bound together in such wise that This Moment draweth all coming things after it?

source_text: CONSEQUENTLY - itself also?
target_text: CONSEQUENTLY - itself also?

source_text: For whatever CAN run its course of all things, also in this long lane OUTWARD -
target_text: For whatever CAN run its course of all things, also in this long lane OUTWARD -

source_text: MUST it once more run!
target_text: MUST it once more run!

source_text: And this slow spider which creepeth in the moonlight, and this moonlight itself, and thou and I in this gateway whispering together, whispering of eternal things -
target_text: And this slow spider which creepeth in the moonlight, and this moonlight itself, and thou and I in this gateway whispering together, whispering of eternal things -

source_text: must we not all have already existed?
target_text: must we not all have already existed?

source_text: And must we not return and run in that other lane out before us, that long weird lane -
target_text: And must we not return and run in that other lane out before us, that long weird lane -

source_text: must we not eternally return?
target_text: must we not eternally return?

source_text: Thus did I speak, and always more softly:
target_text: Thus did I speak, and always more softly:

source_text: Then, suddenly did I hear a dog HOWL near me.
target_text: Then, suddenly did I hear a dog HOWL near me.

source_text: Had I ever heard a dog howl thus?
target_text: Had I ever heard a dog howl thus?

source_text: My thoughts ran back.
target_text: My thoughts ran back.

source_text: Yes!
target_text: Yes!

source_text: When I was a child, in my most distant childhood: -
target_text: When I was a child, in my most distant childhood: -

source_text: Then did I hear a dog howl thus.
target_text: Then did I hear a dog howl thus.

source_text: And saw it also, with hair bristling, its head upwards, trembling in the stillest midnight, when even dogs believe in ghosts:
target_text: And saw it also, with hair bristling, its head upwards, trembling in the stillest midnight, when even dogs believe in ghosts:

source_text: So that it excited my commiseration.
target_text: So that it excited my commiseration.

source_text: For just then went the full moon, silent as death, over the house;
target_text: For just then went the full moon, silent as death, over the house;

source_text: just then did it stand still, a glowing globe -
target_text: just then did it stand still, a glowing globe -

source_text: at rest on the flat roof, as if on some one's property: -
target_text: at rest on the flat roof, as if on some one's property: -

source_text: Thereby had the dog been terrified:
target_text: Thereby had the dog been terrified:

source_text: for dogs believe in thieves and ghosts.
target_text: for dogs believe in thieves and ghosts.

source_text: And when I again heard such howling, then did it excite my commiseration once more.
target_text: And when I again heard such howling, then did it excite my commiseration once more.

source_text: Where was now the dwarf?
target_text: Where was now the dwarf?

source_text: And the gateway?
target_text: And the gateway?

source_text: And the spider?
target_text: And the spider?

source_text: And all the whispering?
target_text: And all the whispering?

source_text: Had I awakened?
target_text: Had I awakened?

source_text: And there!
target_text: And there!

source_text: The dog leaping, bristling, whining -
target_text: The dog leaping, bristling, whining -

source_text: now did it see me coming -
target_text: now did it see me coming -

source_text: then did it howl again, then did it CRY: -
target_text: then did it howl again, then did it CRY: -

source_text: had I ever heard a dog cry so for help?
target_text: had I ever heard a dog cry so for help?

source_text: And verily, what I saw, the like had I never seen.
target_text: And verily, what I saw, the like had I never seen.

source_text: A young shepherd did I see, writhing, choking, quivering, with distorted countenance, and with a heavy black serpent hanging out of his mouth.
target_text: A young shepherd did I see, writhing, choking, quivering, with distorted countenance, and with a heavy black serpent hanging out of his mouth.

source_text: Had I ever seen so much loathing and pale horror on one countenance?
target_text: Had I ever seen so much loathing and pale horror on one countenance?

source_text: He had perhaps gone to sleep?
target_text: He had perhaps gone to sleep?

source_text: Then had the serpent crawled into his throat -
target_text: Then had the serpent crawled into his throat -

source_text: there had it bitten itself fast.
target_text: there had it bitten itself fast.

source_text: I failed to pull the serpent out of his throat.
target_text: I failed to pull the serpent out of his throat.

source_text: Then there cried out of me:
target_text: Then there cried out of me:

source_text: Ye daring ones around me!
target_text: Ye daring ones around me!

source_text: Ye enigma-enjoyers!
target_text: Ye enigma-enjoyers!

source_text: Solve unto me the enigma that I then beheld, interpret unto me the vision of the lonesomest one!
target_text: Solve unto me the enigma that I then beheld, interpret unto me the vision of the lonesomest one!

source_text: For it was a vision and a foresight: -
target_text: For it was a vision and a foresight: -

source_text: And WHO is it that must come some day?
target_text: And WHO is it that must come some day?

source_text: WHO is the shepherd into whose throat the serpent thus crawled?
target_text: WHO is the shepherd into whose throat the serpent thus crawled?

source_text: WHO is the man into whose throat all the heaviest and blackest will thus crawl?
target_text: WHO is the man into whose throat all the heaviest and blackest will thus crawl?

source_text: The shepherd however bit as my cry had admonished him;
target_text: The shepherd however bit as my cry had admonished him;

source_text: he bit with a strong bite!
target_text: he bit with a strong bite!

source_text: Far away did he spit the head of the serpent - : and sprang up.
target_text: Far away did he spit the head of the serpent - : and sprang up.

source_text: No longer shepherd, no longer man -
target_text: No longer shepherd, no longer man -

source_text: a transfigured being, a light-surrounded being, that LAUGHED!
target_text: a transfigured being, a light-surrounded being, that LAUGHED!

source_text: oh, how can I still endure to live!
target_text: oh, how can I still endure to live!

source_text: And how could I endure to die at present!
target_text: And how could I endure to die at present!

source_text: When, however, he was four day-journeys from the Happy Isles and from his friends, then had he surmounted all his pain -
target_text: When, however, he was four day-journeys from the Happy Isles and from his friends, then had he surmounted all his pain -

source_text: triumphantly and with firm foot did he again accept his fate.
target_text: triumphantly and with firm foot did he again accept his fate.

source_text: And then talked Zarathustra in this wise to his exulting conscience:
target_text: And then talked Zarathustra in this wise to his exulting conscience:

source_text: Alone am I again, and like to be so, alone with the pure heaven, and the open sea;
target_text: Alone am I again, and like to be so, alone with the pure heaven, and the open sea;

source_text: and again is the afternoon around me.
target_text: and again is the afternoon around me.

source_text: On an afternoon did I find my friends for the first time;
target_text: On an afternoon did I find my friends for the first time;

source_text: on an afternoon, also, did I find them a second time: -
target_text: on an afternoon, also, did I find them a second time: -

source_text: at the hour when all light becometh stiller.
target_text: at the hour when all light becometh stiller.

source_text: WITH HAPPINESS hath all light now become stiller.
target_text: WITH HAPPINESS hath all light now become stiller.

source_text: O afternoon of my life!
target_text: O afternoon of my life!

source_text: Once did my happiness also descend to the valley that it might seek a lodging:
target_text: Once did my happiness also descend to the valley that it might seek a lodging:

source_text: then did it find those open hospitable souls.
target_text: then did it find those open hospitable souls.

source_text: What did I not surrender that I might have one thing:
target_text: What did I not surrender that I might have one thing:

source_text: this living plantation of my thoughts, and this dawn of my highest hope!
target_text: this living plantation of my thoughts, and this dawn of my highest hope!

source_text: Companions did the creating one once seek, and children of HIS hope:
target_text: Companions did the creating one once seek, and children of HIS hope:

source_text: Thus am I in the midst of my work, to my children going, and from them returning:
target_text: Thus am I in the midst of my work, to my children going, and from them returning:

source_text: for the sake of his children must Zarathustra perfect himself.
target_text: for the sake of his children must Zarathustra perfect himself.

source_text: For in one's heart one loveth only one's child and one's work;
target_text: For in one's heart one loveth only one's child and one's work;

source_text: so have I found it.
target_text: so have I found it.

source_text: Still are my children verdant in their first spring, standing nigh one another, and shaken in common by the winds, the trees of my garden and of my best soil.
target_text: Still are my children verdant in their first spring, standing nigh one another, and shaken in common by the winds, the trees of my garden and of my best soil.

source_text: And verily, where such trees stand beside one another, there ARE Happy Isles!
target_text: And verily, where such trees stand beside one another, there ARE Happy Isles!

source_text: But one day will I take them up, and put each by itself alone:
target_text: But one day will I take them up, and put each by itself alone:

source_text: that it may learn lonesomeness and defiance and prudence.
target_text: that it may learn lonesomeness and defiance and prudence.

source_text: Gnarled and crooked and with flexible hardness shall it then stand by the sea, a living lighthouse of unconquerable life.
target_text: Gnarled and crooked and with flexible hardness shall it then stand by the sea, a living lighthouse of unconquerable life.

source_text: Yonder where the storms rush down into the sea, and the snout of the mountain drinketh water, shall each on a time have his day and night watches, for HIS testing and recognition.
target_text: Yonder where the storms rush down into the sea, and the snout of the mountain drinketh water, shall each on a time have his day and night watches, for HIS testing and recognition.

source_text: So that he may one day become my companion, a fellow-creator and fellow-enjoyer with Zarathustra:
target_text: So that he may one day become my companion, a fellow-creator and fellow-enjoyer with Zarathustra:

source_text: And for his sake and for those like him, must I perfect MYSELF:
target_text: And for his sake and for those like him, must I perfect MYSELF:

source_text: therefore do I now avoid my happiness, and present myself to every misfortune -
target_text: therefore do I now avoid my happiness, and present myself to every misfortune -

source_text: for MY final testing and recognition.
target_text: for MY final testing and recognition.

source_text: And verily, it were time that I went away;
target_text: And verily, it were time that I went away;

source_text: have all said unto me:
target_text: have all said unto me:

source_text: "It is the highest time!"
target_text: "It is the highest time!"

source_text: The word blew to me through the keyhole and said
target_text: The word blew to me through the keyhole and said

source_text: "Go!"
target_text: "Go!"

source_text: desire spread this snare for me -
target_text: desire spread this snare for me -

source_text: the desire for love -
target_text: the desire for love -

source_text: that I should become the prey of my children, and lose myself in them.
target_text: that I should become the prey of my children, and lose myself in them.

source_text: Desiring - that is now for me to have lost myself.
target_text: Desiring - that is now for me to have lost myself.

source_text: In this possessing shall everything be assurance and nothing desire.
target_text: In this possessing shall everything be assurance and nothing desire.

source_text: then did shadows and doubts fly past me.
target_text: then did shadows and doubts fly past me.

source_text: For frost and winter I now longed:
target_text: For frost and winter I now longed:

source_text: "Oh, that frost and winter would again make me crack and crunch!"
target_text: "Oh, that frost and winter would again make me crack and crunch!"

source_text: My past burst its tomb, many pains buried alive woke up -
target_text: My past burst its tomb, many pains buried alive woke up -

source_text: fully slept had they merely, concealed in corpse-clothes.
target_text: fully slept had they merely, concealed in corpse-clothes.

source_text: So called everything unto me in signs:
target_text: So called everything unto me in signs:

source_text: heard not, until at last mine abyss moved, and my thought bit me.
target_text: heard not, until at last mine abyss moved, and my thought bit me.

source_text: Ah, abysmal thought, which art MY thought!
target_text: Ah, abysmal thought, which art MY thought!

source_text: When shall I find strength to hear thee burrowing, and no longer tremble?
target_text: When shall I find strength to hear thee burrowing, and no longer tremble?

source_text: As yet have I never ventured to call thee UP;
target_text: As yet have I never ventured to call thee UP;

source_text: it hath been enough that I - have carried thee about with me!
target_text: it hath been enough that I - have carried thee about with me!

source_text: As yet have I not been strong enough for my final lion-wantonness and playfulness.
target_text: As yet have I not been strong enough for my final lion-wantonness and playfulness.

source_text: Sufficiently formidable unto me hath thy weight ever been:
target_text: Sufficiently formidable unto me hath thy weight ever been:

source_text: but one day shall I yet find the strength and the lion's voice which will call thee up!
target_text: but one day shall I yet find the strength and the lion's voice which will call thee up!

source_text: When I shall have surmounted myself therein, then will I surmount myself also in that which is greater;
target_text: When I shall have surmounted myself therein, then will I surmount myself also in that which is greater;

source_text: and a VICTORY shall be the seal of my perfection!
target_text: and a VICTORY shall be the seal of my perfection!

source_text: Meanwhile do I sail along on uncertain seas;
target_text: Meanwhile do I sail along on uncertain seas;

source_text: chance flattereth me, smooth-tongued chance;
target_text: chance flattereth me, smooth-tongued chance;

source_text: forward and backward do I gaze - , still see I no end.
target_text: forward and backward do I gaze - , still see I no end.

source_text: As yet hath the hour of my final struggle not come to me -
target_text: As yet hath the hour of my final struggle not come to me -

source_text: or doth it come to me perhaps just now?
target_text: or doth it come to me perhaps just now?

source_text: Verily, with insidious beauty do sea and life gaze upon me round about:
target_text: Verily, with insidious beauty do sea and life gaze upon me round about:

source_text: O afternoon of my life!
target_text: O afternoon of my life!

source_text: O happiness before eventide!
target_text: O happiness before eventide!

source_text: O haven upon high seas!
target_text: O haven upon high seas!

source_text: O peace in uncertainty!
target_text: O peace in uncertainty!

source_text: How I distrust all of you!
target_text: How I distrust all of you!

source_text: Verily, distrustful am I of your insidious beauty!
target_text: Verily, distrustful am I of your insidious beauty!

source_text: Like the lover am I, who distrusteth too sleek smiling.
target_text: Like the lover am I, who distrusteth too sleek smiling.

source_text: tender even in severity, the jealous one -
target_text: tender even in severity, the jealous one -

source_text: so do I push this blissful hour before me.
target_text: so do I push this blissful hour before me.

source_text: Away with thee, thou blissful hour!
target_text: Away with thee, thou blissful hour!

source_text: With thee hath there come to me an involuntary bliss!
target_text: With thee hath there come to me an involuntary bliss!

source_text: Ready for my severest pain do I here stand: -
target_text: Ready for my severest pain do I here stand: -

source_text: at the wrong time hast thou come!
target_text: at the wrong time hast thou come!

source_text: Away with thee, thou blissful hour!
target_text: Away with thee, thou blissful hour!

source_text: Rather harbour there - with my children!
target_text: Rather harbour there - with my children!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: And he waited for his misfortune the whole night;
target_text: And he waited for his misfortune the whole night;

source_text: but he waited in vain.
target_text: but he waited in vain.

source_text: The night remained clear and calm, and happiness itself came nigher and nigher unto him.
target_text: The night remained clear and calm, and happiness itself came nigher and nigher unto him.

source_text: Happiness runneth after me.
target_text: Happiness runneth after me.

source_text: That is because I do not run after women.
target_text: That is because I do not run after women.

source_text: Happiness, however, is a woman.
target_text: Happiness, however, is a woman.

source_text: O heaven above me, thou pure, thou deep heaven!
target_text: O heaven above me, thou pure, thou deep heaven!

source_text: Gazing on thee, I tremble with divine desires.
target_text: Gazing on thee, I tremble with divine desires.

source_text: Up to thy height to toss myself - that is MY depth!
target_text: Up to thy height to toss myself - that is MY depth!

source_text: In thy purity to hide myself - that is MINE innocence!
target_text: In thy purity to hide myself - that is MINE innocence!

source_text: The God veileth his beauty: thus hidest thou thy stars.
target_text: The God veileth his beauty: thus hidest thou thy stars.

source_text: Thou speakest not: THUS proclaimest thou thy wisdom unto me.
target_text: Thou speakest not: THUS proclaimest thou thy wisdom unto me.

source_text: Mute o'er the raging sea hast thou risen for me to-day;
target_text: Mute o'er the raging sea hast thou risen for me to-day;

source_text: thy love and thy modesty make a revelation unto my raging soul.
target_text: thy love and thy modesty make a revelation unto my raging soul.

source_text: BEFORE the sun didst thou come unto me - the lonesomest one.
target_text: BEFORE the sun didst thou come unto me - the lonesomest one.

source_text: We have been friends from the beginning:
target_text: We have been friends from the beginning:

source_text: to us are grief, gruesomeness, and ground common;
target_text: to us are grief, gruesomeness, and ground common;

source_text: even the sun is common to us.
target_text: even the sun is common to us.

source_text: We do not speak to each other, because we know too much -
target_text: We do not speak to each other, because we know too much -

source_text: we keep silent to each other, we smile our knowledge to each other.
target_text: we keep silent to each other, we smile our knowledge to each other.

source_text: Art thou not the light of my fire?
target_text: Art thou not the light of my fire?

source_text: Hast thou not the sister-soul of mine insight?
target_text: Hast thou not the sister-soul of mine insight?

source_text: Together did we learn everything;
target_text: Together did we learn everything;

source_text: together did we learn to ascend beyond ourselves to ourselves, and to smile uncloudedly:
target_text: together did we learn to ascend beyond ourselves to ourselves, and to smile uncloudedly:

source_text: Uncloudedly to smile down out of luminous eyes and out of miles of distance, when under us constraint and purpose and guilt steam like rain.
target_text: Uncloudedly to smile down out of luminous eyes and out of miles of distance, when under us constraint and purpose and guilt steam like rain.

source_text: And all my wandering and mountain-climbing:
target_text: And all my wandering and mountain-climbing:

source_text: a necessity was it merely, and a makeshift of the unhandy one:
target_text: a necessity was it merely, and a makeshift of the unhandy one:

source_text: to FLY only, wanteth mine entire will, to fly into THEE!
target_text: to FLY only, wanteth mine entire will, to fly into THEE!

source_text: And what have I hated more than passing clouds, and whatever tainteth thee?
target_text: And what have I hated more than passing clouds, and whatever tainteth thee?

source_text: And mine own hatred have I even hated, because it tainted thee!
target_text: And mine own hatred have I even hated, because it tainted thee!

source_text: those stealthy cats of prey:
target_text: those stealthy cats of prey:

source_text: they take from thee and me what is common to us -
target_text: they take from thee and me what is common to us -

source_text: These mediators and mixers we detest -
target_text: These mediators and mixers we detest -

source_text: the passing clouds:
target_text: the passing clouds:

source_text: those half-and-half ones, that have neither learned to bless nor to curse from the heart.
target_text: those half-and-half ones, that have neither learned to bless nor to curse from the heart.

source_text: thou heaven above me, thou pure, thou luminous heaven!
target_text: thou heaven above me, thou pure, thou luminous heaven!

source_text: because they rob thee of MY Yea and Amen.
target_text: because they rob thee of MY Yea and Amen.

source_text: "he who cannot bless shall LEARN to curse!"
target_text: "he who cannot bless shall LEARN to curse!"

source_text: into all abysses do I then carry my beneficent Yea-saying.
target_text: into all abysses do I then carry my beneficent Yea-saying.

source_text: This, however, is my blessing:
target_text: This, however, is my blessing:

source_text: and blessed is he who thus blesseth!
target_text: and blessed is he who thus blesseth!

source_text: For all things are baptized at the font of eternity, and beyond good and evil;
target_text: For all things are baptized at the font of eternity, and beyond good and evil;

source_text: good and evil themselves, however, are but fugitive shadows and damp afflictions and passing clouds.
target_text: good and evil themselves, however, are but fugitive shadows and damp afflictions and passing clouds.

source_text: Verily, it is a blessing and not a blasphemy when I teach that
target_text: Verily, it is a blessing and not a blasphemy when I teach that

source_text: above all things there standeth the heaven of chance, the heaven of innocence, the heaven of hazard, the heaven of wantonness.
target_text: above all things there standeth the heaven of chance, the heaven of innocence, the heaven of hazard, the heaven of wantonness.

source_text: that is the oldest nobility in the world;
target_text: that is the oldest nobility in the world;

source_text: that gave I back to all things;
target_text: that gave I back to all things;

source_text: I emancipated them from bondage under purpose.
target_text: I emancipated them from bondage under purpose.

source_text: This freedom and celestial serenity did I put like an azure bell above all things, when I taught that over them and through them, no
target_text: This freedom and celestial serenity did I put like an azure bell above all things, when I taught that over them and through them, no

source_text: "eternal Will"
target_text: "eternal Will"

source_text: This wantonness and folly did I put in place of that Will, when I taught that
target_text: This wantonness and folly did I put in place of that Will, when I taught that

source_text: "In everything there is one thing impossible - rationality!"
target_text: "In everything there is one thing impossible - rationality!"

source_text: A LITTLE reason, to be sure, a germ of wisdom scattered from star to star -
target_text: A LITTLE reason, to be sure, a germ of wisdom scattered from star to star -

source_text: this leaven is mixed in all things:
target_text: this leaven is mixed in all things:

source_text: for the sake of folly, wisdom is mixed in all things!
target_text: for the sake of folly, wisdom is mixed in all things!

source_text: A little wisdom is indeed possible;
target_text: A little wisdom is indeed possible;

source_text: but this blessed security have I found in all things, that they prefer -
target_text: but this blessed security have I found in all things, that they prefer -

source_text: to DANCE on the feet of chance.
target_text: to DANCE on the feet of chance.

source_text: thou pure, thou lofty heaven!
target_text: thou pure, thou lofty heaven!

source_text: This is now thy purity unto me, that there is no eternal reason-spider and reason-cobweb:
target_text: This is now thy purity unto me, that there is no eternal reason-spider and reason-cobweb:

source_text: That thou art to me a dancing-floor for divine chances, that thou art to me a table of the Gods, for divine dice and dice-players!
target_text: That thou art to me a dancing-floor for divine chances, that thou art to me a table of the Gods, for divine dice and dice-players!

source_text: But thou blushest?
target_text: But thou blushest?

source_text: Have I spoken unspeakable things?
target_text: Have I spoken unspeakable things?

source_text: Have I abused, when I meant to bless thee?
target_text: Have I abused, when I meant to bless thee?

source_text: Or is it the shame of being two of us that maketh thee blush!
target_text: Or is it the shame of being two of us that maketh thee blush!

source_text: Dost thou bid me go and be silent, because now - DAY cometh?
target_text: Dost thou bid me go and be silent, because now - DAY cometh?

source_text: The world is deep: - and deeper than e'er the day could read.
target_text: The world is deep: - and deeper than e'er the day could read.

source_text: Not everything may be uttered in presence of day.
target_text: Not everything may be uttered in presence of day.

source_text: But day cometh: so let us part!
target_text: But day cometh: so let us part!

source_text: The day cometh: so let us part!
target_text: The day cometh: so let us part!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: so that he said of himself jestingly:
target_text: so that he said of himself jestingly:

source_text: "Lo, a river that floweth back unto its source in many windings!"
target_text: "Lo, a river that floweth back unto its source in many windings!"

source_text: For he wanted to learn what had taken place AMONG MEN during the interval:
target_text: For he wanted to learn what had taken place AMONG MEN during the interval:

source_text: whether they had become greater or smaller.
target_text: whether they had become greater or smaller.

source_text: And once, when he saw a row of new houses, he marvelled, and said:
target_text: And once, when he saw a row of new houses, he marvelled, and said:

source_text: What do these houses mean?
target_text: What do these houses mean?

source_text: Verily, no great soul put them up as its simile!
target_text: Verily, no great soul put them up as its simile!

source_text: Did perhaps a silly child take them out of its toy-box?
target_text: Did perhaps a silly child take them out of its toy-box?

target_text: And these rooms and chambers - can MEN go out and in there?

target_text: And Zarathustra stood still and meditated.

source_text: At last he said sorrowfully:
target_text: At last he said sorrowfully:

source_text: he must stoop!
target_text: he must stoop!

source_text: Oh, when shall I arrive again at my home, where I shall no longer have to stoop -
target_text: Oh, when shall I arrive again at my home, where I shall no longer have to stoop -

target_text: And Zarathustra sighed, and gazed into the distance.

target_text: The same day, however, he gave his discourse on the bedwarfing virtue.

source_text: I pass through this people and keep mine eyes open:
target_text: I pass through this people and keep mine eyes open:

source_text: they do not forgive me for not envying their virtues.
target_text: they do not forgive me for not envying their virtues.

source_text: They bite at me, because I say unto them that for small people, small virtues are necessary -
target_text: They bite at me, because I say unto them that for small people, small virtues are necessary -

source_text: and because it is hard for me to understand that small people are NECESSARY!
target_text: and because it is hard for me to understand that small people are NECESSARY!

source_text: Here am I still like a cock in a strange farm-yard, at which even the hens peck:
target_text: Here am I still like a cock in a strange farm-yard, at which even the hens peck:

source_text: but on that account I am not unfriendly to the hens.
target_text: but on that account I am not unfriendly to the hens.

source_text: They all speak of me when they sit around their fire in the evening -
target_text: They all speak of me when they sit around their fire in the evening -

source_text: they speak of me, but no one thinketh -
target_text: they speak of me, but no one thinketh -

source_text: This is the new stillness which I have experienced:
target_text: This is the new stillness which I have experienced:

source_text: their noise around me spreadeth a mantle over my thoughts.
target_text: their noise around me spreadeth a mantle over my thoughts.

source_text: They shout to one another:
target_text: They shout to one another:

source_text: What is this gloomy cloud about to do to us?
target_text: What is this gloomy cloud about to do to us?

source_text: Let us see that it doth not bring a plague upon us!
target_text: Let us see that it doth not bring a plague upon us!

source_text: And recently did a woman seize upon her child that was coming unto me:
target_text: And recently did a woman seize upon her child that was coming unto me:

source_text: "Take the children away,"
target_text: "Take the children away,"

source_text: cried she,
target_text: cried she,

source_text: such eyes scorch children's souls.
target_text: such eyes scorch children's souls.

source_text: They cough when I speak:
target_text: They cough when I speak:

source_text: they divine nothing of the boisterousness of my happiness!
target_text: they divine nothing of the boisterousness of my happiness!

source_text: "We have not yet time for Zarathustra"
target_text: "We have not yet time for Zarathustra"
