target_text: so they object; but what matter about a time that

source_text: "hath no time"
target_text: "hath no time"

source_text: for Zarathustra?
target_text: for Zarathustra?

source_text: And if they should altogether praise me, how could I go to sleep on THEIR praise?
target_text: And if they should altogether praise me, how could I go to sleep on THEIR praise?

source_text: A girdle of spines is their praise unto me:
target_text: A girdle of spines is their praise unto me:

source_text: it scratcheth me even when I take it off.
target_text: it scratcheth me even when I take it off.

source_text: And this also did I learn among them:
target_text: And this also did I learn among them:

source_text: the praiser doeth as if he gave back;
target_text: the praiser doeth as if he gave back;

source_text: I pass through this people and keep mine eyes open;
target_text: I pass through this people and keep mine eyes open;

source_text: they have become SMALLER, and ever become smaller: -
target_text: they have become SMALLER, and ever become smaller: -

source_text: THE REASON THEREOF IS THEIR DOCTRINE OF HAPPINESS AND VIRTUE. For they are moderate also in virtue, -
target_text: THE REASON THEREOF IS THEIR DOCTRINE OF HAPPINESS AND VIRTUE. For they are moderate also in virtue, -

source_text: because they want comfort.
target_text: because they want comfort.

source_text: With comfort, however, moderate virtue only is compatible.
target_text: With comfort, however, moderate virtue only is compatible.

source_text: To be sure, they also learn in their way to stride on and stride forward:
target_text: To be sure, they also learn in their way to stride on and stride forward:

source_text: that, I call their HOBBLING. -
target_text: that, I call their HOBBLING. -

source_text: Thereby they become a hindrance to all who are in haste.
target_text: Thereby they become a hindrance to all who are in haste.

source_text: And many of them go forward, and look backwards thereby, with stiffened necks:
target_text: And many of them go forward, and look backwards thereby, with stiffened necks:

source_text: those do I like to run up against.
target_text: those do I like to run up against.

source_text: But there is much lying among small people.
target_text: But there is much lying among small people.

source_text: Some of them WILL, but most of them are WILLED. Some of them are genuine, but most of them are bad actors.
target_text: Some of them WILL, but most of them are WILLED. Some of them are genuine, but most of them are bad actors.

source_text: There are actors without knowing it amongst them, and actors without intending it -
target_text: There are actors without knowing it amongst them, and actors without intending it -

source_text: the genuine ones are always rare, especially the genuine actors.
target_text: the genuine ones are always rare, especially the genuine actors.

source_text: Of man there is little here:
target_text: Of man there is little here:

source_text: For only he who is man enough, will - SAVE THE WOMAN in woman.
target_text: For only he who is man enough, will - SAVE THE WOMAN in woman.

source_text: And this hypocrisy found I worst amongst them, that even those who command feign the virtues of those who serve.
target_text: And this hypocrisy found I worst amongst them, that even those who command feign the virtues of those who serve.

source_text: so chanteth here even the hypocrisy of the rulers - and alas!
target_text: so chanteth here even the hypocrisy of the rulers - and alas!

source_text: if the first lord be ONLY the first servant!
target_text: if the first lord be ONLY the first servant!

source_text: and well did I divine all their fly-happiness, and their buzzing around sunny window-panes.
target_text: and well did I divine all their fly-happiness, and their buzzing around sunny window-panes.

source_text: So much kindness, so much weakness do I see.
target_text: So much kindness, so much weakness do I see.

source_text: So much justice and pity, so much weakness.
target_text: So much justice and pity, so much weakness.

source_text: Modestly to embrace a small happiness - that do they call
target_text: Modestly to embrace a small happiness - that do they call

source_text: and at the same time they peer modestly after a new small happiness.
target_text: and at the same time they peer modestly after a new small happiness.

source_text: In their hearts they want simply one thing most of all:
target_text: In their hearts they want simply one thing most of all:

source_text: that no one hurt them.
target_text: that no one hurt them.

source_text: Thus do they anticipate every one's wishes and do well unto every one.
target_text: Thus do they anticipate every one's wishes and do well unto every one.

source_text: That, however, is COWARDICE, though it be called
target_text: That, however, is COWARDICE, though it be called

source_text: And when they chance to speak harshly, those small people, then do I hear therein only their hoarseness -
target_text: And when they chance to speak harshly, those small people, then do I hear therein only their hoarseness -

source_text: every draught of air maketh them hoarse.
target_text: every draught of air maketh them hoarse.

source_text: Shrewd indeed are they, their virtues have shrewd fingers.
target_text: Shrewd indeed are they, their virtues have shrewd fingers.

source_text: But they lack fists:
target_text: But they lack fists:

source_text: their fingers do not know how to creep behind fists.
target_text: their fingers do not know how to creep behind fists.

source_text: "We set our chair in the MIDST"
target_text: "We set our chair in the MIDST"

source_text: and as far from dying gladiators as from satisfied swine.
target_text: and as far from dying gladiators as from satisfied swine.

source_text: That, however, is - MEDIOCRITY, though it be called moderation.
target_text: That, however, is - MEDIOCRITY, though it be called moderation.

source_text: but they know neither how to take nor how to retain them.
target_text: but they know neither how to take nor how to retain them.

source_text: and verily, I came not to warn against pickpockets either!
target_text: and verily, I came not to warn against pickpockets either!

source_text: And when I call out:
target_text: And when I call out:

source_text: then do they shout:
target_text: then do they shout:

source_text: Zarathustra is godless.
target_text: Zarathustra is godless.

source_text: And especially do their teachers of submission shout this;
target_text: And especially do their teachers of submission shout this;

source_text: but precisely in their ears do I love to cry:
target_text: but precisely in their ears do I love to cry:

source_text: I AM Zarathustra, the godless!
target_text: I AM Zarathustra, the godless!

source_text: Those teachers of submission!
target_text: Those teachers of submission!

source_text: and only my disgust preventeth me from cracking them.
target_text: and only my disgust preventeth me from cracking them.

source_text: Well!
target_text: Well!

source_text: This is my sermon for THEIR ears:
target_text: This is my sermon for THEIR ears:

source_text: I am Zarathustra the godless, who saith:
target_text: I am Zarathustra the godless, who saith:

source_text: "Who is more godless than I, that I may enjoy his teaching?"
target_text: "Who is more godless than I, that I may enjoy his teaching?"

source_text: I am Zarathustra the godless: where do I find mine equal?
target_text: I am Zarathustra the godless: where do I find mine equal?

source_text: And all those are mine equals who give unto themselves their Will, and divest themselves of all submission.
target_text: And all those are mine equals who give unto themselves their Will, and divest themselves of all submission.

source_text: I am Zarathustra the godless!
target_text: I am Zarathustra the godless!

source_text: I cook every chance in MY pot.
target_text: I cook every chance in MY pot.

source_text: And only when it hath been quite cooked do I welcome it as MY food.
target_text: And only when it hath been quite cooked do I welcome it as MY food.

source_text: And verily, many a chance came imperiously unto me:
target_text: And verily, many a chance came imperiously unto me:

source_text: but still more imperiously did my WILL speak unto it, -
target_text: but still more imperiously did my WILL speak unto it, -

source_text: then did it lie imploringly upon its knees -
target_text: then did it lie imploringly upon its knees -

source_text: Imploring that it might find home and heart with me, and saying flatteringly:
target_text: Imploring that it might find home and heart with me, and saying flatteringly:

source_text: Ye will yet perish -
target_text: Ye will yet perish -

source_text: By your many small virtues, by your many small omissions, and by your many small submissions!
target_text: By your many small virtues, by your many small omissions, and by your many small submissions!

source_text: But for a tree to become GREAT, it seeketh to twine hard roots around hard rocks!
target_text: But for a tree to become GREAT, it seeketh to twine hard roots around hard rocks!

source_text: Also what ye omit weaveth at the web of all the human future;
target_text: Also what ye omit weaveth at the web of all the human future;

source_text: And when ye take, then is it like stealing, ye small virtuous ones;
target_text: And when ye take, then is it like stealing, ye small virtuous ones;

source_text: but even among knaves HONOUR saith that
target_text: but even among knaves HONOUR saith that

source_text: one shall only steal when one cannot rob.
target_text: one shall only steal when one cannot rob.

source_text: that is also a doctrine of submission.
target_text: that is also a doctrine of submission.

source_text: But I say unto you, ye comfortable ones, that IT TAKETH TO ITSELF, and will ever take more and more from you!
target_text: But I say unto you, ye comfortable ones, that IT TAKETH TO ITSELF, and will ever take more and more from you!

source_text: Such as love with great love, such as love with great contempt!
target_text: Such as love with great love, such as love with great contempt!

source_text: Thus speaketh Zarathustra the godless.
target_text: Thus speaketh Zarathustra the godless.

source_text: But why talk I, when no one hath MINE ears!
target_text: But why talk I, when no one hath MINE ears!

source_text: It is still an hour too early for me here.
target_text: It is still an hour too early for me here.

source_text: And there cometh also mine!
target_text: And there cometh also mine!

source_text: poor earth!
target_text: poor earth!

source_text: And SOON shall they stand before me like dry grass and prairie, and verily, weary of themselves -
target_text: And SOON shall they stand before me like dry grass and prairie, and verily, weary of themselves -

source_text: and panting for FIRE, more than for water!
target_text: and panting for FIRE, more than for water!

source_text: O blessed hour of the lightning!
target_text: O blessed hour of the lightning!

source_text: O mystery before noontide!
target_text: O mystery before noontide!

source_text: Running fires will I one day make of them, and heralds with flaming tongues:
target_text: Running fires will I one day make of them, and heralds with flaming tongues:

source_text: Herald shall they one day with flaming tongues:
target_text: Herald shall they one day with flaming tongues:

source_text: It cometh, it is nigh, THE GREAT NOONTIDE!
target_text: It cometh, it is nigh, THE GREAT NOONTIDE!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: Winter, a bad guest, sitteth with me at home;
target_text: Winter, a bad guest, sitteth with me at home;

source_text: I honour him, that bad guest, but gladly leave him alone.
target_text: I honour him, that bad guest, but gladly leave him alone.

source_text: Gladly do I run away from him;
target_text: Gladly do I run away from him;

source_text: and when one runneth WELL, then one escapeth him!
target_text: and when one runneth WELL, then one escapeth him!

source_text: With warm feet and warm thoughts do I run where the wind is calm -
target_text: With warm feet and warm thoughts do I run where the wind is calm -

source_text: to the sunny corner of mine olive-mount.
target_text: to the sunny corner of mine olive-mount.

source_text: There do I laugh at my stern guest, and am still fond of him;
target_text: There do I laugh at my stern guest, and am still fond of him;

source_text: because he cleareth my house of flies, and quieteth many little noises.
target_text: because he cleareth my house of flies, and quieteth many little noises.

source_text: For he suffereth it not if a gnat wanteth to buzz, or even two of them;
target_text: For he suffereth it not if a gnat wanteth to buzz, or even two of them;

source_text: also the lanes maketh he lonesome, so that the moonlight is afraid there at night.
target_text: also the lanes maketh he lonesome, so that the moonlight is afraid there at night.

source_text: A hard guest is he, -
target_text: A hard guest is he, -

source_text: but I honour him, and do not worship, like the tenderlings, the pot-bellied fire-idol.
target_text: but I honour him, and do not worship, like the tenderlings, the pot-bellied fire-idol.

source_text: so willeth my nature.
target_text: so willeth my nature.

source_text: And especially have I a grudge against all ardent, steaming, steamy fire-idols.
target_text: And especially have I a grudge against all ardent, steaming, steamy fire-idols.

source_text: Him whom I love, I love better in winter than in summer;
target_text: Him whom I love, I love better in winter than in summer;

source_text: better do I now mock at mine enemies, and more heartily, when winter sitteth in my house.
target_text: better do I now mock at mine enemies, and more heartily, when winter sitteth in my house.

source_text: Heartily, verily, even when I CREEP into bed -
target_text: Heartily, verily, even when I CREEP into bed -

source_text: I, a - creeper?
target_text: I, a - creeper?

source_text: and if ever I lied, then did I lie out of love.
target_text: and if ever I lied, then did I lie out of love.

source_text: Therefore am I glad even in my winter-bed.
target_text: Therefore am I glad even in my winter-bed.

source_text: And in winter she is most faithful unto me.
target_text: And in winter she is most faithful unto me.

source_text: With a wickedness do I begin every day:
target_text: With a wickedness do I begin every day:

source_text: I mock at the winter with a cold bath:
target_text: I mock at the winter with a cold bath:

source_text: For especially wicked am I in the morning:
target_text: For especially wicked am I in the morning:

source_text: Impatiently do I then wait, that the clear sky may finally dawn for me, the snow-bearded winter-sky, the hoary one, the white-head, -
target_text: Impatiently do I then wait, that the clear sky may finally dawn for me, the snow-bearded winter-sky, the hoary one, the white-head, -

source_text: The winter-sky, the silent winter-sky, which often stifleth even its sun!
target_text: The winter-sky, the silent winter-sky, which often stifleth even its sun!

source_text: Did I perhaps learn from it the long clear silence?
target_text: Did I perhaps learn from it the long clear silence?

source_text: Or did it learn it from me?
target_text: Or did it learn it from me?

source_text: Or hath each of us devised it himself?
target_text: Or hath each of us devised it himself?

source_text: Of all good things the origin is a thousandfold, -
target_text: Of all good things the origin is a thousandfold, -

source_text: how could they always do so -
target_text: how could they always do so -

source_text: for once only!
target_text: for once only!

source_text: A good roguish thing is also the long silence, and to look, like the winter-sky, out of a clear, round-eyed countenance:
target_text: A good roguish thing is also the long silence, and to look, like the winter-sky, out of a clear, round-eyed countenance:

source_text: verily, this art and this winter-roguishness have I learnt WELL!
target_text: verily, this art and this winter-roguishness have I learnt WELL!

source_text: My best-loved wickedness and art is it, that my silence hath learned not to betray itself by silence.
target_text: My best-loved wickedness and art is it, that my silence hath learned not to betray itself by silence.

source_text: all those stern watchers, shall my will and purpose elude.
target_text: all those stern watchers, shall my will and purpose elude.

source_text: That no one might see down into my depth and into mine ultimate will -
target_text: That no one might see down into my depth and into mine ultimate will -

source_text: for that purpose did I devise the long clear silence.
target_text: for that purpose did I devise the long clear silence.

source_text: Many a shrewd one did I find:
target_text: Many a shrewd one did I find:

source_text: precisely from him did they fish his best-concealed fish!
target_text: precisely from him did they fish his best-concealed fish!

source_text: But the clear, the honest, the transparent -
target_text: But the clear, the honest, the transparent -

source_text: these are for me the wisest silent ones:
target_text: these are for me the wisest silent ones:

source_text: in them, so PROFOUND is the depth that even the clearest water doth not -
target_text: in them, so PROFOUND is the depth that even the clearest water doth not -

source_text: betray it.
target_text: betray it.

source_text: And MUST I not conceal myself like one who hath swallowed gold -
target_text: And MUST I not conceal myself like one who hath swallowed gold -

source_text: lest my soul should be ripped up?
target_text: lest my soul should be ripped up?

source_text: MUST I not wear stilts, that they may OVERLOOK my long legs -
target_text: MUST I not wear stilts, that they may OVERLOOK my long legs -

source_text: all those enviers and injurers around me?
target_text: all those enviers and injurers around me?

source_text: how COULD their envy endure my happiness!
target_text: how COULD their envy endure my happiness!

source_text: Thus do I show them only the ice and winter of my peaks -
target_text: Thus do I show them only the ice and winter of my peaks -

source_text: and NOT that my mountain windeth all the solar girdles around it!
target_text: and NOT that my mountain windeth all the solar girdles around it!

source_text: They hear only the whistling of my winter-storms:
target_text: They hear only the whistling of my winter-storms:

source_text: and know NOT that I also travel over warm seas, like longing, heavy, hot south-winds.
target_text: and know NOT that I also travel over warm seas, like longing, heavy, hot south-winds.

source_text: They commiserate also my accidents and chances: - but MY word saith:
target_text: They commiserate also my accidents and chances: - but MY word saith:

source_text: "Suffer the chance to come unto me: innocent is it as a little child!"
target_text: "Suffer the chance to come unto me: innocent is it as a little child!"

source_text: If I did not myself sigh before them, and chatter with cold, and patiently LET myself be swathed in their pity!
target_text: If I did not myself sigh before them, and chatter with cold, and patiently LET myself be swathed in their pity!

source_text: This is the wise waggish-will and good-will of my soul, that it CONCEALETH NOT its winters and glacial storms;
target_text: This is the wise waggish-will and good-will of my soul, that it CONCEALETH NOT its winters and glacial storms;

source_text: To one man, lonesomeness is the flight of the sick one;
target_text: To one man, lonesomeness is the flight of the sick one;

source_text: to another, it is the flight FROM the sick ones.
target_text: to another, it is the flight FROM the sick ones.

source_text: With such sighing and chattering do I flee from their heated rooms.
target_text: With such sighing and chattering do I flee from their heated rooms.

source_text: "At the ice of knowledge will he yet FREEZE TO DEATH!"
target_text: "At the ice of knowledge will he yet FREEZE TO DEATH!"

source_text: so they mourn.
target_text: so they mourn.

source_text: Meanwhile do I run with warm feet hither and thither on mine olive-mount:
target_text: Meanwhile do I run with warm feet hither and thither on mine olive-mount:

source_text: in the sunny corner of mine olive-mount do I sing, and mock at all pity.
target_text: in the sunny corner of mine olive-mount do I sing, and mock at all pity.

source_text: And behold, thereby came he unawares also to the gate of the GREAT CITY. Here, however, a foaming fool, with extended hands, sprang forward to him and stood in his way.
target_text: And behold, thereby came he unawares also to the gate of the GREAT CITY. Here, however, a foaming fool, with extended hands, sprang forward to him and stood in his way.

target_text: It was the same fool whom the people called

source_text: "the ape of Zarathustra:"
target_text: "the ape of Zarathustra:"

target_text: for he had learned from him something of the expression and modulation of language, and perhaps liked also to borrow from the store of his wisdom.

target_text: And the fool talked thus to Zarathustra:

target_text: here hast thou nothing to seek and everything to lose.

source_text: Why wouldst thou wade through this mire?
target_text: Why wouldst thou wade through this mire?

source_text: Have pity upon thy foot!
target_text: Have pity upon thy foot!

source_text: Spit rather on the gate of the city, and - turn back!
target_text: Spit rather on the gate of the city, and - turn back!

source_text: Here do all great sentiments decay:
target_text: Here do all great sentiments decay:

source_text: And they make newspapers also out of these rags!
target_text: And they make newspapers also out of these rags!

source_text: Hearest thou not how spirit hath here become a verbal game?
target_text: Hearest thou not how spirit hath here become a verbal game?

source_text: Loathsome verbal swill doth it vomit forth!
target_text: Loathsome verbal swill doth it vomit forth!

source_text: And they make newspapers also out of this verbal swill.
target_text: And they make newspapers also out of this verbal swill.

source_text: They hound one another, and know not whither!
target_text: They hound one another, and know not whither!

source_text: They inflame one another, and know not why!
target_text: They inflame one another, and know not why!

source_text: They are cold, and seek warmth from distilled waters:
target_text: They are cold, and seek warmth from distilled waters:

source_text: they are inflamed, and seek coolness from frozen spirits;
target_text: they are inflamed, and seek coolness from frozen spirits;

source_text: they are all sick and sore through public opinion.
target_text: they are all sick and sore through public opinion.

source_text: All lusts and vices are here at home;
target_text: All lusts and vices are here at home;

source_text: but here there are also the virtuous;
target_text: but here there are also the virtuous;

source_text: Much appointable virtue with scribe-fingers, and hardy sitting-flesh and waiting-flesh, blessed with small breast-stars, and padded, haunchless daughters.
target_text: Much appointable virtue with scribe-fingers, and hardy sitting-flesh and waiting-flesh, blessed with small breast-stars, and padded, haunchless daughters.

source_text: "From on high,"
target_text: "From on high,"

source_text: for the high, longeth every starless bosom.
target_text: for the high, longeth every starless bosom.

target_text: How from a deep breast this stillness fetcheth pure breath!

target_text: there speaketh everything, there is everything misheard.

target_text: no one knoweth any longer how to understand.

target_text: Freed at last is my nose from the smell of all human hubbub!

source_text: beyond the world;

source_text: O mine animals, answered Zarathustra, talk on thus and let me listen!
target_text: O mine animals, answered Zarathustra, talk on thus and let me listen!

source_text: It refresheth me so to hear your talk:
target_text: It refresheth me so to hear your talk:

source_text: where there is talk, there is the world as a garden unto me.
target_text: where there is talk, there is the world as a garden unto me.

source_text: How charming it is that there are words and tones;
target_text: How charming it is that there are words and tones;

source_text: To each soul belongeth another world;
target_text: To each soul belongeth another world;

source_text: Among the most alike doth semblance deceive most delightfully:
target_text: Among the most alike doth semblance deceive most delightfully:

source_text: for the smallest gap is most difficult to bridge over.
target_text: for the smallest gap is most difficult to bridge over.

source_text: For me - how could there be an outside-of-me?
target_text: For me - how could there be an outside-of-me?

source_text: There is no outside!
target_text: There is no outside!

source_text: But this we forget on hearing tones;
target_text: But this we forget on hearing tones;

source_text: how delightful it is that we forget!
target_text: how delightful it is that we forget!

source_text: Have not names and tones been given unto things that man may refresh himself with them?
target_text: Have not names and tones been given unto things that man may refresh himself with them?

source_text: It is a beautiful folly, speaking;
target_text: It is a beautiful folly, speaking;

source_text: therewith danceth man over everything.
target_text: therewith danceth man over everything.

source_text: How lovely is all speech and all falsehoods of tones!
target_text: How lovely is all speech and all falsehoods of tones!

source_text: With tones danceth our love on variegated rainbows.
target_text: With tones danceth our love on variegated rainbows.

source_text: to those who think like us, things all dance themselves:
target_text: to those who think like us, things all dance themselves:

source_text: they come and hold out the hand and laugh and flee -
target_text: they come and hold out the hand and laugh and flee -

source_text: and return.
target_text: and return.

source_text: Everything goeth, everything returneth;
target_text: Everything goeth, everything returneth;

source_text: eternally rolleth the wheel of existence.
target_text: eternally rolleth the wheel of existence.

source_text: Everything dieth, everything blossometh forth again;
target_text: Everything dieth, everything blossometh forth again;

source_text: eternally buildeth itself the same house of existence.
target_text: eternally buildeth itself the same house of existence.

source_text: eternally true to itself remaineth the ring of existence.
target_text: eternally true to itself remaineth the ring of existence.

source_text: Crooked is the path of eternity.
target_text: Crooked is the path of eternity.

source_text: answered Zarathustra, and smiled once more, how well do ye know what had to be fulfilled in seven days:
target_text: answered Zarathustra, and smiled once more, how well do ye know what had to be fulfilled in seven days:

source_text: And how that monster crept into my throat and choked me!
target_text: And how that monster crept into my throat and choked me!

source_text: But I bit off its head and spat it away from me.
target_text: But I bit off its head and spat it away from me.

source_text: Now, however, do I lie here, still exhausted with that biting and spitting-away, still sick with mine own salvation.
target_text: Now, however, do I lie here, still exhausted with that biting and spitting-away, still sick with mine own salvation.

source_text: Did ye like to look at my great pain as men do?
target_text: Did ye like to look at my great pain as men do?

source_text: For man is the cruellest animal.
target_text: For man is the cruellest animal.

source_text: and when he invented his hell, behold, that was his heaven on earth.
target_text: and when he invented his hell, behold, that was his heaven on earth.

source_text: When the great man crieth -
target_text: When the great man crieth -

source_text: He, however, calleth it his
target_text: He, however, calleth it his

source_text: The little man, especially the poet -
target_text: The little man, especially the poet -

source_text: Hearken to him, but do not fail to hear the delight which is in all accusation!
target_text: Hearken to him, but do not fail to hear the delight which is in all accusation!

source_text: Such accusers of life - them life overcometh with a glance of the eye.
target_text: Such accusers of life - them life overcometh with a glance of the eye.

source_text: "Thou lovest me?"
target_text: "Thou lovest me?"

source_text: saith the insolent one;
target_text: saith the insolent one;

source_text: and in all who call themselves
target_text: and in all who call themselves

source_text: do not overlook the voluptuousness in their plaints and accusations!
target_text: do not overlook the voluptuousness in their plaints and accusations!

source_text: And I myself - do I thereby want to be man's accuser?
target_text: And I myself - do I thereby want to be man's accuser?

source_text: Not to THIS torture-stake was I tied, that I know man is bad, -
target_text: Not to THIS torture-stake was I tied, that I know man is bad, -

source_text: but I cried, as no one hath yet cried:
target_text: but I cried, as no one hath yet cried:

source_text: Ah, that his best is so very small!
target_text: Ah, that his best is so very small!

source_text: The great disgust at man -
target_text: The great disgust at man -

source_text: IT strangled me and had crept into my throat:
target_text: IT strangled me and had crept into my throat:

source_text: All is alike, nothing is worth while, knowledge strangleth.
target_text: All is alike, nothing is worth while, knowledge strangleth.

source_text: A long twilight limped on before me, a fatally weary, fatally intoxicated sadness, which spake with yawning mouth.
target_text: A long twilight limped on before me, a fatally weary, fatally intoxicated sadness, which spake with yawning mouth.

source_text: "Eternally he returneth, the man of whom thou art weary, the small man"
target_text: "Eternally he returneth, the man of whom thou art weary, the small man"

source_text: so yawned my sadness, and dragged its foot and could not go to sleep.
target_text: so yawned my sadness, and dragged its foot and could not go to sleep.

source_text: A cavern, became the human earth to me;
target_text: A cavern, became the human earth to me;

source_text: its breast caved in;
target_text: its breast caved in;

source_text: everything living became to me human dust and bones and mouldering past.
target_text: everything living became to me human dust and bones and mouldering past.

source_text: my sighing and questioning croaked and choked, and gnawed and nagged day and night:
target_text: my sighing and questioning croaked and choked, and gnawed and nagged day and night:

source_text: Ah, man returneth eternally!
target_text: Ah, man returneth eternally!

source_text: The small man returneth eternally!
target_text: The small man returneth eternally!

source_text: Naked had I once seen both of them, the greatest man and the smallest man:
target_text: Naked had I once seen both of them, the greatest man and the smallest man:

source_text: all too like one another -
target_text: all too like one another -

source_text: all too human, even the greatest man!
target_text: all too human, even the greatest man!

source_text: All too small, even the greatest man!
target_text: All too small, even the greatest man!

source_text: And the eternal return also of the smallest man!
target_text: And the eternal return also of the smallest man!

source_text: that was my disgust at all existence!
target_text: that was my disgust at all existence!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and sighed and shuddered;
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and sighed and shuddered;

source_text: for he remembered his sickness.
target_text: for he remembered his sickness.

source_text: Then did his animals prevent him from speaking further.
target_text: Then did his animals prevent him from speaking further.

source_text: "Do not speak further, thou convalescent!"
target_text: "Do not speak further, thou convalescent!"

source_text: so answered his animals,
target_text: so answered his animals,

source_text: but go out where the world waiteth for thee like a garden.
target_text: but go out where the world waiteth for thee like a garden.

source_text: Go out unto the roses, the bees, and the flocks of doves!
target_text: Go out unto the roses, the bees, and the flocks of doves!

source_text: Especially, however, unto the singing-birds, to learn SINGING from them!
target_text: Especially, however, unto the singing-birds, to learn SINGING from them!

source_text: For singing is for the convalescent; the sound ones may talk.
target_text: For singing is for the convalescent; the sound ones may talk.

source_text: answered Zarathustra, and smiled at his animals.
target_text: answered Zarathustra, and smiled at his animals.

source_text: How well ye know what consolation I devised for myself in seven days!
target_text: How well ye know what consolation I devised for myself in seven days!

source_text: That I have to sing once more -
target_text: That I have to sing once more -

source_text: THAT consolation did I devise for myself, and THIS convalescence:
target_text: THAT consolation did I devise for myself, and THIS convalescence:

source_text: "Do not talk further,"
target_text: "Do not talk further,"

source_text: answered his animals once more;
target_text: answered his animals once more;

source_text: For behold, O Zarathustra!
target_text: For behold, O Zarathustra!

source_text: that thou mayest bear thy great fate, which hath not yet been any one's fate!
target_text: that thou mayest bear thy great fate, which hath not yet been any one's fate!

source_text: For thine animals know it well, O Zarathustra, who thou art and must become:
target_text: For thine animals know it well, O Zarathustra, who thou art and must become:

source_text: behold, THOU ART THE TEACHER OF THE ETERNAL RETURN, -
target_text: behold, THOU ART THE TEACHER OF THE ETERNAL RETURN, -

source_text: that is now THY fate!
target_text: that is now THY fate!

source_text: That thou must be the first to teach this teaching -
target_text: That thou must be the first to teach this teaching -

source_text: how could this great fate not be thy greatest danger and infirmity!
target_text: how could this great fate not be thy greatest danger and infirmity!

source_text: Behold, we know what thou teachest:
target_text: Behold, we know what thou teachest:

source_text: that all things eternally return, and ourselves with them, and that we have already existed times without number, and all things with us.
target_text: that all things eternally return, and ourselves with them, and that we have already existed times without number, and all things with us.

source_text: Thou teachest that there is a great year of Becoming, a prodigy of a great year;
target_text: Thou teachest that there is a great year of Becoming, a prodigy of a great year;

source_text: it must, like a sand-glass, ever turn up anew, that it may anew run down and run out:
target_text: it must, like a sand-glass, ever turn up anew, that it may anew run down and run out:

source_text: So that all those years are like one another in the greatest and also in the smallest, so that we ourselves, in every great year, are like ourselves in the greatest and also in the smallest.
target_text: So that all those years are like one another in the greatest and also in the smallest, so that we ourselves, in every great year, are like ourselves in the greatest and also in the smallest.

source_text: And if thou wouldst now die, O Zarathustra, behold, we know also how thou wouldst then speak to thyself:
target_text: And if thou wouldst now die, O Zarathustra, behold, we know also how thou wouldst then speak to thyself:

source_text: but thine animals beseech thee not to die yet!
target_text: but thine animals beseech thee not to die yet!

source_text: Thou wouldst speak, and without trembling, buoyant rather with bliss, for a great weight and worry would be taken from thee, thou patientest one!
target_text: Thou wouldst speak, and without trembling, buoyant rather with bliss, for a great weight and worry would be taken from thee, thou patientest one!

source_text: Souls are as mortal as bodies.
target_text: Souls are as mortal as bodies.

source_text: But the plexus of causes returneth in which I am intertwined, -
target_text: But the plexus of causes returneth in which I am intertwined, -

source_text: it will again create me!
target_text: it will again create me!

source_text: I myself pertain to the causes of the eternal return.
target_text: I myself pertain to the causes of the eternal return.

source_text: I come again with this sun, with this earth, with this eagle, with this serpent -
target_text: I come again with this sun, with this earth, with this eagle, with this serpent -

source_text: NOT to a new life, or a better life, or a similar life: -
target_text: NOT to a new life, or a better life, or a similar life: -

source_text: To speak again the word of the great noontide of earth and man, to announce again to man the Superman.
target_text: To speak again the word of the great noontide of earth and man, to announce again to man the Superman.

source_text: I have spoken my word.
target_text: I have spoken my word.

source_text: I break down by my word: so willeth mine eternal fate -
target_text: I break down by my word: so willeth mine eternal fate -

source_text: as announcer do I succumb!
target_text: as announcer do I succumb!

source_text: The hour hath now come for the down-goer to bless himself.
target_text: The hour hath now come for the down-goer to bless himself.

source_text: When the animals had spoken these words they were silent and waited, so that Zarathustra might say something to them:
target_text: When the animals had spoken these words they were silent and waited, so that Zarathustra might say something to them:

source_text: but Zarathustra did not hear that they were silent.
target_text: but Zarathustra did not hear that they were silent.

source_text: On the contrary, he lay quietly with closed eyes like a person sleeping, although he did not sleep;
target_text: On the contrary, he lay quietly with closed eyes like a person sleeping, although he did not sleep;

source_text: for he communed just then with his soul.
target_text: for he communed just then with his soul.

source_text: The serpent, however, and the eagle, when they found him silent in such wise, respected the great stillness around him, and prudently retired.
target_text: The serpent, however, and the eagle, when they found him silent in such wise, respected the great stillness around him, and prudently retired.

source_text: O my soul, I have taught thee to say
target_text: O my soul, I have taught thee to say

source_text: "once on a time"
target_text: "once on a time"

source_text: and to dance thy measure over every Here and There and Yonder.
target_text: and to dance thy measure over every Here and There and Yonder.

source_text: With the storm that is called
target_text: With the storm that is called

source_text: did I blow over thy surging sea;
target_text: did I blow over thy surging sea;

source_text: all clouds did I blow away from it;
target_text: all clouds did I blow away from it;

source_text: I strangled even the strangler called
target_text: I strangled even the strangler called

source_text: O my soul, I gave thee the right to say Nay like the storm, and to say Yea as the open heaven saith Yea:
target_text: O my soul, I gave thee the right to say Nay like the storm, and to say Yea as the open heaven saith Yea:

source_text: calm as the light remainest thou, and now walkest through denying storms.
target_text: calm as the light remainest thou, and now walkest through denying storms.

source_text: O my soul, I restored to thee liberty over the created and the uncreated;
target_text: O my soul, I restored to thee liberty over the created and the uncreated;

source_text: O my soul, I taught thee so to persuade that thou persuadest even the grounds themselves to thee:
target_text: O my soul, I taught thee so to persuade that thou persuadest even the grounds themselves to thee:

source_text: like the sun, which persuadeth even the sea to its height.
target_text: like the sun, which persuadeth even the sea to its height.

source_text: O my soul, I have taken from thee all obeying and knee-bending and homage-paying;
target_text: O my soul, I have taken from thee all obeying and knee-bending and homage-paying;

source_text: "Change of need"
target_text: "Change of need"

source_text: and
target_text: and

source_text: Fate.
target_text: Fate.

source_text: and
target_text: and

source_text: "the Circuit of circuits"
target_text: "the Circuit of circuits"

source_text: and
target_text: and

source_text: O my soul, every sun shed I upon thee, and every night and every silence and every longing:
target_text: O my soul, every sun shed I upon thee, and every night and every silence and every longing:

source_text: O my soul, there is nowhere a soul which could be more loving and more comprehensive and more extensive!
target_text: O my soul, there is nowhere a soul which could be more loving and more comprehensive and more extensive!

source_text: Where could future and past be closer together than with thee?
target_text: Where could future and past be closer together than with thee?

source_text: Is bestowing not a necessity?
target_text: Is bestowing not a necessity?

source_text: Is receiving not - pitying?
target_text: Is receiving not - pitying?

source_text: O my soul, I understand the smiling of thy melancholy:
target_text: O my soul, I understand the smiling of thy melancholy:

source_text: thine over-abundance itself now stretcheth out longing hands!
target_text: thine over-abundance itself now stretcheth out longing hands!

source_text: Who could see thy smiling and not melt into tears?
target_text: Who could see thy smiling and not melt into tears?

source_text: The angels themselves melt into tears through the over-graciousness of thy smiling.
target_text: The angels themselves melt into tears through the over-graciousness of thy smiling.

source_text: Thy graciousness and over-graciousness, is it which will not complain and weep:
target_text: Thy graciousness and over-graciousness, is it which will not complain and weep:

source_text: and yet, O my soul, longeth thy smiling for tears, and thy trembling mouth for sobs.
target_text: and yet, O my soul, longeth thy smiling for tears, and thy trembling mouth for sobs.

source_text: Is not all weeping complaining?
target_text: Is not all weeping complaining?

source_text: And all complaining, accusing?
target_text: And all complaining, accusing?

source_text: Thus speakest thou to thyself;
target_text: Thus speakest thou to thyself;

source_text: and therefore, O my soul, wilt thou rather smile than pour forth thy grief -
target_text: and therefore, O my soul, wilt thou rather smile than pour forth thy grief -

source_text: But wilt thou not weep, wilt thou not weep forth thy purple melancholy, then wilt thou have to SING, O my soul!
target_text: But wilt thou not weep, wilt thou not weep forth thy purple melancholy, then wilt thou have to SING, O my soul!

source_text: Behold, I smile myself, who foretell thee this: -
target_text: Behold, I smile myself, who foretell thee this: -

source_text: Thou wilt have to sing with passionate song, until all seas turn calm to hearken unto thy longing, -
target_text: Thou wilt have to sing with passionate song, until all seas turn calm to hearken unto thy longing, -

source_text: Towards the golden marvel, the spontaneous bark, and its master:
target_text: Towards the golden marvel, the spontaneous bark, and its master:

source_text: he, however, is the vintager who waiteth with the diamond vintage-knife, -
target_text: he, however, is the vintager who waiteth with the diamond vintage-knife, -

source_text: Thy great deliverer, O my soul, the nameless one -
target_text: Thy great deliverer, O my soul, the nameless one -

source_text: And verily, already hath thy breath the fragrance of future songs, -
target_text: And verily, already hath thy breath the fragrance of future songs, -

source_text: O my soul, now have I given thee all, and even my last possession, and all my hands have become empty by thee:
target_text: O my soul, now have I given thee all, and even my last possession, and all my hands have become empty by thee:

source_text: THAT I BADE THEE SING, behold, that was my last thing to give!
target_text: THAT I BADE THEE SING, behold, that was my last thing to give!

source_text: That I bade thee sing, -
target_text: That I bade thee sing, -

source_text: say now, say: WHICH of us now -
target_text: say now, say: WHICH of us now -

source_text: And let me thank thee!
target_text: And let me thank thee!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: gold saw I gleam in thy night-eyes, -
target_text: gold saw I gleam in thy night-eyes, -

source_text: my heart stood still with delight: -
target_text: my heart stood still with delight: -

source_text: A golden bark saw I gleam on darkened waters, a sinking, drinking, reblinking, golden swing-bark!
target_text: A golden bark saw I gleam on darkened waters, a sinking, drinking, reblinking, golden swing-bark!

source_text: then did my feet swing with dance-fury.
target_text: then did my feet swing with dance-fury.

source_text: thee they would know: hath not the dancer his ear -
target_text: thee they would know: hath not the dancer his ear -

source_text: Away from thee did I spring, and from thy snaky tresses:
target_text: Away from thee did I spring, and from thy snaky tresses:

source_text: then stoodst thou there half-turned, and in thine eye caresses.
target_text: then stoodst thou there half-turned, and in thine eye caresses.

source_text: With crooked glances - dost thou teach me crooked courses;
target_text: With crooked glances - dost thou teach me crooked courses;

source_text: on crooked courses learn my feet - crafty fancies!
target_text: on crooked courses learn my feet - crafty fancies!

source_text: I fear thee near, I love thee far;
target_text: I fear thee near, I love thee far;

source_text: thy flight allureth me, thy seeking secureth me: -
target_text: thy flight allureth me, thy seeking secureth me: -

source_text: I suffer, but for thee, what would I not gladly bear!
target_text: I suffer, but for thee, what would I not gladly bear!

source_text: Whither pullest thou me now, thou paragon and tomboy?
target_text: Whither pullest thou me now, thou paragon and tomboy?

source_text: I dance after thee, I follow even faint traces lonely.
target_text: I dance after thee, I follow even faint traces lonely.

source_text: Give me thy hand!
target_text: Give me thy hand!

source_text: Or thy finger only!
target_text: Or thy finger only!

source_text: Here are caves and thickets: we shall go astray!
target_text: Here are caves and thickets: we shall go astray!

source_text: Stand still!
target_text: Stand still!

source_text: Seest thou not owls and bats in fluttering fray?
target_text: Seest thou not owls and bats in fluttering fray?

source_text: Thou wouldst play me foul?
target_text: Thou wouldst play me foul?

source_text: From the dogs hast thou learned thus to bark and howl.
target_text: From the dogs hast thou learned thus to bark and howl.

source_text: Thou gnashest on me sweetly with little white teeth;
target_text: Thou gnashest on me sweetly with little white teeth;

source_text: thine evil eyes shoot out upon me, thy curly little mane from underneath!
target_text: thine evil eyes shoot out upon me, thy curly little mane from underneath!

source_text: This is a dance over stock and stone: I am the hunter, -
target_text: This is a dance over stock and stone: I am the hunter, -

source_text: Now beside me!
target_text: Now beside me!

source_text: And quickly, wickedly springing!
target_text: And quickly, wickedly springing!

source_text: Now up!
target_text: Now up!

source_text: And over!
target_text: And over!

source_text: Alas!
target_text: Alas!

source_text: Oh, see me lying, thou arrogant one, and imploring grace!
target_text: Oh, see me lying, thou arrogant one, and imploring grace!

source_text: Gladly would I walk with thee - in some lovelier place!
target_text: Gladly would I walk with thee - in some lovelier place!

source_text: Thou art now a-weary?
target_text: Thou art now a-weary?

source_text: Thou art so very weary?
target_text: Thou art so very weary?

source_text: And art thou thirsty - I should have something;
target_text: And art thou thirsty - I should have something;

source_text: but thy mouth would not like it to drink!
target_text: but thy mouth would not like it to drink!

source_text: Oh, that cursed, nimble, supple serpent and lurking-witch!
target_text: Oh, that cursed, nimble, supple serpent and lurking-witch!

source_text: Where art thou gone?
target_text: Where art thou gone?

source_text: To the rhythm of my whip shalt thou dance and cry!
target_text: To the rhythm of my whip shalt thou dance and cry!

source_text: Then did Life answer me thus, and kept thereby her fine ears closed:
target_text: Then did Life answer me thus, and kept thereby her fine ears closed:

source_text: O Zarathustra!
target_text: O Zarathustra!

source_text: Crack not so terribly with thy whip!
target_text: Crack not so terribly with thy whip!

source_text: Thou knowest surely that noise killeth thought, -
target_text: Thou knowest surely that noise killeth thought, -

source_text: and just now there came to me such delicate thoughts.
target_text: and just now there came to me such delicate thoughts.

source_text: Therefore must we be friendly to each other!
target_text: Therefore must we be friendly to each other!

source_text: And even should we not love each other from the bottom of our hearts, -
target_text: And even should we not love each other from the bottom of our hearts, -

source_text: must we then have a grudge against each other if we do not love each other perfectly?
target_text: must we then have a grudge against each other if we do not love each other perfectly?

source_text: And that I am friendly to thee, and often too friendly, that knowest thou:
target_text: And that I am friendly to thee, and often too friendly, that knowest thou:

source_text: and the reason is that I am envious of thy Wisdom.
target_text: and the reason is that I am envious of thy Wisdom.

source_text: If thy Wisdom should one day run away from thee, ah!
target_text: If thy Wisdom should one day run away from thee, ah!

source_text: then would also my love run away from thee quickly.
target_text: then would also my love run away from thee quickly.

source_text: Thereupon did Life look thoughtfully behind and around, and said softly:
target_text: Thereupon did Life look thoughtfully behind and around, and said softly:

source_text: O Zarathustra, thou art not faithful enough to me!
target_text: O Zarathustra, thou art not faithful enough to me!

source_text: Thou lovest me not nearly so much as thou sayest;
target_text: Thou lovest me not nearly so much as thou sayest;

source_text: I know thou thinkest of soon leaving me.
target_text: I know thou thinkest of soon leaving me.

source_text: There is an old heavy, heavy, booming-clock:
target_text: There is an old heavy, heavy, booming-clock:

source_text: it boometh by night up to thy cave:
target_text: it boometh by night up to thy cave:

source_text: When thou hearest this clock strike the hours at midnight, then thinkest thou between one and twelve thereon -
target_text: When thou hearest this clock strike the hours at midnight, then thinkest thou between one and twelve thereon -

source_text: of soon leaving me!
target_text: of soon leaving me!

source_text: answered I, hesitatingly,
