source_text: And verily, although a man should gain the whole world, and yet not learn one thing, ruminating, what would it profit him!
target_text: And verily, although a man should gain the whole world, and yet not learn one thing, ruminating, what would it profit him!

source_text: He would not be rid of his affliction, -
target_text: He would not be rid of his affliction, -

source_text: His great affliction:
target_text: His great affliction:

source_text: that, however, is at present called DISGUST. Who hath not at present his heart, his mouth and his eyes full of disgust?
target_text: that, however, is at present called DISGUST. Who hath not at present his heart, his mouth and his eyes full of disgust?

source_text: Thus spake the Preacher-on-the-Mount, and turned then his own look towards Zarathustra -
target_text: Thus spake the Preacher-on-the-Mount, and turned then his own look towards Zarathustra -

source_text: then, however, he put on a different expression.
target_text: then, however, he put on a different expression.

source_text: "Who is this with whom I talk?"
target_text: "Who is this with whom I talk?"

source_text: he exclaimed frightened, and sprang up from the ground.
target_text: he exclaimed frightened, and sprang up from the ground.

source_text: This is the man without disgust, this is Zarathustra himself, the surmounter of the great disgust, this is the eye, this is the mouth, this is the heart of Zarathustra himself.
target_text: This is the man without disgust, this is Zarathustra himself, the surmounter of the great disgust, this is the eye, this is the mouth, this is the heart of Zarathustra himself.

source_text: said Zarathustra, and restrained his affection,
target_text: said Zarathustra, and restrained his affection,

source_text: speak to me firstly of thyself!
target_text: speak to me firstly of thyself!

source_text: Art thou not the voluntary beggar who once cast away great riches, -
target_text: Art thou not the voluntary beggar who once cast away great riches, -

source_text: Who was ashamed of his riches and of the rich, and fled to the poorest to bestow upon them his abundance and his heart?
target_text: Who was ashamed of his riches and of the rich, and fled to the poorest to bestow upon them his abundance and his heart?

source_text: But they received him not.
target_text: But they received him not.

source_text: "But they received me not,"
target_text: "But they received me not,"

source_text: said the voluntary beggar,
target_text: said the voluntary beggar,

source_text: thou knowest it, forsooth.
target_text: thou knowest it, forsooth.

source_text: interrupted Zarathustra,
target_text: interrupted Zarathustra,

source_text: the last, subtlest master-art of kindness.
target_text: the last, subtlest master-art of kindness.

source_text: "Especially nowadays,"
target_text: "Especially nowadays,"

source_text: answered the voluntary beggar:
target_text: answered the voluntary beggar:

source_text: at present, that is to say, when everything low hath become rebellious and exclusive and haughty in its manner -
target_text: at present, that is to say, when everything low hath become rebellious and exclusive and haughty in its manner -

source_text: in the manner of the populace.
target_text: in the manner of the populace.

source_text: For the hour hath come, thou knowest it forsooth, for the great, evil, long, slow mob-and-slave-insurrection:
target_text: For the hour hath come, thou knowest it forsooth, for the great, evil, long, slow mob-and-slave-insurrection:

source_text: it extendeth and extendeth!
target_text: it extendeth and extendeth!

source_text: Now doth it provoke the lower classes, all benevolence and petty giving;
target_text: Now doth it provoke the lower classes, all benevolence and petty giving;

source_text: and the overrich may be on their guard!
target_text: and the overrich may be on their guard!

source_text: of such bottles at present one willingly breaketh the necks.
target_text: of such bottles at present one willingly breaketh the necks.

source_text: all these struck mine eye.
target_text: all these struck mine eye.

source_text: It is no longer true that the poor are blessed.
target_text: It is no longer true that the poor are blessed.

source_text: "And why is it not with the rich?"
target_text: "And why is it not with the rich?"

source_text: "Why dost thou tempt me?"
target_text: "Why dost thou tempt me?"

source_text: answered the other.
target_text: answered the other.

source_text: Thou knowest it thyself better even than I. What was it drove me to the poorest, O Zarathustra?
target_text: Thou knowest it thyself better even than I. What was it drove me to the poorest, O Zarathustra?

source_text: Was it not my disgust at the richest?
target_text: Was it not my disgust at the richest?

source_text: At the culprits of riches, with cold eyes and rank thoughts, who pick up profit out of all kinds of rubbish -
target_text: At the culprits of riches, with cold eyes and rank thoughts, who pick up profit out of all kinds of rubbish -

source_text: That distinction did I unlearn, -
target_text: That distinction did I unlearn, -

source_text: Thus spake the peaceful one, and puffed himself and perspired with his words:
target_text: Thus spake the peaceful one, and puffed himself and perspired with his words:

source_text: Zarathustra, however, kept looking into his face with a smile, all the time the man talked so severely -
target_text: Zarathustra, however, kept looking into his face with a smile, all the time the man talked so severely -

source_text: and shook silently his head.
target_text: and shook silently his head.

source_text: Thou doest violence to thyself, thou Preacher-on-the-Mount, when thou usest such severe words.
target_text: Thou doest violence to thyself, thou Preacher-on-the-Mount, when thou usest such severe words.

source_text: For such severity neither thy mouth nor thine eye have been given thee.
target_text: For such severity neither thy mouth nor thine eye have been given thee.

source_text: unto IT all such rage and hatred and foaming-over is repugnant.
target_text: unto IT all such rage and hatred and foaming-over is repugnant.

source_text: Thy stomach wanteth softer things: thou art not a butcher.
target_text: Thy stomach wanteth softer things: thou art not a butcher.

source_text: Perhaps thou grindest corn.
target_text: Perhaps thou grindest corn.

source_text: "Thou hast divined me well,"
target_text: "Thou hast divined me well,"

source_text: answered the voluntary beggar, with lightened heart.
target_text: answered the voluntary beggar, with lightened heart.

source_text: I love honey, I also grind corn;
target_text: I love honey, I also grind corn;

source_text: for I have sought out what tasteth sweetly and maketh pure breath: -
target_text: for I have sought out what tasteth sweetly and maketh pure breath: -

source_text: Also what requireth a long time, a day's-work and a mouth's-work for gentle idlers and sluggards.
target_text: Also what requireth a long time, a day's-work and a mouth's-work for gentle idlers and sluggards.

source_text: they have devised ruminating and lying in the sun.
target_text: they have devised ruminating and lying in the sun.

source_text: They also abstain from all heavy thoughts which inflate the heart.
target_text: They also abstain from all heavy thoughts which inflate the heart.

source_text: said Zarathustra,
target_text: said Zarathustra,

source_text: their like do not at present exist on earth.
target_text: their like do not at present exist on earth.

source_text: Behold, thither leadeth the way to my cave: be to-night its guest.
target_text: Behold, thither leadeth the way to my cave: be to-night its guest.

source_text: And talk to mine animals of the happiness of animals, -
target_text: And talk to mine animals of the happiness of animals, -

source_text: Until I myself come home.
target_text: Until I myself come home.

source_text: For now a cry of distress calleth me hastily away from thee.
target_text: For now a cry of distress calleth me hastily away from thee.

source_text: thou amiable one!
target_text: thou amiable one!

source_text: though it be hard for thee.
target_text: though it be hard for thee.

source_text: For they are thy warmest friends and preceptors!
target_text: For they are thy warmest friends and preceptors!

source_text: answered the voluntary beggar.
target_text: answered the voluntary beggar.

source_text: thou evil flatterer!
target_text: thou evil flatterer!

source_text: cried Zarathustra mischievously,
target_text: cried Zarathustra mischievously,

source_text: why dost thou spoil me with such praise and flattery-honey?
target_text: why dost thou spoil me with such praise and flattery-honey?

source_text: "Away, away from me!"
target_text: "Away, away from me!"

source_text: cried he once more, and heaved his stick at the fond beggar, who, however, ran nimbly away.
target_text: cried he once more, and heaved his stick at the fond beggar, who, however, ran nimbly away.

source_text: Do wait!
target_text: Do wait!

source_text: But Zarathustra did not wait;
target_text: But Zarathustra did not wait;

source_text: for a sudden irritation came over him on account of the crowd and the crowding in his mountains.
target_text: for a sudden irritation came over him on account of the crowd and the crowding in his mountains.

source_text: "Whither hath my lonesomeness gone?"
target_text: "Whither hath my lonesomeness gone?"

source_text: It is verily becoming too much for me;
target_text: It is verily becoming too much for me;

source_text: these mountains swarm;
target_text: these mountains swarm;

source_text: my kingdom is no longer of THIS world;
target_text: my kingdom is no longer of THIS world;

source_text: I require new mountains.
target_text: I require new mountains.

source_text: My shadow calleth me?
target_text: My shadow calleth me?

source_text: What matter about my shadow!
target_text: What matter about my shadow!

source_text: Let it run after me!
target_text: Let it run after me!

source_text: I - run away from it.
target_text: I - run away from it.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra to his heart and ran away.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra to his heart and ran away.

source_text: But the one behind followed after him, so that immediately there were three runners, one after the other -
target_text: But the one behind followed after him, so that immediately there were three runners, one after the other -

source_text: namely, foremost the voluntary beggar, then Zarathustra, and thirdly, and hindmost, his shadow.
target_text: namely, foremost the voluntary beggar, then Zarathustra, and thirdly, and hindmost, his shadow.

source_text: But not long had they run thus when Zarathustra became conscious of his folly, and shook off with one jerk all his irritation and detestation.
target_text: But not long had they run thus when Zarathustra became conscious of his folly, and shook off with one jerk all his irritation and detestation.

source_text: "What!"
target_text: "What!"

source_text: said he,
target_text: said he,

source_text: Verily, my folly hath grown big in the mountains!
target_text: Verily, my folly hath grown big in the mountains!

source_text: But doth Zarathustra need to be frightened by his shadow?
target_text: But doth Zarathustra need to be frightened by his shadow?

source_text: Also, methinketh that after all it hath longer legs than mine.
target_text: Also, methinketh that after all it hath longer legs than mine.

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and, laughing with eyes and entrails, he stood still and turned round quickly -
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and, laughing with eyes and entrails, he stood still and turned round quickly -

source_text: and behold, he almost thereby threw his shadow and follower to the ground, so closely had the latter followed at his heels, and so weak was he.
target_text: and behold, he almost thereby threw his shadow and follower to the ground, so closely had the latter followed at his heels, and so weak was he.

source_text: asked Zarathustra vehemently,
target_text: asked Zarathustra vehemently,

source_text: what doest thou here?
target_text: what doest thou here?

source_text: And why callest thou thyself my shadow?
target_text: And why callest thou thyself my shadow?

source_text: Thou art not pleasing unto me.
target_text: Thou art not pleasing unto me.

source_text: answered the shadow,
target_text: answered the shadow,

source_text: that it is I; and if I please thee not - well, O Zarathustra!
target_text: that it is I; and if I please thee not - well, O Zarathustra!

source_text: therein do I admire thee and thy good taste.
target_text: therein do I admire thee and thy good taste.

source_text: always on the way, but without a goal, also without a home:
target_text: always on the way, but without a goal, also without a home:

source_text: so that verily, I lack little of being the eternally Wandering Jew, except that I am not eternal and not a Jew.
target_text: so that verily, I lack little of being the eternally Wandering Jew, except that I am not eternal and not a Jew.

source_text: O earth, thou hast become too round for me!
target_text: O earth, thou hast become too round for me!

source_text: everything taketh from me, nothing giveth;
target_text: everything taketh from me, nothing giveth;

source_text: I become thin - I am almost equal to a shadow.
target_text: I become thin - I am almost equal to a shadow.

source_text: and though I hid myself from thee, I was nevertheless thy best shadow:
target_text: and though I hid myself from thee, I was nevertheless thy best shadow:

source_text: wherever thou hast sat, there sat I also.
target_text: wherever thou hast sat, there sat I also.

source_text: With thee have I wandered about in the remotest, coldest worlds, like a phantom that voluntarily haunteth winter roofs and snows.
target_text: With thee have I wandered about in the remotest, coldest worlds, like a phantom that voluntarily haunteth winter roofs and snows.

source_text: With thee have I pushed into all the forbidden, all the worst and the furthest:
target_text: With thee have I pushed into all the forbidden, all the worst and the furthest:

source_text: and if there be anything of virtue in me, it is that I have had no fear of any prohibition.
target_text: and if there be anything of virtue in me, it is that I have had no fear of any prohibition.

source_text: With thee have I broken up whatever my heart revered;
target_text: With thee have I broken up whatever my heart revered;

source_text: the most dangerous wishes did I pursue, -
target_text: the most dangerous wishes did I pursue, -

source_text: verily, beyond every crime did I once go.
target_text: verily, beyond every crime did I once go.

source_text: It is also skin.
target_text: It is also skin.

source_text: The devil himself is perhaps - skin.
target_text: The devil himself is perhaps - skin.

source_text: Ah, where have gone all my goodness and all my shame and all my belief in the good!
target_text: Ah, where have gone all my goodness and all my shame and all my belief in the good!

source_text: Too oft, verily, did I follow close to the heels of truth:
target_text: Too oft, verily, did I follow close to the heels of truth:

source_text: Sometimes I meant to lie, and behold!
target_text: Sometimes I meant to lie, and behold!

source_text: then only did I hit - the truth.
target_text: then only did I hit - the truth.

source_text: Too much hath become clear unto me:
target_text: Too much hath become clear unto me:

source_text: now it doth not concern me any more.
target_text: now it doth not concern me any more.

source_text: But alas!
target_text: But alas!

source_text: how have I still - inclination?
target_text: how have I still - inclination?

source_text: What still remaineth to me?
target_text: What still remaineth to me?

source_text: A heart weary and flippant;
target_text: A heart weary and flippant;

source_text: This seeking for MY home:
target_text: This seeking for MY home:

source_text: O Zarathustra, dost thou know that this seeking hath been MY home-sickening;
target_text: O Zarathustra, dost thou know that this seeking hath been MY home-sickening;

source_text: it eateth me up.
target_text: it eateth me up.

source_text: "Thou art my shadow!"
target_text: "Thou art my shadow!"

source_text: said he at last sadly.
target_text: said he at last sadly.

source_text: Thy danger is not small, thou free spirit and wanderer!
target_text: Thy danger is not small, thou free spirit and wanderer!

source_text: Thou hast had a bad day:
target_text: Thou hast had a bad day:

source_text: see that a still worse evening doth not overtake thee!
target_text: see that a still worse evening doth not overtake thee!

source_text: Didst thou ever see how captured criminals sleep?
target_text: Didst thou ever see how captured criminals sleep?

source_text: They sleep quietly, they enjoy their new security.
target_text: They sleep quietly, they enjoy their new security.

source_text: Beware lest in the end a narrow faith capture thee, a hard, rigorous delusion!
target_text: Beware lest in the end a narrow faith capture thee, a hard, rigorous delusion!

source_text: Thou hast lost thy goal.
target_text: Thou hast lost thy goal.

source_text: Alas, how wilt thou forego and forget that loss?
target_text: Alas, how wilt thou forego and forget that loss?

source_text: Thereby - hast thou also lost thy way!
target_text: Thereby - hast thou also lost thy way!

source_text: Thou poor rover and rambler, thou tired butterfly!
target_text: Thou poor rover and rambler, thou tired butterfly!

source_text: wilt thou have a rest and a home this evening?
target_text: wilt thou have a rest and a home this evening?

source_text: Then go up to my cave!
target_text: Then go up to my cave!

source_text: Thither leadeth the way to my cave.
target_text: Thither leadeth the way to my cave.

source_text: And now will I run quickly away from thee again.
target_text: And now will I run quickly away from thee again.

source_text: I will run alone, so that it may again become bright around me.
target_text: I will run alone, so that it may again become bright around me.

source_text: Therefore must I still be a long time merrily upon my legs.
target_text: Therefore must I still be a long time merrily upon my legs.

source_text: In the evening, however, there will be - dancing with me!
target_text: In the evening, however, there will be - dancing with me!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra.

source_text: And Zarathustra ran and ran, but he found no one else, and was alone and ever found himself again;
target_text: And Zarathustra ran and ran, but he found no one else, and was alone and ever found himself again;

source_text: he enjoyed and quaffed his solitude, and thought of good things -
target_text: he enjoyed and quaffed his solitude, and thought of good things -

source_text: Then he felt inclined to quench a little thirst, and to break off for himself a cluster of grapes.
target_text: Then he felt inclined to quench a little thirst, and to break off for himself a cluster of grapes.

source_text: namely, to lie down beside the tree at the hour of perfect noontide and sleep.
target_text: namely, to lie down beside the tree at the hour of perfect noontide and sleep.

source_text: This Zarathustra did;
target_text: This Zarathustra did;

source_text: For as the proverb of Zarathustra saith:
target_text: For as the proverb of Zarathustra saith:

source_text: One thing is more necessary than the other.
target_text: One thing is more necessary than the other.

source_text: Only that his eyes remained open: -
target_text: Only that his eyes remained open: -

source_text: for they never grew weary of viewing and admiring the tree and the love of the vine.
target_text: for they never grew weary of viewing and admiring the tree and the love of the vine.

source_text: Hath not the world now become perfect?
target_text: Hath not the world now become perfect?

source_text: What hath happened unto me?
target_text: What hath happened unto me?

source_text: It persuadeth me, I know not how, it toucheth me inwardly with a caressing hand, it constraineth me.
target_text: It persuadeth me, I know not how, it toucheth me inwardly with a caressing hand, it constraineth me.

source_text: Yea, it constraineth me, so that my soul stretcheth itself out: -
target_text: Yea, it constraineth me, so that my soul stretcheth itself out: -

source_text: How long and weary it becometh, my strange soul!
target_text: How long and weary it becometh, my strange soul!

source_text: Hath a seventh-day evening come to it precisely at noontide?
target_text: Hath a seventh-day evening come to it precisely at noontide?

source_text: Hath it already wandered too long, blissfully, among good and ripe things?
target_text: Hath it already wandered too long, blissfully, among good and ripe things?

source_text: It stretcheth itself out, long - longer!
target_text: It stretcheth itself out, long - longer!

source_text: Too many good things hath it already tasted;
target_text: Too many good things hath it already tasted;

source_text: As a ship that putteth into the calmest cove: -
target_text: As a ship that putteth into the calmest cove: -

source_text: it now draweth up to the land, weary of long voyages and uncertain seas.
target_text: it now draweth up to the land, weary of long voyages and uncertain seas.

source_text: Is not the land more faithful?
target_text: Is not the land more faithful?

source_text: then it sufficeth for a spider to spin its thread from the ship to the land.
target_text: then it sufficeth for a spider to spin its thread from the ship to the land.

source_text: No stronger ropes are required there.
target_text: No stronger ropes are required there.

source_text: O happiness!
target_text: O happiness!

source_text: Wilt thou perhaps sing, O my soul?
target_text: Wilt thou perhaps sing, O my soul?

source_text: But this is the secret, solemn hour, when no shepherd playeth his pipe.
target_text: But this is the secret, solemn hour, when no shepherd playeth his pipe.

source_text: Do not sing!
target_text: Do not sing!

source_text: The world is perfect.
target_text: The world is perfect.

source_text: Do not sing, thou prairie-bird, my soul!
target_text: Do not sing, thou prairie-bird, my soul!

source_text: Do not even whisper!
target_text: Do not even whisper!

source_text: Lo - hush!
target_text: Lo - hush!

source_text: doth it not just now drink a drop of happiness -
target_text: doth it not just now drink a drop of happiness -

source_text: But it was a blasphemy: THAT have I now learned.
target_text: But it was a blasphemy: THAT have I now learned.

source_text: Wise fools speak better.
target_text: Wise fools speak better.

source_text: The least thing precisely, the gentlest thing, the lightest thing, a lizard's rustling, a breath, a whisk, an eye-glance -
target_text: The least thing precisely, the gentlest thing, the lightest thing, a lizard's rustling, a breath, a whisk, an eye-glance -

source_text: LITTLE maketh up the BEST happiness.
target_text: LITTLE maketh up the BEST happiness.

source_text: What hath befallen me: Hark!
target_text: What hath befallen me: Hark!

source_text: Do I not fall?
target_text: Do I not fall?

source_text: Have I not fallen - hark!
target_text: Have I not fallen - hark!

source_text: into the well of eternity?
target_text: into the well of eternity?

source_text: Hush!
target_text: Hush!

source_text: It stingeth me - alas - to the heart?
target_text: It stingeth me - alas - to the heart?

source_text: What?
target_text: What?

source_text: Hath not the world just now become perfect?
target_text: Hath not the world just now become perfect?

source_text: Round and ripe?
target_text: Round and ripe?

source_text: Oh, for the golden round ring - whither doth it fly?
target_text: Oh, for the golden round ring - whither doth it fly?

source_text: Let me run after it!
target_text: Let me run after it!

source_text: and here Zarathustra stretched himself, and felt that he was asleep.
target_text: and here Zarathustra stretched himself, and felt that he was asleep.

source_text: said he to himself,
target_text: said he to himself,

source_text: thou sleeper!
target_text: thou sleeper!

source_text: Well then, up, ye old legs!
target_text: Well then, up, ye old legs!

source_text: It is time and more than time;
target_text: It is time and more than time;

source_text: many a good stretch of road is still awaiting you -
target_text: many a good stretch of road is still awaiting you -

source_text: Now have ye slept your fill;
target_text: Now have ye slept your fill;

source_text: for how long a time?
target_text: for how long a time?

source_text: (But then did he fall asleep anew, and his soul spake against him and defended itself, and lay down again) -
target_text: (But then did he fall asleep anew, and his soul spake against him and defended itself, and lay down again) -

source_text: Leave me alone!
target_text: Leave me alone!

source_text: Hath not the world just now become perfect?
target_text: Hath not the world just now become perfect?

source_text: Oh, for the golden round ball!
target_text: Oh, for the golden round ball!

source_text: "Get up,"
target_text: "Get up,"

source_text: said Zarathustra,
target_text: said Zarathustra,

source_text: What!
target_text: What!

source_text: Still stretching thyself, yawning, sighing, falling into deep wells?
target_text: Still stretching thyself, yawning, sighing, falling into deep wells?

source_text: Who art thou then, O my soul!
target_text: Who art thou then, O my soul!

source_text: and here he became frightened, for a sunbeam shot down from heaven upon his face.
target_text: and here he became frightened, for a sunbeam shot down from heaven upon his face.

source_text: said he sighing, and sat upright,
target_text: said he sighing, and sat upright,

source_text: when wilt thou drink this strange soul -
target_text: when wilt thou drink this strange soul -

source_text: When, thou well of eternity!
target_text: When, thou well of eternity!

source_text: thou joyous, awful, noontide abyss!
target_text: thou joyous, awful, noontide abyss!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and rose from his couch beside the tree, as if awakening from a strange drunkenness:
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and rose from his couch beside the tree, as if awakening from a strange drunkenness:

source_text: and behold!
target_text: and behold!

source_text: there stood the sun still exactly above his head.
target_text: there stood the sun still exactly above his head.

source_text: One might, however, rightly infer therefrom that Zarathustra had not then slept long.
target_text: One might, however, rightly infer therefrom that Zarathustra had not then slept long.

source_text: When, however, he stood over against it, not more than twenty paces therefrom, the thing happened which he now least of all expected:
target_text: When, however, he stood over against it, not more than twenty paces therefrom, the thing happened which he now least of all expected:

source_text: he heard anew the great CRY OF DISTRESS. And extraordinary!
target_text: he heard anew the great CRY OF DISTRESS. And extraordinary!

source_text: It was a long, manifold, peculiar cry, and Zarathustra plainly distinguished that it was composed of many voices:
target_text: It was a long, manifold, peculiar cry, and Zarathustra plainly distinguished that it was composed of many voices:

source_text: although heard at a distance it might sound like the cry out of a single mouth.
target_text: although heard at a distance it might sound like the cry out of a single mouth.

source_text: Thereupon Zarathustra rushed forward to his cave, and behold!
target_text: Thereupon Zarathustra rushed forward to his cave, and behold!

source_text: what a spectacle awaited him after that concert!
target_text: what a spectacle awaited him after that concert!

source_text: For there did they all sit together whom he had passed during the day:
target_text: For there did they all sit together whom he had passed during the day:

source_text: the king on the right and the king on the left, the old magician, the pope, the voluntary beggar, the shadow, the intellectually conscientious one, the sorrowful soothsayer, and the ass;
target_text: the king on the right and the king on the left, the old magician, the pope, the voluntary beggar, the shadow, the intellectually conscientious one, the sorrowful soothsayer, and the ass;

source_text: the ugliest man, however, had set a crown on his head, and had put round him two purple girdles, -
target_text: the ugliest man, however, had set a crown on his head, and had put round him two purple girdles, -

source_text: for he liked, like all ugly ones, to disguise himself and play the handsome person.
target_text: for he liked, like all ugly ones, to disguise himself and play the handsome person.

source_text: In the midst, however, of that sorrowful company stood Zarathustra's eagle, ruffled and disquieted, for it had been called upon to answer too much for which its pride had not any answer;
target_text: In the midst, however, of that sorrowful company stood Zarathustra's eagle, ruffled and disquieted, for it had been called upon to answer too much for which its pride had not any answer;

source_text: the wise serpent however hung round its neck.
target_text: the wise serpent however hung round its neck.

source_text: All this did Zarathustra behold with great astonishment;
target_text: All this did Zarathustra behold with great astonishment;

source_text: In the meantime the assembled ones had risen from their seats, and waited with reverence for Zarathustra to speak.
target_text: In the meantime the assembled ones had risen from their seats, and waited with reverence for Zarathustra to speak.

source_text: Zarathustra however spake thus:
target_text: Zarathustra however spake thus:

source_text: So it was YOUR cry of distress that I heard?
target_text: So it was YOUR cry of distress that I heard?

source_text: And now do I know also where he is to be sought, whom I have sought for in vain to-day:
target_text: And now do I know also where he is to be sought, whom I have sought for in vain to-day:

source_text: But why do I wonder!
target_text: But why do I wonder!

source_text: ye make one another's hearts fretful, ye that cry for help, when ye sit here together?
target_text: ye make one another's hearts fretful, ye that cry for help, when ye sit here together?

source_text: There is one that must first come, -
target_text: There is one that must first come, -

source_text: One who will make you laugh once more, a good jovial buffoon, a dancer, a wind, a wild romp, some old fool:
target_text: One who will make you laugh once more, a good jovial buffoon, a dancer, a wind, a wild romp, some old fool:

source_text: what think ye?
target_text: what think ye?

source_text: Ye yourselves do it, and your aspect, forgive it me!
target_text: Ye yourselves do it, and your aspect, forgive it me!

source_text: For every one becometh courageous who beholdeth a despairing one.
target_text: For every one becometh courageous who beholdeth a despairing one.

source_text: To encourage a despairing one -
target_text: To encourage a despairing one -

source_text: every one thinketh himself strong enough to do so.
target_text: every one thinketh himself strong enough to do so.

source_text: To myself have ye given this power, -
target_text: To myself have ye given this power, -

source_text: a good gift, mine honourable guests!
target_text: a good gift, mine honourable guests!

source_text: Well, do not then upbraid when I also offer you something of mine.
target_text: Well, do not then upbraid when I also offer you something of mine.

source_text: This is mine empire and my dominion:
target_text: This is mine empire and my dominion:

source_text: Mine animals shall serve you: let my cave be your resting-place!
target_text: Mine animals shall serve you: let my cave be your resting-place!

source_text: And that is the first thing which I offer you: security!
target_text: And that is the first thing which I offer you: security!

source_text: The second thing, however, is my little finger.
target_text: The second thing, however, is my little finger.

source_text: And when ye have THAT, then take the whole hand also, yea, and the heart with it!
target_text: And when ye have THAT, then take the whole hand also, yea, and the heart with it!

source_text: Welcome here, welcome to you, my guests!
target_text: Welcome here, welcome to you, my guests!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and laughed with love and mischief.
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and laughed with love and mischief.

source_text: After this greeting his guests bowed once more and were reverentially silent;
target_text: After this greeting his guests bowed once more and were reverentially silent;

source_text: the king on the right, however, answered him in their name.
target_text: the king on the right, however, answered him in their name.

source_text: Thou hast humbled thyself before us;
target_text: Thou hast humbled thyself before us;

source_text: a refreshment is it, to our eyes and hearts.
target_text: a refreshment is it, to our eyes and hearts.

source_text: For as eager beholders have we come;
target_text: For as eager beholders have we come;

source_text: we wanted to see what brighteneth dim eyes.
target_text: we wanted to see what brighteneth dim eyes.

source_text: now is it all over with our cries of distress.
target_text: now is it all over with our cries of distress.

source_text: Little is lacking for our spirits to become wanton.
target_text: Little is lacking for our spirits to become wanton.

source_text: There is nothing, O Zarathustra, that groweth more pleasingly on earth than a lofty, strong will:
target_text: There is nothing, O Zarathustra, that groweth more pleasingly on earth than a lofty, strong will:

source_text: it is the finest growth.
target_text: it is the finest growth.

source_text: An entire landscape refresheth itself at one such tree.
target_text: An entire landscape refresheth itself at one such tree.

source_text: To the pine do I compare him, O Zarathustra, which groweth up like thee -
target_text: To the pine do I compare him, O Zarathustra, which groweth up like thee -

source_text: In the end, however, grasping out for ITS dominion with strong, green branches, asking weighty questions of the wind, the storm, and whatever is at home on high places;
target_text: In the end, however, grasping out for ITS dominion with strong, green branches, asking weighty questions of the wind, the storm, and whatever is at home on high places;

source_text: At thy tree, O Zarathustra, the gloomy and ill-constituted also refresh themselves;
target_text: At thy tree, O Zarathustra, the gloomy and ill-constituted also refresh themselves;

source_text: at thy look even the wavering become steady and heal their hearts.
target_text: at thy look even the wavering become steady and heal their hearts.

source_text: And verily, towards thy mountain and thy tree do many eyes turn to-day;
target_text: And verily, towards thy mountain and thy tree do many eyes turn to-day;

source_text: a great longing hath arisen, and many have learned to ask:
target_text: a great longing hath arisen, and many have learned to ask:

source_text: all the hidden ones, the lone-dwellers and the twain-dwellers, have simultaneously said to their hearts:
target_text: all the hidden ones, the lone-dwellers and the twain-dwellers, have simultaneously said to their hearts:

source_text: It is no longer worth while to live, everything is indifferent, everything is useless:
target_text: It is no longer worth while to live, everything is indifferent, everything is useless:

source_text: Everywhere one seeth resurrected ones.
target_text: Everywhere one seeth resurrected ones.

source_text: Now do the waves rise and rise around thy mountain, O Zarathustra.
target_text: Now do the waves rise and rise around thy mountain, O Zarathustra.

source_text: And however high be thy height, many of them must rise up to thee:
target_text: And however high be thy height, many of them must rise up to thee:

source_text: thy boat shall not rest much longer on dry ground.
target_text: thy boat shall not rest much longer on dry ground.

source_text: And that we despairing ones have now come into thy cave, and already no longer despair:
target_text: And that we despairing ones have now come into thy cave, and already no longer despair:

source_text: it is but a prognostic and a presage that better ones are on the way to thee, -
target_text: it is but a prognostic and a presage that better ones are on the way to thee, -

source_text: that is to say, all the men of great longing, of great loathing, of great satiety, -
target_text: that is to say, all the men of great longing, of great loathing, of great satiety, -

source_text: All who do not want to live unless they learn again to HOPE -
target_text: All who do not want to live unless they learn again to HOPE -

source_text: unless they learn from thee, O Zarathustra, the GREAT hope!
target_text: unless they learn from thee, O Zarathustra, the GREAT hope!

source_text: Thus spake the king on the right, and seized the hand of Zarathustra in order to kiss it;
target_text: Thus spake the king on the right, and seized the hand of Zarathustra in order to kiss it;

source_text: but Zarathustra checked his veneration, and stepped back frightened, fleeing as it were, silently and suddenly into the far distance.
target_text: but Zarathustra checked his veneration, and stepped back frightened, fleeing as it were, silently and suddenly into the far distance.

source_text: My guests, ye higher men, I will speak plain language and plainly with you.
target_text: My guests, ye higher men, I will speak plain language and plainly with you.

source_text: It is not for YOU that I have waited here in these mountains.
target_text: It is not for YOU that I have waited here in these mountains.

source_text: That is not the worst taste in these days!
target_text: That is not the worst taste in these days!

source_text: continued Zarathustra;
target_text: continued Zarathustra;

source_text: but for me - ye are neither high enough, nor strong enough.
target_text: but for me - ye are neither high enough, nor strong enough.

source_text: For me, that is to say, for the inexorable which is now silent in me, but will not always be silent.
target_text: For me, that is to say, for the inexorable which is now silent in me, but will not always be silent.

source_text: And if ye appertain to me, still it is not as my right arm.
target_text: And if ye appertain to me, still it is not as my right arm.

source_text: For he who himself standeth, like you, on sickly and tender legs, wisheth above all to be TREATED INDULGENTLY, whether he be conscious of it or hide it from himself.
target_text: For he who himself standeth, like you, on sickly and tender legs, wisheth above all to be TREATED INDULGENTLY, whether he be conscious of it or hide it from himself.

source_text: My arms and my legs, however, I do not treat indulgently, I DO NOT TREAT MY WARRIORS INDULGENTLY:
target_text: My arms and my legs, however, I do not treat indulgently, I DO NOT TREAT MY WARRIORS INDULGENTLY:

source_text: With you I should spoil all my victories.
target_text: With you I should spoil all my victories.

source_text: Moreover, ye are not sufficiently beautiful and well-born for me.
target_text: Moreover, ye are not sufficiently beautiful and well-born for me.

source_text: I require pure, smooth mirrors for my doctrines;
target_text: I require pure, smooth mirrors for my doctrines;

source_text: on your surface even mine own likeness is distorted.
target_text: on your surface even mine own likeness is distorted.

source_text: On your shoulders presseth many a burden, many a recollection;
target_text: On your shoulders presseth many a burden, many a recollection;

source_text: There is concealed populace also in you.
target_text: There is concealed populace also in you.

source_text: And though ye be high and of a higher type, much in you is crooked and misshapen.
target_text: And though ye be high and of a higher type, much in you is crooked and misshapen.

source_text: There is no smith in the world that could hammer you right and straight for me.
target_text: There is no smith in the world that could hammer you right and straight for me.

source_text: Ye are only bridges: may higher ones pass over upon you!
target_text: Ye are only bridges: may higher ones pass over upon you!

source_text: so do not upbraid him who ascendeth beyond you into HIS height!
target_text: so do not upbraid him who ascendeth beyond you into HIS height!

source_text: but that time is distant.
target_text: but that time is distant.

source_text: Not for you do I wait here in these mountains;
target_text: Not for you do I wait here in these mountains;

source_text: not with you may I descend for the last time.
target_text: not with you may I descend for the last time.

source_text: Ye have come unto me only as a presage that higher ones are on the way to me, -
target_text: Ye have come unto me only as a presage that higher ones are on the way to me, -

source_text: NOT the men of great longing, of great loathing, of great satiety, and that which ye call the remnant of God;
target_text: NOT the men of great longing, of great loathing, of great satiety, and that which ye call the remnant of God;

source_text: Three times Nay!
target_text: Three times Nay!

source_text: For higher ones, stronger ones, triumphanter ones, merrier ones, for such as are built squarely in body and soul:
target_text: For higher ones, stronger ones, triumphanter ones, merrier ones, for such as are built squarely in body and soul:

source_text: LAUGHING LIONS must come!
target_text: LAUGHING LIONS must come!

source_text: have ye yet heard nothing of my children?
target_text: have ye yet heard nothing of my children?

source_text: And that they are on the way to me?
target_text: And that they are on the way to me?

source_text: why do ye not speak unto me thereof?
target_text: why do ye not speak unto me thereof?

source_text: For them am I rich, for them I became poor:
target_text: For them am I rich, for them I became poor:

source_text: what have I not surrendered, -
target_text: what have I not surrendered, -

source_text: What would I not surrender that I might have one thing:
target_text: What would I not surrender that I might have one thing:

source_text: THESE children, THIS living plantation, THESE life-trees of my will and of my highest hope!
target_text: THESE children, THIS living plantation, THESE life-trees of my will and of my highest hope!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and stopped suddenly in his discourse:
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra, and stopped suddenly in his discourse:

source_text: for his longing came over him, and he closed his eyes and his mouth, because of the agitation of his heart.
target_text: for his longing came over him, and he closed his eyes and his mouth, because of the agitation of his heart.

source_text: And all his guests also were silent, and stood still and confounded:
target_text: And all his guests also were silent, and stood still and confounded:

source_text: except only that the old soothsayer made signs with his hands and his gestures.
target_text: except only that the old soothsayer made signs with his hands and his gestures.

source_text: For at this point the soothsayer interrupted the greeting of Zarathustra and his guests:
target_text: For at this point the soothsayer interrupted the greeting of Zarathustra and his guests:

source_text: he pressed forward as one who had no time to lose, seized Zarathustra's hand and exclaimed:
target_text: he pressed forward as one who had no time to lose, seized Zarathustra's hand and exclaimed:

source_text: But Zarathustra!
target_text: But Zarathustra!

source_text: One thing is more necessary than the other, so sayest thou thyself:
target_text: One thing is more necessary than the other, so sayest thou thyself:

source_text: well, one thing is now more necessary UNTO ME than all others.
target_text: well, one thing is now more necessary UNTO ME than all others.

source_text: A word at the right time: didst thou not invite me to TABLE?
target_text: A word at the right time: didst thou not invite me to TABLE?

source_text: And here are many who have made long journeys.
target_text: And here are many who have made long journeys.

source_text: Thou dost not mean to feed us merely with discourses?
target_text: Thou dost not mean to feed us merely with discourses?

source_text: none of you, however, have thought of MY danger, namely, perishing of hunger-
target_text: none of you, however, have thought of MY danger, namely, perishing of hunger-

source_text: When Zarathustra's animals, however, heard these words, they ran away in terror.
target_text: When Zarathustra's animals, however, heard these words, they ran away in terror.

source_text: For they saw that all they had brought home during the day would not be enough to fill the one soothsayer.
target_text: For they saw that all they had brought home during the day would not be enough to fill the one soothsayer.

source_text: "Likewise perishing of thirst,"
target_text: "Likewise perishing of thirst,"

source_text: continued the soothsayer.
target_text: continued the soothsayer.

source_text: And although I hear water splashing here like words of wisdom -
target_text: And although I hear water splashing here like words of wisdom -

source_text: want WINE!
target_text: want WINE!

source_text: IT alone giveth immediate vigour and improvised health!
target_text: IT alone giveth immediate vigour and improvised health!

source_text: On this occasion, when the soothsayer was longing for wine, it happened that the king on the left, the silent one, also found expression for once.
target_text: On this occasion, when the soothsayer was longing for wine, it happened that the king on the left, the silent one, also found expression for once.

source_text: "WE took care,"
target_text: "WE took care,"

source_text: said he,
target_text: said he,

source_text: about wine, I, along with my brother the king on the right:
target_text: about wine, I, along with my brother the king on the right:

source_text: we have enough of wine, -
target_text: we have enough of wine, -

source_text: a whole ass-load of it.
target_text: a whole ass-load of it.

source_text: So there is nothing lacking but bread.
target_text: So there is nothing lacking but bread.

source_text: replied Zarathustra, laughing when he spake,
target_text: replied Zarathustra, laughing when he spake,

source_text: But man doth not live by bread alone, but also by the flesh of good lambs, of which I have two:
target_text: But man doth not live by bread alone, but also by the flesh of good lambs, of which I have two:

source_text: THESE shall we slaughter quickly, and cook spicily with sage:
target_text: THESE shall we slaughter quickly, and cook spicily with sage:

source_text: it is so that I like them.
target_text: it is so that I like them.

source_text: And there is also no lack of roots and fruits, good enough even for the fastidious and dainty, -
target_text: And there is also no lack of roots and fruits, good enough even for the fastidious and dainty, -

source_text: nor of nuts and other riddles for cracking.
target_text: nor of nuts and other riddles for cracking.

source_text: Thus will we have a good repast in a little while.
target_text: Thus will we have a good repast in a little while.

source_text: For with Zarathustra even a king may be a cook.
target_text: For with Zarathustra even a king may be a cook.

source_text: This proposal appealed to the hearts of all of them, save that the voluntary beggar objected to the flesh and wine and spices.
target_text: This proposal appealed to the hearts of all of them, save that the voluntary beggar objected to the flesh and wine and spices.

source_text: "Just hear this glutton Zarathustra!"
target_text: "Just hear this glutton Zarathustra!"

source_text: said he jokingly:
target_text: said he jokingly:

source_text: Now indeed do I understand what he once taught us:
target_text: Now indeed do I understand what he once taught us:

source_text: "Be of good cheer,"
target_text: "Be of good cheer,"

source_text: replied Zarathustra,
target_text: replied Zarathustra,

source_text: as I am.
target_text: as I am.

source_text: Abide by thy customs, thou excellent one:
target_text: Abide by thy customs, thou excellent one:

source_text: grind thy corn, drink thy water, praise thy cooking, -
target_text: grind thy corn, drink thy water, praise thy cooking, -

source_text: if only it make thee glad!
target_text: if only it make thee glad!

source_text: I am a law only for mine own; I am not a law for all.
target_text: I am a law only for mine own; I am not a law for all.

source_text: He, however, who belongeth unto me must be strong of bone and light of foot, -
target_text: He, however, who belongeth unto me must be strong of bone and light of foot, -

source_text: and if it be not given us, then do we take it: -
target_text: and if it be not given us, then do we take it: -

source_text: the best food, the purest sky, the strongest thoughts, the fairest women!
target_text: the best food, the purest sky, the strongest thoughts, the fairest women!

source_text: Thus spake Zarathustra;
target_text: Thus spake Zarathustra;

source_text: the king on the right however answered and said:
target_text: the king on the right however answered and said:

source_text: Did one ever hear such sensible things out of the mouth of a wise man?
target_text: Did one ever hear such sensible things out of the mouth of a wise man?

source_text: Thus spake the king on the right and wondered;
target_text: Thus spake the king on the right and wondered;

source_text: When I came unto men for the first time, then did I commit the anchorite folly, the great folly:
target_text: When I came unto men for the first time, then did I commit the anchorite folly, the great folly:

source_text: And when I spake unto all, I spake unto none.
target_text: And when I spake unto all, I spake unto none.

source_text: In the evening, however, rope-dancers were my companions, and corpses;
target_text: In the evening, however, rope-dancers were my companions, and corpses;

source_text: and I myself almost a corpse.
target_text: and I myself almost a corpse.

source_text: then did I learn to say:
target_text: then did I learn to say:

source_text: But if ye will speak there, very well!
target_text: But if ye will speak there, very well!

source_text: The populace, however, blinketh:
target_text: The populace, however, blinketh:

source_text: We are all equal.
target_text: We are all equal.

source_text: so blinketh the populace -
target_text: so blinketh the populace -

source_text: there are no higher men, we are all equal;
target_text: there are no higher men, we are all equal;

source_text: man is man, before God - we are all equal!
target_text: man is man, before God - we are all equal!

source_text: Before God!
target_text: Before God!

source_text: Now, however, this God hath died.
target_text: Now, however, this God hath died.

source_text: Before the populace, however, we will not be equal.
target_text: Before the populace, however, we will not be equal.

source_text: Before God!
target_text: Before God!

source_text: Now however this God hath died!
target_text: Now however this God hath died!

source_text: Now only cometh the great noontide, now only doth the higher man become -
target_text: Now only cometh the great noontide, now only doth the higher man become -

source_text: Ye are frightened: do your hearts turn giddy?
target_text: Ye are frightened: do your hearts turn giddy?

source_text: Doth the abyss here yawn for you?
target_text: Doth the abyss here yawn for you?

source_text: Now only travaileth the mountain of the human future.
target_text: Now only travaileth the mountain of the human future.

source_text: God hath died: now do WE desire - the Superman to live.
target_text: God hath died: now do WE desire - the Superman to live.

source_text: "How is man to be maintained?"
target_text: "How is man to be maintained?"

source_text: Zarathustra however asketh, as the first and only one:
target_text: Zarathustra however asketh, as the first and only one:

source_text: "How is man to be SURPASSED?"
target_text: "How is man to be SURPASSED?"

source_text: The Superman, I have at heart;
target_text: The Superman, I have at heart;

source_text: THAT is the first and only thing to me -
target_text: THAT is the first and only thing to me -

source_text: and NOT man:
target_text: and NOT man:

source_text: not the neighbour, not the poorest, not the sorriest, not the best.
target_text: not the neighbour, not the poorest, not the sorriest, not the best.

source_text: And also in you there is much that maketh me love and hope.
target_text: And also in you there is much that maketh me love and hope.

source_text: In that ye have despaired, there is much to honour.
target_text: In that ye have despaired, there is much to honour.

source_text: For ye have not learned to submit yourselves, ye have not learned petty policy.
target_text: For ye have not learned to submit yourselves, ye have not learned petty policy.

source_text: For to-day have the petty people become master:
target_text: For to-day have the petty people become master:

source_text: they all preach submission and humility and policy and diligence and consideration and the long et cetera of petty virtues.
target_text: they all preach submission and humility and policy and diligence and consideration and the long et cetera of petty virtues.

source_text: THAT wisheth now to be master of all human destiny -
target_text: THAT wisheth now to be master of all human destiny -

source_text: "How is man to maintain himself best, longest, most pleasantly?"
target_text: "How is man to maintain himself best, longest, most pleasantly?"

source_text: Thereby - are they the masters of to-day.
target_text: Thereby - are they the masters of to-day.

source_text: These masters of to-day -
target_text: These masters of to-day -

source_text: these petty people: THEY are the Superman's greatest danger!
target_text: these petty people: THEY are the Superman's greatest danger!

source_text: "happiness of the greatest number"
target_text: "happiness of the greatest number"

source_text: And rather despair than submit yourselves.
target_text: And rather despair than submit yourselves.

source_text: And verily, I love you, because ye know not to-day how to live, ye higher men!
target_text: And verily, I love you, because ye know not to-day how to live, ye higher men!

source_text: For thus do YE live - best!
target_text: For thus do YE live - best!

source_text: Have ye courage, O my brethren?
target_text: Have ye courage, O my brethren?

source_text: Are ye stout-hearted?
target_text: Are ye stout-hearted?

source_text: Cold souls, mules, the blind and the drunken, I do not call stout-hearted.
target_text: Cold souls, mules, the blind and the drunken, I do not call stout-hearted.

source_text: "Man is evil"
target_text: "Man is evil"

source_text: so said to me for consolation, all the wisest ones.
target_text: so said to me for consolation, all the wisest ones.

source_text: For the evil is man's best force.
target_text: For the evil is man's best force.

source_text: "Man must become better and eviler"
target_text: "Man must become better and eviler"

source_text: so do I teach.
target_text: so do I teach.

source_text: It may have been well for the preacher of the petty people to suffer and be burdened by men's sin.
